#### 70. Composed URL credential scrub targets use post-http.params query indexes against the autho
**Where:** `pkg/convert/bruno/native_url_sanitize.go:321` · **Area:** AREA-13 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

rewriteNativeURLTemplates (pkg/convert/bruno/native_url_sanitize.go:298-335) assigns pointer '/http/url/query/<index>/value' and scrub target {Kind:'url_query_value', Index:<index>} from the query string AFTER applyNativeHTTPParams (pkg/convert/bruno/native.go:818-876) has removed every raw-query pair whose name is managed by an http.params entry (including disabled ones) and re-appended enabled params at the end. applyNativeProjectedVariableSecrets (pkg/convert/bruno/native_sanitize.go:143-288) later applies that index via setNativeURLQueryValue (native_url_sanitize.go:442-480) to the AUTHORED /http/url string in the source file, whose '&'-split positions still include the removed pairs, so the index addresses the wrong pair whenever a managed/disabled pair precedes the credential pair in the authored query.

**Failure scenario:** Native import (output_mode=native_requests) of a request file with http.url 'https://api.test/login?debug=1&token=abc-{{tokenSuffix}}', http.params [{name: debug, type: query, value: '1', disabled: true}], and vars tokenSuffix: '12345'. Candidate-time query becomes 'token=abc-{{tokenSuffix}}' (index 0), so the composed-credential requirement records url_query_value Index 0. During Inspect's variable scrub, setNativeURLQueryValue rewrites index 0 of the AUTHORED query — 'debug=1' — so the stored sanitized source bundle becomes '?debug={{secret.LOGIN_QUERY_TOKEN_x}}&token=abc-{{tokenSuffix}}': the innocuous debug parameter now carries the token secret reference while the real credential pair keeps its authored composition. The manifest, collection view, and durable protected artifact are all rebuilt from these corrupted bytes and import succeeds silently. If the mis-indexed authored pair happens to have no '=' (e.g. '?flag&token=...'), the same flow instead hard-fails the whole import with 'URL query scrub index 0 has no value'. A secondary effect: the requirement ID/name embed the shifted index, so adding or removing an unrelated http.params entry churns the stable identity of an untouched query credential.

**Suggested fix:** Record scrub targets for raw-query credentials in the AUTHORED index space: compute the authored-parts index (or carry the authored offset through applyNativeHTTPParams by tagging surviving parts with their source index) and use that for both the '/http/url/query/N/value' identity and the url_query_value scrub Index. Alternatively, make setNativeURLQueryValue match by decoded pair name + occurrence rather than positional index.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **V082 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Chain verified. pkg/convert/bruno/native.go:1537-1547: rawTarget passes through applyNativeHTTPParams BEFORE rewriteNativeURLTemplates. native.go:805-807/819-822: paramNames includes every query-type http.params entry (Disabled checked only at 840, not when building paramNames); lines 824-838 drop authored raw-query pairs with managed keys; 839-876 re-append enabled params at the end. native_url_sanitize.go:298-334: query index is computed on this composed string and recorded as scrub target {Pointer:"/http/url", Kind:"url_query_value", Index:index}. native_sanitize.go:226-248 applies the plan to the source file's document (authored /http/url, unmarshalled from file.Data), and setNativeURLQueryValue (native_url_sanitize.go:464-475) rewrites parts[index] of the AUTHORED query positionally; inspect.go:180-207 then rebuilds bundle/manifest/collection from the corrupted bytes. Requirement flows through nativeProjectedVariableRequirements (native_sanitize.go:31-33) because scrubTargets is non-empty. A managed/disabled pair preceding the credential pair shifts the index → wrong pair scrubbed, or hard-fail at native_url_sanitize.go:469-471 when the mis-indexed pair has no '='. No test mixes http.params with raw-query credentials.

**Where:** `pkg/convert/eventhubscapture/eventhubscapture.go:128` · **Area:** AREA-14 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

#### 72. Wildcard response keys like "2XX" parse as status 2 and emit an always-failing assertion
**Where:** `pkg/convert/openapi/converter.go:2426` · **Area:** AREA-14 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

firstSuccessStatus (pkg/convert/openapi/converter.go:2420-2437) accepts any 3-byte key starting with '2' and parses it with fmt.Sscanf(key, "%d", &status). Sscanf does not require consuming the whole input, so the OpenAPI 3.x wildcard range key "2XX" (and "2xx") yields status=2 with a nil error (verified empirically: key="2XX" -> n=1, err=nil, status=2). buildAction (line 1346-1350) then emits Assertion{Type: status_code, Expected: 2}, and successResponseSchema (replay_helpers.go:30-37) looks up responses["2"], which misses.

**Suggested fix:** In firstSuccessStatus, treat keys matching 2XX/2xx as status 200 for lookup purposes but either skip the exact status_code assertion (fall back to a 200-299 status_code_range assertion) or verify the Sscanf consumed all three digits (require key to be all digits before parsing). Also make successResponseSchema consult the wildcard key.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **V088 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Sscanf does not require full-input consumption: on "2XX"/"2xx" it fills status=2 with err==nil (one verb, one operand matched), so the function returns (2, true). buildAction (converter.go:1333, 1346-1350) emits Assertion{Type:"status_code", Expected: 2}, which can never match a real 2xx response. successResponseSchema (replay_helpers.go:30-40) looks up responses["2"], missing the "2XX" entry (falls back to "default" or nil). Grep confirms no wildcard normalization anywhere in pkg/convert/openapi and firstSuccessStatus has a single caller. Every action from a wildcard-only spec fails replay. Confirmed.

#### 74. Doc-literal SOAP envelopes ignore schema targetNamespace and elementFormDefault
**Where:** `pkg/convert/wsdl/converter.go:1214` · **Area:** AREA-14 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The xsdSchema struct captures targetNamespace (line 116) and elementFormDefault (line 117) but neither field is read anywhere in the package (grep-verified). For doc-literal bindings soap:body has no namespace attribute, so tns is always the WSDL definitions targetNamespace even when the input element is declared in a schema with a different targetNamespace, and child elements are namespace-qualified even when elementFormDefault is unqualified (the XSD default). RPC and encoded operations are execution-gated (credential_projection.go:66-85) but resolved doc-literal bodies ship ungated as 'converted'.

**Suggested fix:** Track the declaring xsdSchema for each resolved element/type and emit its targetNamespace as the element's namespace (extra xmlns binding per schema namespace); honor elementFormDefault=unqualified by emitting local (unprefixed) child elements. Alternatively, when the element's declaring schema targetNamespace differs from the tns binding or elementFormDefault is unqualified, attach the existing wsdl_incomplete_xsd_type-style execution review gate instead of shipping the body as converted.

Dotted action names from importers (e.g. "checkout_flow.submit_payment.confirm_page") suffer the same fate in ByTransaction.

**Suggested fix:** Tighten the JWT heuristic: require at least one segment to contain both upper and lower case or a base64url '=' / typical JWT header prefix (eyJ), or require segments of >= 16 chars, and/or exempt strings that parse as hostnames (all-lowercase with hyphens).

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **E04 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Pattern verified at pkg/engine/redaction.go:100-103: `\b[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b` → "[REDACTED]", with no eyJ/case/entropy guard. It matches any three consecutive dot-separated 8+ char segments; for "internal-api.payments-svc.cluster1.local" the first three segments (12/12/8) match, `\b` holds at '1'|'.', yielding "[REDACTED].local". scrubSensitiveTextWithConfig applies all payloadRedactionPatterns unconditionally, even with nil config (redaction.go:906-908). ActionName/CorrelationID/DependencyTarget are scrubbed by scrubSensitiveResultMetadata (redaction.go:692,697,700), called from scrubSensitiveResultWithOptions (redaction.go:645) before Metrics.Record (pkg/engine/vuser_execute.go:49-60), and ByDependencyTarget keys on the scrubbed value (pkg/engine/metrics.go:663-676), so distinct hosts collapse into one "[REDACTED].local" bucket. Not related to the prior "response body retention" item; no regression.

</details>


#### 84. CDP sessions leak on every window switch / popup activation
**Where:** `pkg/protocol/browser/runtime_context.go:629` · **Area:** AREA-17 · **Category:** resource-leak · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

installCDPSession (runtime_context.go:614-635) calls browserContext.NewCDPSession(page) and overwrites b.pwCDP without detaching the previous session; registerPage(page, true) calls it on EVERY activation — every browser_switch_window resolution path (frame_actions.go:648,658,668,677,687) and every popup activation — even when the page is already known. Detach happens only for the final b.pwCDP at close() (lifecycle.go:10-19). When chromium + (clientMetricsEnabled or cpuThrottleRate>1 or network simulation) is active, each switch creates a fresh CDP session (with Network.enable re-sent when shaping is on) that stays attached to a live page for the whole browser session.

**Failure scenario:** A soak scenario on chromium with client metrics or network shaping enabled alternates between two windows via browser_switch_window each iteration. Each iteration attaches one more CDP session per switch to the same long-lived pages; over hours, thousands of undetached sessions accumulate in the playwright-go connection registry and in the Chromium process (each with its own event routing, and Network domain enabled), growing memory in both the generator and the browser and multiplying CDP event traffic until the pod degrades.

**Suggested fix:** In installCDPSession, detach the previous b.pwCDP (if any) before storing the new one, and skip creating a session when the activated page is already the current page with a live session.

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **W02 — CDP sessions leak on window switch / popup activation — CONFIRMED (medium)**

2. Reachable: `registerPage(page, true)` invokes it on every activation (runtime_context.go:395-397), including for already-known pages; every `trySwitchWindow` resolution path calls `registerPage(...,true)` (frame_actions.go:648,658,668,677,687), plus setup (runtime_context.go:91), open (action_dispatch.go:263), and popup activation when `autoActivatePopups` (runtime_context.go:165).
3. Gate is realistic: chromium + (clientMetrics config.go:180-185, cpu throttle, or network shaping) — runtime_context.go:618.
4. No refuting guard: sole `Detach` is close() on the final `b.pwCDP` (lifecycle.go:10-19). Browser lives for the whole VU (engine.go:356 teardown deferred after all iterations); per-iteration reset only with `new_user_per_iteration` (vuser.go:434). Pages survive switches, so orphaned sessions stay attached; with shaping, each got `Network.enable` (runtime_context.go:649), multiplying event traffic.

Prior-report check: WEEK_REVIEW_2026-07-02 W49 was a popup auto-activation *behavior* change, not this leak — not a regression.

#### 85. SSE streams silently killed by the default 60s client timeout despite a larger validated ...
**Where:** `pkg/protocol/http/http.go:536` · **Area:** AREA-17 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** previously_reported_open

So stream_timeout_ms=300000 with defaults fails every sample at 60s. Prior-report item (work-limit hard-fail deliberate-nonfix) is a different branch — no match, no regression.

#### 86. Extractor on_miss contract implemented inconsistently: ws/grpc ignore it, network always ...
**Where:** `pkg/protocol/websocket/websocket.go:272` · **Area:** AREA-17 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The DSL validates on_miss ("", ignore, empty, fail) and mode (all) for extractors of every protocol family (pkg/dsl/validate.go:757-780 — the source/type allowlist is skipped for websocket/grpc/network but on_miss/mode are checked and accepted), and protocol.Extractor documents fail semantics (pkg/protocol/protocol.go:553-554). But websocket.receive (websocket.go:271-279) and grpc.applyResponseChecks (grpc.go:391-400) silently ignore extraction errors — on_miss:"fail" never fails, on_miss:"empty" never assigns "", mode:"all" is unsupported — while network.runNetworkExtractors (network.go:625-635) fails the whole sample on ANY miss, even with the default on_miss (ignore).

**Failure scenario:** Scenario A: ws_receive with extractor {name: token, on_miss: fail}; the server message lacks the field. The action reports success, the variable stays unset, and the next ws_send transmits the literal '{{var.token}}' — a downstream 4xx blamed on the wrong step. Scenario B: a network dns/tcp action has an optional extractor with default on_miss; a miss fails the whole sample, inflating error rates for a run where the author explicitly chose lenient semantics.

**Suggested fix:** Implement on_miss handling (fail/empty/ignore) in websocket.receive, grpc.applyResponseChecks, and network.runNetworkExtractors mirroring http.go's semantics; alternatively reject unsupported on_miss/mode values at DSL validation for these protocols.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **W03 — on_miss contract inconsistent (ws/grpc ignore, network always fails) — CONFIRMED (medium)**

pkg/dsl/validate.go:768-777 validates OnMiss (""/ignore/fail/empty) and Mode (""/all) for every protocol — only the source/type allowlist is HTTP-scoped (validate.go:744-750). protocol.go:553-554 documents "fail: fail the request". HTTP implements it (http.go:659,674,697 + on_miss tests). But websocket.go:271-279 does `if err == nil { store }` — extraction errors silently dropped, so on_miss:"fail" never fails and "empty" never assigns; grpc.go:391-400 is the identical pattern. network.go:625-635 (runNetworkExtractors) returns the error string on ANY miss, failing the sample even with default on_miss=ignore. grep confirms zero OnMiss references in websocket/grpc/network packages. Failure scenarios (unset var sent literally; inflated network error rates) follow directly. Severity medium stands.

#### 87. websocket_reconnect does not cover connections discarded by a failed receive
**Where:** `pkg/protocol/websocket/websocket.go:206` · **Area:** AREA-17 · **Category:** reliability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

receive() discards the connection on ANY read error, including an ordinary read-deadline timeout (websocket.go:259-262 -> discardConn sets w.conn=nil, correct because gorilla read errors are sticky). But send() and ping() only attempt reconnection when writeMessage/WriteControl fails on an existing conn (websocket.go:214-225, 294-306); when currentConn() finds w.conn==nil they return 'websocket connection is not open' immediately (websocket.go:206-208, 330-337) even though websocket_reconnect defaults to true (websocket.go:69) and lastTarget/lastHeaders are retained precisely for reconnection (websocket.go:349-385).

**Failure scenario:** Polling script: ws_connect once, then loop {ws_send, ws_receive(timeout_ms=5000)}. The server is slow once and the receive times out; the conn is discarded. Every subsequent ws_send in every remaining iteration fails with 'websocket connection is not open' for the rest of the VUser's session, despite reconnect=true — one transient timeout converts into a permanently failing VUser without an explicit ws_connect in the loop.

**Suggested fix:** In send/ping (and optionally receive), when currentConn reports no connection and w.reconnect is true and lastTarget is set, call reconnectConn instead of failing.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **W05 — reconnect does not cover conn discarded by failed receive — CONFIRMED (medium)**

websocket.go:259-262: receive() calls discardConn on ANY ReadMessage error, including an ordinary read-deadline timeout (deadline set at 243-251), nil-ing w.conn (387-394). send() (206-209) and ping() (289-292) call currentConn(), which returns "websocket connection is not open" when w.conn==nil (330-337) — returned immediately with no reconnect attempt. The reconnect path (reconnectConn, 349-385, using retained lastTarget/lastHeaders from 196-197) is only reachable when writeMessage/WriteControl fails on an existing conn (214-225, 294-306), despite websocket_reconnect defaulting true (line 69). So one receive timeout permanently fails all later ws_send/ws_ping for the VUser unless the script re-issues ws_connect. Minor caveat: same code path also applies after deliberate ws_close (312-316), so a fix must distinguish the two. Medium stands.

</details>


#### 88. Sidecar batch validation misreports timeout exhaustion as target_validation_failed
**Where:** `pkg/javasidecar/server.go:512` · **Area:** AREA-18 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

handleValidate (server.go:490-518) validates every target sequentially — each an independent JVM launch via runHarness — under one shared bounded context (default 30s via boundedTimeout at server.go:478). When that budget expires mid-batch, the remaining targets' runHarness outcomes fail with a context error but are recorded indistinguishably as `target_validation_failed` (server.go:513-517). The caller preflightSidecar (pkg/protocol/java_vuser/java_vuser.go:1605-1609) passes TimeoutMS = cfg.ActionTimeout (default 30s, java_vuser.go:38) for the WHOLE batch and fails the entire preflight with the misleading per-target code (java_vuser.go:1616-1625).

**Failure scenario:** A multi-class LR Java import (importer splits into 10+ Actions classes) runs runtime preflight against the sidecar. JVM spin-up is ~2-4s per target on a cold node, so targets after ~8-12 exceed the 30s batch budget. Preflight reports 'java_vuser sidecar validation failed (target_validation_failed at index 9)' — the operator debugs a perfectly valid class instead of raising the timeout, and the import is blocked on a phantom validation failure.

**Suggested fix:** In handleValidate, check ctx.Err() after each target and emit a distinct issue code (e.g. validation_timeout with the index reached) instead of target_validation_failed; optionally scale the effective budget by len(targets) up to MaximumExecutionTimeout, and have preflightSidecar surface the distinct code.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **J02 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

handleValidate (pkg/javasidecar/server.go:468-521) builds one ctx from boundedTimeout(request.TimeoutMS, DefaultExecutionTimeout=30s; types.go:26) at server.go:490 and runs prepareRuntime, verifyHarness, then every target's runHarness (line 512, one JVM launch each) under that shared budget. runProcess sets outcome.success=false with errorCode from contextErrorCode(ctx) = "execution_timeout" on deadline expiry (server.go:1719-1722, 2025-2026), but handleValidate discards errorCode and records every failure as `target_validation_failed` (server.go:513-517). Caller preflightSidecar passes TimeoutMS = cfg.ActionTimeout (java_vuser.go:1608; default 30s at java_vuser.go:38/466) for the whole batch and surfaces the first issue verbatim (java_vuser.go:1617-1622). Timeout exhaustion mid-batch is thus reported as a per-target validation failure. Confirmed.

</details>


#### 89. Real Kafka adapter silently ignores explicit partition targeting and partition strategy
**Where:** `pkg/protocol/kafka/realclient_franz.go:387` · **Area:** AREA-18 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

kafka.go buildRecord (kafka.go:886) sets rec.Partition via resolvePartition (kafka.go:904-926: explicit params.partition, else key-hash/round-robin per cfg.PartitionStrategy) and the mock honors it, but franzClient.Produce (realclient_franz.go:383-392) only copies rec.Partition into the kgo.Record when >0 and newClient (realclient_franz.go:163-259) never sets kgo.RecordPartitioner; franz-go v1.21.5 defaults to UniformBytesPartitioner (config.go:666 in the dependency), which ignores Record.Partition — only ManualPartitioner (partitioner.go:121) reads it. Additionally the `> 0` guard makes partition 0 unaddressable even if a manual partitioner were configured.

**Failure scenario:** A script imported from LoadRunner/JMeter that pins records to a specific partition (params.partition = 2) — or relies on kafka_partition_strategy round_robin/key-hash — validates green against the mock broker (which routes via resolvePartition), then runs against a real cluster where every record is routed by franz's uniform-bytes partitioner instead. Per-partition ordering assumptions are silently violated; a partition_equals assertion fails intermittently depending on where the sticky partitioner lands, and without an assertion the misrouting is completely silent (extractions report the actual partition, masking the ignored intent).

**Suggested fix:** In newClient, install a wrapper partitioner: if the record carries a non-negative explicit partition (track intent with a sentinel, e.g. Partition >= 0 plus an explicit-flag header or a dedicated field on kafkaRecord), delegate to kgo.ManualPartitioner semantics, else fall back to the default. Alternatively reject params.partition on the real adapter loudly (matching the existing per-action consumer_group fail-loud precedent at realclient_franz.go:412-414).

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **J01 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

kafka.go:886 buildRecord sets Partition via resolvePartition (kafka.go:904-926: explicit `partition` param wins, else round-robin/key-hash per cfg.PartitionStrategy). The mock honors it (broker.go:239 returns recordMeta with rec.Partition). The real adapter does not: franzClient.Produce (realclient_franz.go:387-389) copies rec.Partition into kgo.Record only when >0 (partition 0 unaddressable), and newClient (realclient_franz.go:163-259) never sets kgo.RecordPartitioner — grep over pkg/protocol/kafka shows zero RecordPartitioner/ManualPartitioner uses. go.mod pins franz-go v1.21.5, whose default UniformBytesPartitioner ignores Record.Partition; only kgo.ManualPartitioner reads it. So explicit targeting and strategy are silently dropped on real clusters while validating green on the mock. Causal chain holds.

</details>

#### 91. Coordinated start barrier trusts generator wall clocks: skew either skews the fleet ramp ...
**Where:** `pkg/distributed/generatorrpc/execution_control.go:365` · **Area:** AREA-19 · **Category:** reliability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

CommitWork evaluates the controller-chosen start_at_unix_nano against the generator's local clock: a barrier not after local now is rejected outright ('coordinated start barrier has already elapsed', execution_control.go:366-370), one beyond the stage TTL is rejected as too far in the future (371-373), and waitForCoordinatedExecutionStart (485-498) sleeps time.Until(startAt) on the local clock. With -1.5s drift the generator instead starts 1.5s late, so the distributed ramp the barrier exists to align is skewed by exactly the node drift.

**Suggested fix:** Estimate per-generator clock offset from the heartbeat exchange (or echo the controller's now alongside start_at) and apply the offset when translating the barrier to a local deadline; include local-vs-barrier delta in the rejection message.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **S05 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Controller picks the barrier from its own clock: startAt = time.Now().Add(distributedCommitStartLead(...)) (pkg/api/distributed_stream.go:195); lead is ackWindow (≤2s) + 0.5-1s margin (pkg/api/distributed_execution_backend.go:1155-1179), so ~2.5-3s. Generator evaluates it against generator-local time.Now() (execution_control.go:430 passes time.Now(); 366-373 rejects "already elapsed" if !startAt.After(now) or "too far in the future" beyond stage TTL), and waitForCoordinatedExecutionStart sleeps local time.Until(startAt) (485-498). Grep confirms no clock-offset/skew estimation anywhere in generatorrpc, though heartbeat pong clamps TimestampUnixMs to max(local, ping) (service.go:1215), acknowledging skew. So drift > ~2.5s lead hard-rejects the fleet commit; smaller drift staggers the ramp by the node offset. Causal chain holds.

#### 97. HAR scrub destroys base64-encoded response content while leaving encoding flag intact
**Where:** `pkg/scrub/scrub.go:1484` · **Area:** AREA-22 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

scrubHAREntry (scrub.go:1484-1488) runs cp.value over response content.text without checking content.encoding == "base64". A base64 body is one long [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{24,} run with letters, digits, and >=4.0 shannon entropy, so highEntropyToken + looksSensitiveToken (scrub.go:75, 1048-1054, 1544-1562) replace it — sometimes partially, leaving invalid base64 — with [REDACTED], while the sibling "encoding":"base64" field is preserved. Every binary response (images, fonts, protobuf) in every scrubbed HAR is destroyed and no longer decodes, contradicting redactBareTokens' own stated contract (scrub.go:1038-1040: 'keeping scrubbed artifacts usable as evidence and re-import inputs').

**Failure scenario:** A browser-recorder session records a page with images; scrub-on-write replaces each base64 content.text with [REDACTED] (or a partial '[REDACTED]<residue>') while encoding stays 'base64'. Any consumer that decodes content per the HAR spec (viewer preview, replay-fidelity comparison, re-import) gets a decode error or garbage for every binary entry of every recording — silent, systematic loss of all binary evidence rather than targeted secret removal.

**Suggested fix:** In scrubHAREntry, when content.encoding is 'base64' either skip the value pass, or decode → scrub → re-encode, or replace the whole content object with a deliberate redaction marker (empty text plus a _scrubbed annotation) so the encoding contract is not silently violated. At minimum drop the encoding field when text is redacted.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **T03 — HAR scrub destroys base64 response content — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Chain verified at HEAD. `scrubHAREntry` (pkg/scrub/scrub.go:1484-1488) runs `cp.value` on `response.content.text` unconditionally; grep shows no read of `content["encoding"]` anywhere in the package (only the `encoding/json` import matches). `cp.value` calls `redactBareTokens` (scrub.go:228 → 1041-1054), which applies `highEntropyToken` (`\b[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{24,}\b`, line 75) gated by `looksSensitiveToken` (1544-1562: len>=24, letter+digit, entropy>=4.0). Empirical check (scratch Python, same formulas): even the 96-char 1x1-PNG base64 has entropy 4.39 with letters+digits → redacted, and the `\b` regex matches span [0,94), producing `[REDACTED]==` — invalid base64 exactly as claimed; 4KB binary bodies hit entropy 6.0. Production reachability: `scrub.HAR` with default Policy is called on the persistence/import paths at pkg/protocol/browser/har_capture.go:301 (Playwright HAR scrub-on-write; Playwright emits base64 binary content), pkg/convert/har/converter.go:73, pkg/api/handlers_recorder.go:441, pkg/api/handlers_browser_recorder.go:1737 (DevTools HAR uploads use `encoding:"base64"`). No test pins base64 content preservation. Prior-report check: WEEK_REVIEW_2026-07-02's entropy/JWT fixes added the hostname/low-entropy gates — distinct issue, not a regression; base64 binary legitimately passes those gates. Data-integrity defect, not security → medium stands.

</details>


#### 98. apexctl run --api polls forever with no overall deadline
**Where:** `cmd/apexctl/api_client.go:272` · **Area:** AREA-23 · **Category:** reliability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

pollTest (cmd/apexctl/api_client.go:269-332) loops on a fixed 2s time.Sleep with no context, no overall timeout, and no flag to bound it; maxPollErrors=5 only bounds consecutive transport errors, so a controller that keeps answering 200 with a non-terminal status keeps the CLI alive indefinitely. `apexctl run` exposes no --timeout flag (parseRunArgs, main.go:253-360), unlike `apexctl wait` (30m default) and `apexctl ci run` (hard timeout + abort).

**Failure scenario:** A distributed run wedges non-terminal on the controller (e.g. generator fleet lost mid-run and the run stays RUNNING); a pipeline invoking `apexctl run --api ... --junit out.xml` hangs until the CI job's own wall-clock limit kills it, producing no JUnit evidence at all instead of a failed gate.

**Suggested fix:** Add a --timeout flag (default e.g. duration+30m) to run, thread a context into pollTest, and on expiry write the JUnit/JSON evidence with an execution error before exiting non-zero.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **C04 — `apexctl run --api` polls forever — CONFIRMED (medium)**

cmd/apexctl/api_client.go:269-332: pollTest is an unbounded `for {}` with `time.Sleep(2s)`, no context/deadline; maxPollErrors=5 (line 267) only bounds *consecutive transport errors* and resets to 0 on any 200 (line ~292). Loop exits only on status COMPLETE/FAILED/ABORTED, so a run wedged in RUNNING keeps the CLI alive indefinitely. Called from the run --api path at api_client.go:172. parseRunArgs (main.go:253-360 case list: --script/--api/--api-key/--bearer-token/--base-url/--env/--format/--junit/--vusers/--duration/--ramp-up/SLA flags) has no --timeout. Contrast: `wait` defaults 30m (commands.go:29,63-67) and `ci run` has a hard timeout + ctx (ci.go:215,433). Causal chain holds.

</details>


#### 99. apexctl wait fails the CI gate on a single transient status-poll error
**Where:** `cmd/apexctl/api_client.go:364` · **Area:** AREA-23 · **Category:** reliability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

cmd/apexctl/api_client.go:357-379: inside WaitForTest's loop, `test, err := c.GetTestStatus(testID); if err != nil { return nil, err }` — any single error (transient 502/timeout surfaces as error from GetTestStatus, api_client.go:337-354 returns error on any non-200) aborts immediately, with no retry counter. #### 102. Semantic highlighting re-parses and rebuilds the whole decoration set on every document c...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/apexDslSemanticHighlighting.ts:413` · **Area:** AREA-24 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The StateField update handler calls buildApexDslSemanticDecorations(tr.state) whenever tr.docChanged, with no incrementality and no debounce. That helper runs jsonLanguage.parser.parse over the entire document, mirrors the whole Lezer tree into plain JS objects (parseJsonTree/readNode at 82-109 allocates a JsonNodeRecord for every node including punctuation tokens), walks every String node again for `{{param.…}}` references (collectParameterReferences at 172-188), then sorts and dedupes the resulting ranges and materializes one line decoration per line of every block. Code at HEAD matches the claim. `apexDslSemanticHighlightField.update` (apexDslSemanticHighlighting.ts:413-418) calls

restriction. `buildApexDslSemanticDecorations` (:379-382) only short-circuits above `APEX_DSL_SEMANTIC_MAX_DOC_CHARS =
200_000` (:377), then re-runs `collectApexDslSemanticRanges` -> `parseJsonTree` (:82-109, full Lezer parse plus a
`JsonNodeRecord` object per node, punctuation included), `collectParameterReferences` (:172-188, revisits every String
node), `uniqueSortedRanges` (:300-311), and materializes one line decoration per line of every block (:384-403) — the
`actions` sectionBlock alone spans nearly the whole document.

Wiring is real: `ScriptCodePane` unconditionally includes `apexDslSemanticHighlighting()` in its `useMemo` extension set
(ScriptJsonAuthoringView.tsx:126-136) and becomes editable via the "Edit JSON" toggle (:249-258, `editable` at :282).
Nothing in `dslEditorAssist.ts` (only imports the constant at :20/:323) or the tests
(apexDslSemanticHighlighting.test.ts:109-112 only pins the hard cap) debounces or memoizes the rebuild. No refuting
guard found.

Reachability of the primary scenario: to type at all the user must be on the full-document pane (`allowDirectEdit`
false on the selected-action pane, ScriptJsonAuthoringView.tsx:391), and once `jsonDirty` is set
`selectedJsonUnavailable` forces the full pane (ScriptEditor.tsx:4528-4534). So a ~150k-char import under the cap pays
the whole pass on each keystroke.

Magnitude tempering: the pass is tens of milliseconds at 150k chars (Lezer JSON parse + ~10^4-10^5 node objects +
~10^4 decoration ranges), i.e. well past the 16ms frame budget and visibly janky, but "a few frames per second" is
stronger than the evidence supports; per-keystroke React re-render of ScriptEditor also contributes.

If the operator then picks any value from that dropdown (a natural reaction to a blank required-looking field), onUpdate rewrites the marker's type to e.g. 'GET', turning a transaction boundary into an HTTP request with an empty target — the transaction pair is now unbalanced and the run reports a bogus GET action. The same blank dropdown appears for every imported `source_review` / `source_parameter` action.

**Suggested fix:** Drive the option list from dslActionTypesForProtocol(protocol) when the catalog has loaded (falling back to the hardcoded arrays otherwise), and always include the action's current type as an option — e.g. prepend `{value: action.type, label: `${action.type} (current)`}` when it is not in the list — so the control can never silently disagree with the model. For marker/source_* types, prefer rendering a read-only badge instead of an editable select.

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D007 slot A — action-type select has no option for source_* types**

Chain verified statically at HEAD (snapshot), every hop:

1. Control exists: `ScriptEditorActionEditor.tsx:696-697` renders `<select value={action.type} onChange={e => onUpdate(index,'type',e.target.value)}>` with `{actionTypes.map(type => <option key={type}>{type}</option>)}` — options carry no `value`, so option value == text. `actionTypes` is chosen at 664-677 from the hardcoded arrays at 205-233 (CONTROL/BROWSER/JMS/WEBSOCKET/GRPC/DATABASE/NETWORK/HTTP). None contains any `source_*` type (grep confirms).
2. Such actions exist: `scriptEditorWorkbench.ts:435-436` `transactionMarker()` returns `{type:'source_transaction', params:{function:'lr_start_transaction'|'lr_end_transaction'}}`; `wrapActionsInTransactionMarkers` (447-462) splices the pair into the list. #### 104. Merge Source Files pads short sources with blank rows, blanks unmapped parameters, and or...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/scriptEditorParameterDataModel.ts:266` · **Area:** AREA-24 · **Category:** data-integrity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

buildMergedParameterSourceScript builds one row-aligned CSV whose row count is the MAX row count across all merged sources and fills every gap with '' (268-273), so parameters backed by a shorter file silently gain empty values for the tail rows. A candidate whose column could not be resolved (columnIndex === null, which getParameterDataColumnIndexes returns whenever parameter.column matches no header and the source has more than one column, 98-108) is still merged and contributes a column of '' for every row — that parameter now yields empty values for every VUser. Finally, the original sources are deleted from script.data_sources (288-290) and columns are renamed to the parameter name (221-224), but nothing rewrites `{{data.<old_source>.<old_column>}}` tokens embedded in action targets/bodies/headers, and the engine resolves those tokens by the flattened "source.column" key (pkg/engine/vuser_resolve.go:685-689). The caller reports success with no warning about any of this (ScriptEditor.tsx:4013-4027).

**Failure scenario:** A script has two CSV parameter sources: users.csv with 5,000 rows bound to {{param.username}}, and regions.csv with 4 rows bound to {{param.region}}; some action targets also use the raw form {{data.regions.code}}. Click 'Merge Source Files'. The merged file gets 5,000 rows: rows 5-5000 of the region column are empty, so 99.9% of VUsers now send an empty region; regions.csv is deleted from data_sources, so every {{data.regions.code}} token becomes unresolvable at run time. Nothing in the UI warns about either consequence — the success toast only says the merge happened and to save the script.

**Suggested fix:** Before merging, refuse (or explicitly confirm) when candidates disagree on row count or when any candidate has columnIndex === null, and scan the script for {{data.<mergedSourceName>.…}} tokens and rewrite them to the merged source/column (or block the merge and list the offending actions). At minimum, surface the row-count mismatch and orphaned-token count in the confirmation/summary instead of a bare success message.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D006 (slot A) — Merge Source Files: padding, blank columns, orphaned {{data.*}}**

Traced the full chain in the snapshot (HEAD dc05008ab).

**Reachable, unguarded.** `ParameterSidebar` renders a plain `Merge Source Files` button whose only gate is `mergeSummary.canMerge` (ScriptEditorParameterFeatures.tsx:866-876). Its handler `mergeParameterSourceFiles` (ScriptEditor.tsx:4013-4027) calls `buildMergedParameterSourceScript`, `setScript`, and reports `Merged N parameter source files into merged_parameters…` — no confirm dialog, no row-count or data-loss warning.

**Padding is real.** `rowCount` = max over candidates and missing cells become `''` (scriptEditorParameterDataModel.ts:267-273); `stringifyInlineData` emits the empty field (scriptEditorUtils.ts:311-318). Engine side, `columnValues` preserves empty cells verbatim (pkg/engine/data.go:243-255) and `generateSelectedValue` never skips blanks (pkg/engine/parameters.go:365-409). Pre-merge a 4-row source wrapped (`effectiveOnExhaustion` default "wrap", parameters.go:153-158); post-merge the same parameter walks 5,000 values of which 4,996 are `""`. Note the existing unit test pins this padding (`'username,password\nalice,secret\nbob,'`, scriptEditorParameterDataModel.test.ts:105) — it is intended row-alignment, but the operator is never told.

**Orphaning is real and worse than claimed.** `nextSources` drops every merged source (line 288-290) and the merged file keeps only one column per candidate parameter, so non-parameter columns are discarded outright. Nothing rewrites `{{data.<source>.<column>}}`, which the engine resolves via `vu.Variables["source.column"]` (pkg/engine/vuser_resolve.go:685-689); unresolved `data.` tokens are written into the request verbatim and are not even recorded in an unresolved-ref list (vuser_resolve.go:543-556). Reachability is first-party: the shipped `shared-user-data-pool` component defines a `users` CSV source **plus** `type:"file"` parameters (pkg/api/authoring_components.go:287-297) while sibling components embed `{{data.users.entity_id|password|amount}}` (authoring_components.go:67-68,111-112,141,158).

**Partial mitigations found (severity, not verdict).** Undo history is pushed (ScriptEditor.tsx:4020) and the change needs an explicit Save; afterwards `collectAuthoringIssues` raises a *warning* "Referenced data source … is not defined" for the orphaned tokens (scriptAuthoringAssist.ts:455-464). Nothing detects the padded blanks.

**One sub-claim overstated.** `columnIndex === null` only occurs when `parameter.column` matches no header (or is empty) on a multi-column source — in that state the engine already fails the lookup (`param.Column == ""` guard / `GetColumnValues` miss, parameters.go:487-493), so the merge does not break a working parameter; it converts a hard-unresolved parameter into a silently empty one. Severity stays medium.

</details>


#### 105. Parameter Data grid renders every row unvirtualized and re-serializes the whole data file...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ScriptEditorParameterDataSources.tsx:690` · **Area:** AREA-24 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The grid maps over every filtered row and renders one <input> per visible column with no windowing, in a component tree that the rest of the editor deliberately virtualizes above 100 rows (ScriptEditor.tsx:328 LIST_VIRTUALIZE_THRESHOLD / 943-951 useVirtualizer for the action list). Worse, each character typed into a cell runs updateDataCell (ScriptEditor.tsx:4029-4038), which parseInlineData()s the entire CSV, copies every row, stringifyInlineData()s the entire CSV back, and hands it to mutateDataSource (3926-3945) — which performs three JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) deep clones of the data source (including the whole inline_data string) and pushes one of them onto a 100-entry undo stack. The resulting setScript then triggers the whole-script serialization pipeline described in the previous finding, because inline_data lives inside the script document.

**Failure scenario:** Open a LoadRunner-imported script whose parameter .dat file has 20,000 rows, open the Parameter Data tab and expand that source. The grid mounts 20,000 rows x N columns of controlled <input> elements, so the tab takes many seconds to appear and the browser tab balloons in memory. Then type a single character into any cell: the handler re-parses and re-serializes the full 20,000-row file and deep-clones it three times before React re-renders all 20,000 rows, so each keypress costs hundreds of milliseconds and holding a key makes the tab unresponsive.

**Suggested fix:** Virtualize the grid body with @tanstack/react-virtual above the same LIST_VIRTUALIZE_THRESHOLD used for the action list, and stop round-tripping the whole file per keystroke: keep the parsed {columns, rows} as the edit model while a source editor is open and re-serialize on blur/commit, and drop the redundant cloneDataSource calls in mutateDataSource (one structural copy is enough; the history entry can share the previous immutable value).

**Reachability:** the live path is `ScriptEditorParameterFeatures.tsx:398-426` (`ParameterDataDetail` → `ParameterDataEditor`), rendered by `ParameterDataDialog` (145/244), mounted from `ScriptEditor.tsx:6418-6453` via the "Parameter Data" center tab. `parsed` is recomputed unmemoized at 359. The data tabpanel (473-475) is only `hidden`, so the full grid mounts as soon as a mapped file/list parameter is selected — even on the Settings tab. `focusedColumnIndexes` is not passed here, so all columns render as inputs.

**Per-keystroke cost:** `ScriptEditor.tsx:4029-4038` `updateDataCell` re-parses the whole file, copies every row, re-serializes (`stringifyInlineData`), then `mutateDataSource` (3926-3945) does three `cloneDataSource` = `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` (`scriptEditorUtils.ts:404-406`) at 3934/3938/3942 and pushes a full copy onto a 100-deep undo stack (memory ≈ 100 × file size). `setScript` is a plain reducer dispatch (6506-6520; `scriptEditorState.ts:429`) — no debounce. Amplifier confirmed: `ScriptEditor.tsx:1258-1261` `formatScriptJson(currentDraftScript)` re-stringifies the whole script document each change.

**Refutation attempts that failed:** no memoization/`React.memo`, no debounce, no row cap or pagination anywhere on the path, stable `key` (no remount), and the editor's own `LIST_VIRTUALIZE_THRESHOLD = 100` (ScriptEditor.tsx:328, virtualizer 942-951) is applied only to the action list, never to this grid. #### 106. Every keystroke in any structured field re-serializes and re-parses the entire script thr...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/useScriptJsonAuthoringController.ts:58` · **Area:** AREA-24 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

A single setScript (typing one character into an action Name/Target field) changes the `script` identity and cascades into at least three full JSON.stringify passes and one full JSON.parse of the whole document, plus a full pointer-document rebuild: formattedScriptJson = formatScriptJson(script) (useScriptJsonAuthoringController.ts:58); deriveScriptJsonDraftState -> parseScriptJsonDraft(jsonText) full JSON.parse (59-62); the sync effect's synchronizeStructuredScriptJson -> formatScriptJson(structuredScript) (64-67 and scriptEditorJsonModel.ts:152-160); validationDocumentKey = formatScriptJson(currentDraftScript) (ScriptEditor.tsx:1258-1261); scriptDslDocument = buildDslDocument({ script }), which re-serializes the document and allocates a Map entry per JSON value (ScriptEditor.tsx:3260, dslJsonPointers.ts:34-91). On top of that, several O(script) derivations are recomputed on EVERY render with no memo at all: buildBrowserHTTPConversionReview (ScriptEditor.tsx:952), buildLocalReplayPreflight (3129-3130, which walks all phase actions collecting template refs), and buildReplayVariableDiffs (3121-3123). The neighbouring memoized derivations (authoringIssues at 1321, currentEditableActionsKey at 1199 with an explicit 'O(script size); memoize it' comment) show the intended pattern was not applied uniformly.

**Failure scenario:** Open a multi-thousand-action imported script (a LoadRunner archive whose pretty-printed JSON is several MB), select an action, and type a new name into the Action Editor's Name field. Every keystroke runs three full JSON.stringify passes plus a full JSON.parse plus a buildDslDocument walk over the entire document, all synchronously on the main thread, so characters land hundreds of milliseconds behind the keyboard and the field feels frozen. The same cost is paid per render while a debug replay is streaming, because each replay WebSocket event re-renders ScriptEditor and re-runs buildLocalReplayPreflight and buildBrowserHTTPConversionReview over the whole script.

**Suggested fix:** 1) Collapse the duplicate serializations: compute formatScriptJson(script) once per script identity and reuse it for formattedScriptJson, the sync effect and validationDocumentKey. 2) Avoid the full re-parse in deriveScriptJsonDraftState when !jsonDirty — the structured `script` already IS the current script, so short-circuit to it. 3) Memoize httpConversionReview, unreconciledReplayPreflight and replayVariableDiffs on their real inputs. 4) Consider deferring buildDslDocument until a pointer lookup is actually needed (it is only consumed by lineRangeForTargetPath at 3275).

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D003 — verifier A evidence**

Traced the full chain at HEAD; found no refuting guard.

Trigger: `ScriptEditorActionEditor.tsx:694` (`ActionCoreFields`) renders `<input value={action.name} onChange={e => onUpdate(index,'name',e.target.value)} />` — fully controlled, no debounce. `onUpdate` is wired at `ScriptEditor.tsx:4814` to `updatePhaseAction` → `updatePhaseActionObject` (2305) → `updatePhaseActionList` (2170) → `setScript`. `setScript` (`scriptEditorState.ts:431`) only replaces `documentHistory.script`; it never updates `jsonText`.

#### 107. Guided Correlation Repair always attaches the extractor to action #1 and suppresses the s...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/AuthoringSessionsPanel.tsx:235` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

buildCorrelationPayload (AuthoringSessionsPanel.tsx:235-246) hardcodes `found_action_index: 1` and `used_action_indexes: (session.draft?.actions || []).slice(1).map((_, index) => index + 2)`. The panel exposes no control for either. On the server, resolveCorrelationFoundActionIndex (pkg/api/handlers_authoring_correlations.go:341-364) checks `req.FoundActionIndex != nil` FIRST and returns immediately; only when it is nil does it fall through to matching `found_action` by name and then to scanning for the action that actually contains the sample value (`actionContainsSample`). Because the dashboard always sends an explicit index, that auto-detection is dead code from this surface, and the extractor is appended to `script.Actions[0].Extractors` (handlers_authoring_correlations.go:324) regardless of which response really produces the value. Apply Repair (AuthoringSessionsPanel.tsx:141) persists the result into the authoring-session draft.

**Failure scenario:** An imported session's draft has actions [1] POST /api/login, [2] GET /api/dashboard (returns the CSRF token in its JSON body), [3] POST /api/order (needs the token). In the review queue the operator fills Variable=csrf_token, Source=body, Expression=$.token, Sample value=abc123 and clicks Apply Repair. The server attaches the jsonpath extractor to action 1 (POST /api/login), whose response has no $.token, and rewrites actions 2 and 3 to use {{var.csrf_token}}. At replay the extractor yields nothing, {{var.csrf_token}} never resolves, and action 3 fails - so the 'guided repair' turned a one-broken-action script into a two-broken-action script, and the operator's only signal is a changes list that reads 'actions[1].extractors[1]' rather than 'actions[2]'.

**Suggested fix:** Stop sending found_action_index unless the operator picked one. Either omit the field entirely (letting the server's actionContainsSample scan choose) or add a 'Found in action' <select> populated from session.draft.actions and default it to the sample-value match. Likewise omit used_action_indexes so the server's foundIndex+1..N default applies consistently.

#### 108. Deleting an inherited default HTTP header in the per-group runtime editor silently reverts
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/RuntimeSettingsGroupEditor.tsx:152` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** state-management · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

HttpRequestDefaultsEditor.commitEntries (HttpRequestDefaultsEditor.tsx:395-400) emits `{ default_header_list: <list or undefined>, default_headers: undefined }` - it uses `undefined` on default_headers to mean "the legacy compatibility map is now superseded, drop it". In the per-group mount that patch goes through patchHTTPSettings -> patchHttp -> editedHttp (RuntimeSettingsGroupEditor.tsx:486-489, 361-363, 322-329) into editReplacementSection (RuntimeSettingsGroupEditor.tsx:152-170), whose contract is the opposite: `Object.keys(next)` includes the key, `value === undefined`, so it looks up `inherited['default_headers']` and, because the inherited layer has one, re-assigns `Object.assign(edited, { default_headers: structuredClone(inheritedValue) })` (line 164). The group override is then rebuilt with both the edited ordered list and the full inherited legacy map, and httpRequestDefaultsModel.defaultHeaderEntries (httpRequestDefaultsModel.ts:30-37) merges any map entry whose canonical name is not in the ordered list back into the visible rows. The same collision hits the cache path: patchHTTPSettings (RuntimeSettingsGroupEditor.tsx:491-501) clears `cache_content_urls`/`check_newer_versions` with `undefined` when cache is switched off, and editReplacementSection restores the inherited `true` values into the group's browser_emulation.cache instead.

**Failure scenario:** Take an imported LoadRunner/HAR script whose config.http.default_headers is the legacy map form, e.g. {"X-Legacy-Route":"blue","Accept":"application/json"} (importers populate the map, not default_header_list). Open a scenario with a group bound to that script -> Runtime overrides -> HTTP Transport -> Request Defaults. Two rows render. Click the x on 'X-Legacy-Route'. commitEntries sends {default_header_list:[Accept], default_headers:undefined}; editReplacementSection writes back {default_header_list:[Accept], default_headers:{X-Legacy-Route, Accept}}; defaultHeaderEntries recomputes [Accept, X-Legacy-Route] and the deleted row reappears on the same render. The operator cannot remove the header for this group by any route in the UI, and the group override that gets saved and executed still carries X-Legacy-Route: blue - which for a dark-launch/routing header means the group hits the wrong backend for the entire run. Same sequence in the Command Center 'Runtime Settings' dialog (GroupRuntimeSettingsDialog.tsx:450-463 mounts the same editor) for a live run.

**Suggested fix:** Give editReplacementSection an explicit clear sentinel instead of overloading `undefined`, or special-case the legacy-alias keys. Minimal fix: in editedHttp, handle `default_header_list`/`default_headers` before the generic loop - when the patch contains a default_header_list key, set `edited.default_header_list = next.default_header_list` and `delete edited.default_headers` unconditionally rather than routing them through editReplacementSection. Apply the same treatment to the cache_content_urls/check_newer_versions clears in patchHTTPSettings.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**downgraded @ medium — verifier A:** **D012 — verification (slot A)**

Mechanism confirmed hop by hop. `commitEntries` (dashboard/src/components/HttpRequestDefaultsEditor.tsx:395-400) always emits `default_headers: undefined`; `removeHeaderAt` (:406-409) routes deletes through it. The per-group mount passes `onChange={patchHTTPSettings}` (RuntimeSettingsGroupEditor.tsx:1105-1113) with `value={httpSettingsValue}` (:462-465, derived from `effectiveHttp = draft.http ?? inheritedHttp`, :296). #### 109. composeComponentDraft folds a component's init and teardown fragments into the per-iterat...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/scriptDraftFactories.ts:411` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** data-integrity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

scriptDraftFactories.ts:407-410 asserts "The dashboard ScriptDefinition has no init/teardown phases", but ScriptDefinition does declare `init?: ScriptActionDefinition[]` and `teardown?: ScriptActionDefinition[]` (dashboard/src/types/scripts.ts:716-718), and AuthoringComponent carries the same two arrays (dashboard/src/types.ts:2057-2059). composeComponentDraft (scriptDraftFactories.ts:417-421) concatenates `component.init`, `component.actions` and `component.teardown` into a single `actions` array and never populates `draft.init` / `draft.teardown`, so every one-time setup/cleanup step in a Reusable Block becomes a per-iteration action in the composed draft. The rest of the area already reads the phases correctly (replayPreflightUtils.ts:48-55 phaseReplayActions, ScriptRuntimeSettingsView.tsx:73-83 usesPersistentJavaVuserLifecycle, and the debugger's 'init'/'teardown' breakpoint phases in scriptEditorReplayModel.ts:115-117), which confirms the comment is stale rather than describing a real type limitation.

**Failure scenario:** Scripts -> Script Builder -> Start new -> Reusable Blocks -> pick 'OAuth Token Init' (or 'Logout And Cleanup Teardown'). The composed draft opens with 'Acquire Access Token' as actions[0] instead of init[0]. Save it, add it to a scenario group at 500 VUsers and run 1000 iterations each: the token endpoint is hit 500,000 times instead of 500, the SUT's token issuer becomes the bottleneck, and the measured business-transaction throughput is wrong. With the logout component the same composition logs the VUser out at the end of every iteration, so iteration 2 onward runs against an unauthenticated session and fails on assertions that have nothing to do with the code under test. Nothing in the UI signals the phase demotion - the draft simply shows one flat action list.

**Suggested fix:** Populate the phases the type already supports: `init: component.init?.length ? component.init : undefined`, `actions: component.actions ?? []`, `teardown: component.teardown?.length ? component.teardown : undefined`, and delete the stale comment. If the draft editor genuinely cannot display init/teardown yet, keep the fold but surface it (a notice on the composed draft naming the demoted actions) rather than doing it silently.

#### 110. Debug rail rescans the entire replay-event list once per container row on every render
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ScriptReplayDebuggerView.tsx:483` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

Inside the debug rail's inline render IIFE, each container row computes `const subtreeEvents = debugEvents.filter(ev => ev.phase === phase && ev.action_index === actionIndex && (isTopLevel || (...step_path prefix match...)))` (ScriptReplayDebuggerView.tsx:483). That is a full linear scan of debugEvents per container row, executed during render, and `buildDebugRailRenderRows(debugActionRows, effectiveExpandedDebugSequences)` on line 471 is likewise recomputed inline rather than memoized. debugEvents grows monotonically during a live replay (useScriptReplayDebuggerController.ts:208-211 selectDebugEvents recomputes from browserReplaySession.events on every session update), and every session update re-renders this view. The controller already builds exactly the right index structures for this - eventIndexByLocation, debugRowPositionByKey and eventsByStepPath (useScriptReplayDebuggerController.ts:234-236) are all memoized Maps keyed by phase/action_index/step_path - so the rail is doing by scan what the rest of the file does by lookup.

**Failure scenario:** Open the Script Debugger on an imported LoadRunner script with ~200 http_sequence / control_loop containers and start a replay that emits tens of thousands of events. Each incoming batch of replay events changes browserReplaySession, which re-derives debugEvents and re-renders the rail; the rail then performs 200 full scans of a list that is now 20k+ entries, i.e. ~4M predicate evaluations per update, plus a step_path prefix comparison per hit. The rail progressively stops keeping up: the current-step highlight lags behind the engine, the Filter actions box drops keystrokes, and stepping (which triggers another session update per step) becomes visibly unresponsive.

**Suggested fix:** Build one memoized Map<containerKey, {count, anyFail}> from debugEvents (single pass, keyed by `${phase}:${action_index}` plus the step-path prefixes each event belongs to) in useScriptReplayDebuggerController alongside the existing index maps, and have the rail look up rather than filter. Also wrap buildDebugRailRenderRows in useMemo on [debugActionRows, effectiveExpandedDebugSequences].

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D015 (slot A) — Debug rail rescans debugEvents per container row**

Verified at HEAD snapshot. `ScriptReplayDebuggerView.tsx:471-483`: inside an inline render IIFE the view calls `buildDebugRailRenderRows(debugActionRows, effectiveExpandedDebugSequences)` (unmemoized; `countContainerLeaves` recurses per container) and, for every `kind === 'container'` row, runs `debugEvents.filter(...)` — a full linear scan allocating a new array — before the visibility `continue` at 498-503, so filtered-out rows pay it too. Reachability: mounted at `ScriptEditor.tsx:5534-5546` under `workspaceTab === 'debug'`; `ScriptReplayDebuggerView` is a plain function (line 151), no `React.memo`; the rail renders unless `debugActionListCollapsed`, default `false` (`useScriptReplayDebuggerController.ts:186`). Cadence: `script_debug_event` / `browser_replay_event` sockets call `setBrowserReplaySession(msg.session)` per event (`ScriptEditor.tsx:1796`, `2010`), so `debugEvents` (memo, line 208-211) gets a new identity per event; backend `session.Events` is uncapped (`pkg/api/script_debug_manager.go:861-874`). Containers are real: `pkg/convert/enterprisearchive/grouping.go:166` emits one `http_sequence` per LR transaction. Cost is O(containers x events) per render, quadratic over a run; the rail is not virtualized (contrast the author rail, `ScriptEditor.tsx:942`), and the controller already exposes memoized indexes (lines 234-236). Not a regression of the prior fixed item: UNCOMMITTED_REVIEW_2026-07-22's `diagnosisKey` stringify is fixed (now memoized, line 278-287); this scan is a separate survivor. Visible jank needs the large-script + high-event combination and shares the frame with other per-event costs in the same view.

---

**confirmed @ medium — verifier B:** **D015 (slot B) — Debug rail rescans debugEvents per container row**

**Verdict: confirmed (medium).** Chain established at HEAD, hop by hop.

1. **Code exists.** `ScriptReplayDebuggerView.tsx:471` calls `buildDebugRailRenderRows(...)` inline inside a JSX IIFE; `:483` runs `debugEvents.filter(ev => ev.phase === phase && ev.action_index === actionIndex && (isTopLevel || stepPath-prefix match))` for **every** container row, before the visibility `continue` at `:498-503`, so even filtered-out rows pay the scan. No `useMemo`, no virtualization, no row cap (grep for `useVirtualizer`/`slice(0,`/`MAX_` in the file: no hits).
2. **Reachable.** `ScriptEditor.tsx:5534-5535` renders the view whenever `workspaceTab === 'debug'`; the rail is gated only on `!debugActionListCollapsed`, which defaults to `false` (`useScriptReplayDebuggerController.ts:186`). `buildDebugRailRenderRows` (`scriptEditorWorkbench.ts:292-299`) emits a container row for every top-level `http_sequence`/`control_if`/`control_loop`, expanded or not.
3. **Re-render cadence.** Backend broadcasts `script_debug_event` with the full session snapshot (all events cloned: `pkg/api/script_debug_manager.go:869-888, 1542-1545`, no event cap). `ScriptEditor.tsx:1796` does `setBrowserReplaySession(msg.session)` and `:1797-1808` rebuilds `replayReport.events`; both are reducer state in ScriptEditor (`scriptEditorState.ts:413-419, 447`), and the view is a plain function (`:151`), not `React.memo` — so the rail re-renders per replay event, plus on every keystroke in the rail filter input (`:442`).
4. **Consequence.** Cost is O(containers × debugEvents) per render, allocating one array per container, while the controller's own indexes (`useScriptReplayDebuggerController.ts:234-236`) are memoized Maps.

**Refutations hunted, none found:** no memo/effect guard, no parent gate beyond the debug tab, no throttling of socket updates, no virtualization, no test pinning the opposite.

**Prior-report note:** the previously-fixed `ScriptReplayDebuggerView` item (UNCOMMITTED_REVIEW_2026-07-22 #244/#250) was the unmemoized `diagnosisKey` serialization; that fix is present at HEAD (`useMemo` at `:278`). D015 is a *different, uncovered* per-render cost in the same render path — not a regression of that fix.

**Calibration:** magnitude scales with script shape. Requires a container-heavy script (plain recorded HTTP scripts emit `kind: 'action'` rows and never hit `:483`). At a few thousand events × ~200 containers the added cost is single-digit ms per update; the claimed 20k-event/4M-eval figure is the pessimistic (loop-heavy) end. Defect is real either way; severity stays medium — perf-only, confined to the debug workspace, matching the precedent set for the sibling finding.

</details>


#### 111. Script Library stringifies every script's full DSL body on every render, once per row
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:61` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

scriptContainsSecretReferences (ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:61-68) does `JSON.stringify(script.script)` on the complete ScriptDefinition. It is called from the row body at ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:343 as the right-hand side of `(secretStatus?.required.length || 0) > 0 || scriptContainsSecretReferences(script)`, so it runs for every script whose secret status has not yet resolved or that has no required secrets - i.e. for every row during the initial load. The value it inspects is real: pkg/api/handlers.go:841 handleListScripts returns `maskStoredScripts(scripts)` and pkg/api/script_projection.go:790-798 maskStoredScript keeps the full (masked) `Script` body, so StoredScript.script (dashboard/src/types/storedContent.ts:36) carries the whole imported DSL. The component is not memoized (plain function component, no React.memo), has no virtualization despite the repo already depending on @tanstack/react-virtual, and re-renders on every parent state change - sorting, expanding a row, and each of the N secret-status responses that arrive one at a time from ScriptsPage.tsx:199-200.

**Failure scenario:** A project with ~300 imported LoadRunner scripts (this repo's own notes describe single imports around 98k lines). Open Scripts -> Script Library. The initial render stringifies ~300 multi-megabyte objects; then each of the 300 secret-status responses (ScriptsPage.tsx:190-210, concurrency 8) triggers another full-table render that repeats all ~300 stringifies. The main thread is blocked for tens of seconds, the health-filter buttons and the sort headers do not respond, and typing in the library search box (ScriptsPage.tsx:847-853, unthrottled) re-runs the whole pass per keystroke.

**Suggested fix:** Three independent wins, cheapest first: (1) hoist the secret-reference scan out of render - compute it once per script id in a useMemo keyed on the scripts array in ScriptsPage, or better derive it from a backend flag; (2) wrap the row body in a memoized <ScriptLibraryRow> so a single secret-status update re-renders one row; (3) virtualize localScripts with useVirtualizer once row count is large. Longer term, ask the backend for a list projection without `script` (see boundary_leads).

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D014 slot A — verification**

Chain verified hop by hop in the snapshot.

1. Payload is real: `pkg/api/runner.go:993` declares `Script *dsl.Script \`json:"script"\``; `handleListScripts` (pkg/api/handlers.go:840-861) returns `maskStoredScripts(...)`; `maskStoredScript` (pkg/api/script_projection.go:790-798) calls `cloneStoredScriptForReadLocked`, which deep-copies `cloned.Script = cloneScriptDefinition(...)` (pkg/api/script.go:1429). Nothing prunes the DSL for list responses; the client type keeps it (dashboard/src/types/storedContent.ts:36) and `useScriptApi.ts:347` passes the JSON straight through.

2. Hot path: `scriptContainsSecretReferences` (ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:61-68) does `JSON.stringify(script.script)` and is called inside the row map at line 343; it is short-circuited only when an already-resolved `secretStatus.required.length > 0`, so unresolved and zero-secret rows stringify every render. Result feeds `secretStatusUnknown` (344-345), so it is live, not dead.

3. Re-render driver: `secretStatusByScript` / `secretStatusStateByScript` are ScriptsPage state (121-122); each of the N per-script responses (190-213, concurrency 8) sets them in a separate task. No `React.memo`, no row component, no virtualization (333 plain `.map`), and `ScriptsAuthoringShell` renders children in the default `list` subView — so every response re-renders the whole table. Cost is O(N renders x N stringifies). No refuting guard or test found.

#### 112. Script Library issues one secret-status request per script (and up to 100 GitHub requests...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ScriptsPage.tsx:169` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** scalability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The secret-status effect (ScriptsPage.tsx:169-214) fans out one api.getScriptSecretStatus call per addressable script with a fixed concurrency of 8 (SECRET_STATUS_CONCURRENCY, line 57). Its dependency array is `[api, scripts, secretStatusRetryGeneration]`, and `scripts` is replaced by identity on every refresh() (line 227) - refresh is called after every save, import, delete, GitHub bulk import and federation pull/push (lines 412, 429, 598, 606, 612, and via useLibraryFederation's onRefreshLocal at line 362). Each of those re-runs resets secretStatusByScript to {} (line 187) and re-flags every row 'loading' (line 188), so the whole library flips back to 'Checking secrets' and re-fetches N statuses. In parallel the GitHub effect (lines 487-512) fires up to 100 scriptStatus requests with a bare Promise.all (no concurrency limit) and silently truncates at `.slice(0, 100)`, so scripts past the hundredth in unsorted order never get a GitHub badge. onRetrySecretStatus (line 895) is wired to a per-script 'Retry secret check' button but increments a page-wide generation counter, restarting the entire fan-out for one failed row.

**Failure scenario:** A project with 400 scripts, GitHub integration connected. Opening Scripts fires 400 secret-status requests (8 at a time) plus 100 concurrent GitHub status requests; scripts 101-400 never show a GitHub badge even when linked. Delete one script: refresh() replaces `scripts`, the effect resets every row to 'Checking secrets' and re-issues all 400 requests, so the whole library's health column goes back to a pending state for tens of seconds after a single-row action. If one script's status call fails, clicking its 'Retry secret check' button restarts all 400 rather than the one.

**Suggested fix:** Key the fan-out on the set of script ids rather than array identity (e.g. a useMemo'd sorted id string) and merge results into the existing map instead of clearing it, so a refresh only fetches ids it has not seen. Make onRetrySecretStatus take the script and re-fetch just that id. Bound the GitHub fan-out with the same worker-pool pattern and drop the silent 100 cap (or surface it). Ideally replace both with batch endpoints - see boundary_leads.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D017 verification (slot A)**

Traced the full chain at HEAD in the snapshot.

- `dashboard/src/components/ScriptsPage.tsx:169-214`: effect filters `scripts` by `isAddressableScriptId` (`components/scriptIdentity.ts` — passes any non-empty trimmed id, so effectively every script), unconditionally clears `secretStatusByScript` (187) and marks every row `'loading'` (188), then runs a worker pool of `SECRET_STATUS_CONCURRENCY = 8` (57) issuing one `api.getScriptSecretStatus` per script. That maps to a real per-script GET `/scripts/{id}/secret-status` (`hooks/api/useScriptApi.ts:385-388`); `hooks/apiClient.ts:513-544` has no cache or in-flight dedupe.
- Deps are `[api, scripts, secretStatusRetryGeneration]` (214). `refresh()` does `setScripts(res.scripts || [])` (227) with a freshly parsed array, so identity always changes → effect always re-runs and re-fetches all N. `refresh()` is invoked after delete (598), save (606), import (612), GitHub import (412), bulk import (429), and federation pull/push (`useLibraryFederation.ts:229` via `onRefreshLocal` at 362).
- `onRetrySecretStatus={() => setSecretStatusRetryGeneration(g => g + 1)}` (895) ignores the `script` argument the per-row button passes (`ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:505,584`) → one failed row restarts the whole fan-out.
- GitHub effect (487-512): bare `Promise.all` over `.slice(0, 100)`, deps include `scripts`; scripts past the 100th in API order silently get no badge (`githubStatusByScript` consumed at 891).
- Production wiring: `App.tsx:149,2087` renders ScriptsPage on `view.page === 'scripts'`.

One overstatement: the visible "Checking secrets" badge is gated by `requiresSecrets` (`ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:343-345`), i.e. only rows whose script body contains `{{secret.` (61-68) regress visually; the N network requests still fire for every row.

#### 113. Expanding a script row downloads the project's entire test list and filters client-side; ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/useScriptsLibraryModel.ts:87` · **Area:** AREA-25 · **Category:** api-contract · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

onToggleScriptRuns (useScriptsLibraryModel.ts:87-114) calls `api.listTests({project_id})` - the unfiltered run list, each TestSummary carrying groups, live_metrics, history and sparkline arrays (dashboard/src/types.ts:623-672) - and then filters in the browser for runs whose groups reference this script (line 102). There is no server-side script_id filter and no caching beyond the per-script memo at line 94, so expanding k different scripts downloads the whole run list k times. Separately, getRunSortValue (useScriptsLibraryModel.ts:51-56) special-cases only `start_time`; for every other field including `duration` it returns `String(run[field] || '').toLowerCase()`. TestSummary.duration is a Go duration string (`duration: string`, dashboard/src/types.ts:640), so the Duration header rendered at ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:603 sorts those strings alphabetically.

**Failure scenario:** In a mature project with ~5,000 recorded runs, clicking a script name to see its linked runs downloads the full /api/v1/tests payload (many MB including per-run live_metrics history) and discards almost all of it; expanding a second script downloads it again. Then, with the expanded run list showing durations '9m', '10m', '2h', clicking the Duration header orders them '10m', '2h', '9m' - the longest run is not where the operator expects it, which is exactly the wrong answer for the 'which run should I compare against' question this table exists to answer.

**Suggested fix:** Add a script_id (or scenario/script filter) query parameter to the tests list call so the server does the filtering; failing that, hoist the run list into one shared fetch for the page instead of one per expansion. For the sort, parse the Go duration string into milliseconds in getRunSortValue (a small parseGoDuration helper) and reuse it for the cell rendering so display and ordering agree.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D018 slot A — evidence**

useScriptsLibraryModel({api, scripts, projectId}); ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:366-369 calls

limit/summary; useTestApi.ts:325-340 forwards only application/release/scenario/project/folder —

matches are ordered newest-first (tests.go:597, sortTestList) and cut at 200, so in a 5,000-run
project a script's older linked runs are silently absent — ScriptsLibraryTable.tsx:590 then shows

#### 114. Command Center shows no SLA threshold alerts when it auto-discovers the run
**Where:** `dashboard/src/App.tsx:2013` · **Area:** AREA-26 · **Category:** data-flow · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

App.tsx:2013-2019 passes `view.testId ? thresholdAlerts.filter(alert => alert.testId === view.testId) : []` to CommandCenterPrototype — keyed on the ROUTE's test id. But the Command Center's effective run is `testIdProp || autoSelectedTestId || undefined` (CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:960): opened from the sidebar with no run on the route, it auto-discovers the single live run (lines 1070-1118) and renders it fully. In that path `view.testId` is undefined, so the alerts prop is the empty array and ThresholdAlertStrip (CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:1675) renders nothing (ThresholdAlertStrip.tsx:15 returns null on an empty active set), even though App is receiving and holding live threshold_alert entries for that exact run (App.tsx:489-495).
