#### 115. Granularity bucketing rounds every metric to 1 decimal, collapsing sub-0.1% error rates t...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/testExecutionChartModel.ts:938` · **Area:** AREA-26 · **Category:** precision-loss · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

aggregateByGranularity's flush() rounds every averaged numeric field with `Math.round((agg.total / agg.count) * 10) / 10` (testExecutionChartModel.ts:938) — one decimal for all keys. But errorPct is deliberately carried at TWO decimals: mapExecutionMetricToHistoryPoint uses `rounded(metric.error_pct || 0, 100)` (testExecutionMetricsModel.ts:42) while every other metric uses the default precision 10. Bucketing engages automatically: granularitySeconds defaults to 0 = Auto (TestExecutionCharts.tsx:498-501), and autoGranularitySeconds returns the smallest 'nice' interval such that the visible span fits in 600 buckets (testExecutionChartModel.ts:894-903), so any window longer than ~10 minutes at 1 Hz yields a bucket >= 2s, i.e. >1 point per bucket, i.e. the flush() path. granularBaseData feeds every time-series chart via chartDataFor (TestExecutionCharts.tsx:941).

**Failure scenario:** Run a 40-minute test that sustains a 0.04% error rate (roughly 4 failures per 10,000 transactions — a real SLA signal for a payments or checkout scenario). With the default 'Auto' granularity the visible span is 2400s, so auto granularity picks 5s buckets; each bucket averages ~0.04 and rounds to `Math.round(0.4)/10 = 0`. The Error Rate (%) chart draws a flat zero line and its Measurements table reports Latest/Avg/Min/Max = 0 for the whole run, so the operator concludes the run was clean. Switching the granularity selector to 1s makes the errors reappear, which reads as a UI glitch rather than a precision limit.

**Suggested fix:** Make the rounding precision key-aware instead of a flat *10: reuse the same precision map the mapper uses (percent-like keys at 100, everything else at 10), or simply round to a fixed significant-figure count (e.g. `Number(value.toPrecision(4))`) so small magnitudes keep their resolution.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D023 verification (slot A) — granularity bucketing rounds all metrics to 1 decimal**

Every hop traced in the snapshot (repo-relative paths):

1. Code at HEAD: `dashboard/src/components/testExecutionChartModel.ts:938` — `merged[key] = Math.round((agg.total / agg.count) * 10) / 10`, applied to every numeric key not in `NON_AVERAGED_POINT_KEYS` (line 880: only timestampMs/relativeMs/isGapBoundary/resourceSampleOnly are exempt; `errorPct` is not).
2. Precision mismatch is real: `testExecutionMetricsModel.ts:42` maps live `errorPct` at precision 100 (2 decimals); the archive path (`:287`) passes `summary.error_pct` through raw. `pkg/distributed/generatorrpc/service.go:2862` confirms error_pct is 0–100, not a fraction.
3. Reachable by default: `TestExecutionCharts.tsx:498-501` defaults `granularitySeconds` to 0 (Auto); `:780` falls back to `autoGranularitySeconds`, which (`testExecutionChartModel.ts:894-903`) targets 600 buckets; `:783-788` builds `granularBaseData`; `:941` `chartDataFor` returns it for the `errors` chart (`testExecutionChartModel.ts:211`, type `area`, not a stat tile). `TestExecution.tsx:699` supplies `filteredData` in production.
4. Cadence: `pkg/api/settings.go:705` sets `MetricsIntervalSeconds: 1`, so a 40-min run = ~2400 points/2400 s span → target 4 s → nice bucket 5 s → 5 points/bucket → the multi-point `flush()` path (single-point buckets are passed through unchanged, `:915-919`).
5. Consequence: avg 0.04 → `Math.round(0.4)/10 = 0`. The chart line and the Measurements table both consume the same array (`TestExecutionCharts.tsx:1970` / `2077` → `chartMetricSummary`), so Latest/Avg/Min/Max all read 0.

Refutation attempts: no guard, no key-aware precision, and `TestExecutionCharts.test.ts:550-604` pins only tps/avgMs behaviour — nothing contradicts. Partial mitigation found: `TestExecutionHeroMetrics.tsx:41` renders Avg Error Rate at `toFixed(2)` from `summarizeExecutionChartData` over *unbucketed* `filteredData`, so the same page shows 0.04% while the chart shows 0 — a visible contradiction rather than total silence. Exact threshold is sub-0.05% → 0 (0.05–0.149 quantizes to 0.1), so the title's "sub-0.1%" is slightly loose but the cited 0.04 example is exact.

</details>


#### 116. "Avg TPS" hero card shows PEAK TPS once the run has an archive report
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/TestExecutionHeroMetrics.tsx:32` · **Area:** AREA-26 · **Category:** wrong-metric-displayed · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

TestExecutionHeroMetrics.tsx:32 renders `archiveReport?.overview.peak_tps ?? summary?.avgTps ?? metrics?.tps` under the label `Avg TPS` (line 33). `RunArchiveOverview.PeakTPS` is the maximum interval TPS, not an average — pkg/api/archive.go:548 declares `PeakTPS float64 \`json:"peak_tps"\`` and pkg/api/archive_report.go:424 assigns `report.Overview.PeakTPS = summary.TPS` from the peak-selecting scan; the archive overview has no avg-TPS field at all (powerbi_rows.go:39 derives avg_tps separately as transactions/duration). So the same card reports the true trailing average while the run is live (summary.avgTps from summarizeExecutionChartData, testExecutionMetricsModel.ts:580) and silently switches to peak once archiveReport loads.

**Failure scenario:** Run a 30-minute test that averages 120 TPS with a 400 TPS spike during ramp. During the run the Hero Metrics card reads `Avg TPS 120.0`. The run completes, the archive report loads, and the same card — same label — jumps to `Avg TPS 400.0`. Anyone reading the completed-run summary, or comparing two archived runs, records a throughput number ~3x the real average. The neighbouring 'Max VUsers' card genuinely uses `peak_active_vusers` (line 28), so the mistake is not visually obvious.

**Suggested fix:** Either relabel the card to 'Peak TPS' when archiveReport is present (and keep 'Avg TPS' live), or drop the archive branch for this card and always use `summary?.avgTps` (which is populated for completed runs too, from archiveSummaryHistory via useExecutionChartModel). The cleanest is a backend `avg_tps` on RunArchiveOverview so the HTML/PDF/CSV report renderers and this card agree.

#### 117. Poll tick resets the live Test Duration input while the operator is typing
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/useExecutionLiveControls.ts:93` · **Area:** AREA-26 · **Category:** state-management · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The sync effect at useExecutionLiveControls.ts:63-94 unconditionally calls `setDurationInput(test.duration || '')` (line 93). Its dependency array (line 94) includes `test?.groups`, which is a freshly-parsed array on every poll response, and useExecutionTestPolling.ts:60-64 replaces `test` with a brand-new object whenever the JSON payload signature changes — which during a RUNNING test is every 2s poll because `live_metrics` ticks. The same effect goes to deliberate lengths to PRESERVE user edits for the VUser targets (lines 75-80 compare previous vs previously-synced values) but applies no such guard to `durationInput`, so the Test Duration field is overwritten from the server on every tick. DurationField is fully controlled (DurationField.tsx:79-88 renders `value={parts.value}` and emits on each keystroke), so the typed value is discarded, not merely shadowed.

**Failure scenario:** Start a test with duration `30m`. While it is RUNNING, open Live Controls (it auto-opens per the effect at lines 46-61), and in Test Duration → Target type `4` then `5` to change it to 45m. The 2-second poll lands mid-typing, `test.groups` gets a new identity, the effect re-runs, and the number input snaps back to `30`. The operator has a <2s window to type the value and click Apply; most attempts silently revert and `onAdjustDuration` (line 162) then posts the old duration or the user gives up. Extending or shortening a run in flight — the headline reason the Test Duration control exists, since it is only rendered when showLiveControls is true — has no reliable path.

**Suggested fix:** Gate the duration reset on an actual test switch (or on the server duration actually changing), mirroring the vuserTargets pattern: keep a `syncedDurationRef`, and only overwrite `durationInput` when `isNewTest` or when `test.duration !== syncedDurationRef.current` AND the current input still equals the last synced value. Splitting the identity-unstable `test?.groups` out of the dependency array (e.g. depend on a group-name signature string) also stops the effect from firing on every tick.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ high — verifier A:** **D021 — verification (slot A)**

Chain traced end-to-end at HEAD, every hop confirmed:

1. `dashboard/src/components/TestExecution.tsx:108` takes `test` straight from `useExecutionTestPolling(testId)` and passes that same object to `useExecutionLiveControls(testId, test, ...)` at line 203 — no memo, no intermediate normalization.
2. `useExecutionTestPolling.ts:60-63` calls `setTest(data)` (a fresh `JSON.parse` object, hence a fresh `groups` array) whenever `JSON.stringify(data)` differs; interval is 2000 ms (line 8). The payload is `GET /tests/{id}` → `handlers.go:211 GetTestSummary` → `tests.go:798 cloned.LiveMetrics = ...`, and `LiveMetrics.Timestamp` (`pkg/api/runner.go:572`) is re-installed on each metrics tick (`pkg/api/metrics.go:489`), so the signature changes on essentially every poll of a RUNNING test. Only `History` is dropped by the summary path, not `live_metrics`.
3. `useExecutionLiveControls.ts:94` lists `test?.groups` in the deps, so the effect re-runs on every such tick, and line 93 unconditionally does `setDurationInput(test.duration || '')`. Lines 75-80 show the authors' own edit-preserving guard for `vuserTargets`; nothing equivalent guards `durationInput`.
4. `TestExecutionLiveControls.tsx:114,209-216` renders the panel (auto-opened for RUNNING/PAUSED via `useExecutionLiveControls.ts:57-59` + `testExecutionPhaseModel.ts:22`) with `<DurationField value={durationInput}>`; `DurationField.tsx:51,82` is fully controlled (`value={parts.value}` from `splitDurationInput(value)`), so the state reset overwrites what was typed.

No refuting guard found: no `React.memo`/`useMemo` breaks the identity change, no test pins preservation (`useExecutionLiveControls.test.tsx` never re-renders with a new `test` after editing duration), and React 18 does not bail out because the new state string differs from the typed one. Residual nuance: an operator who types and clicks Apply inside the sub-2 s window can still succeed, so the control is flaky rather than provably impossible — the finding already states this. A post-reset keystroke on the `type="number"` input appends to the restored value (e.g. `30` + `5` → `305m`), which is a wrong-value-applied hazard beyond mere annoyance.

Verdict: confirmed, severity high.

---

**downgraded @ medium — verifier B:** **D021 slot-B verification — poll tick resets live Test Duration input**

Mechanism holds at every hop. `useExecutionLiveControls.ts:63-94` ends with an unconditional
`setDurationInput(test.duration || '')` (line 93) whose deps (line 94) include `test?.groups`.
`useExecutionTestPolling.ts:50-64` re-parses the JSON body each 2s poll (line 8,
`EXECUTION_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000`) and calls `setTest(data)` whenever the stringified payload
differs, so `groups` gets a fresh array identity. During a RUNNING test the payload always differs:
`handleGetTest` (pkg/api/handlers.go:201-217) returns the summary snapshot, `tests.go:763-798`
clones `LiveMetrics` into it, and `LiveMetrics.Timestamp` (pkg/api/runner.go:572) is re-installed
on every metrics tick (pkg/api/metrics.go:489). Wiring is live: TestExecution.tsx:108 → :203 →
:574-600 → :916-918, gated on `showLiveControls = isRunning || isPaused`
(testExecutionPhaseModel.ts:22), and the hook auto-opens the panel (lines 46-61). `DurationField`
is fully controlled (DurationField.tsx:51,82 — `useMemo(splitDurationInput(value))`, no internal

#### 119. "Aggregate TPS (active tests)" chart interleaves per-test points instead of aggregating t...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/DashboardPage.tsx:1213` · **Area:** AREA-27 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

aggregateHistory concatenates `history.slice(-60)` from every active test into one flat array, sorts by timestampMs and takes the last 60 entries (DashboardPage.tsx:1213-1223). No summing, averaging or per-timestamp bucketing happens. The chart renders `<Area dataKey="tps">` over that array under the label "Aggregate TPS (active tests)" (DashboardPage.tsx:1534,1544), so with N concurrent runs each plotted point is one individual run's instantaneous TPS, and the window silently shrinks to the most recent 60/N seconds of wall clock.

**Failure scenario:** Start three tests concurrently in the same application/release — say a 300 TPS API soak, a 40 TPS checkout scenario and a 5 TPS smoke run. Open Dashboard → Active Tests. Each WebSocket tick appends one point per test, so aggregateHistory holds interleaved points and the sparkline oscillates 300 → 40 → 5 → 300 on consecutive pixels. The user reads "Aggregate TPS" as fleet throughput collapsing and recovering several times a second, when actual aggregate throughput is a steady ~345 TPS (the number the adjacent snapshot stat shows via stats.activeTps). The chart also only covers the last ~20 seconds instead of 60 because the 60-point cap is shared across the three runs.

**Suggested fix:** Bucket by timestampMs before charting: build a Map<number, number> summing tps across active tests for each timestamp, then emit the last 60 buckets sorted ascending. Reuse the same bucketing for the `time` label. Alternatively rename the card to "Recent TPS samples" and render one Area per test id, but the summing version matches the existing stats.activeTps semantics.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D033 verification (slot A) — CONFIRMED**

Traced the full chain in the snapshot at HEAD.

1. **Code exists.** `dashboard/src/components/DashboardPage.tsx:1213-1223`: `aggregateHistory` loops `activeTestIds`, does `rows.push(...history.slice(-60))` per test (1216-1218), then `.sort((l,r) => (l.timestampMs ?? 0) - (r.timestampMs ?? 0)).slice(-60)` (1221-1222). No per-timestamp bucketing, no sum, no per-series split.
2. **Rendered as an aggregate.** `:1532-1547` gates on `activeTests.length > 0 && aggregateHistory.length > 1`, labels the card "Aggregate TPS (active tests)" (`:1534`) and feeds the flat array straight into `<AreaChart data={aggregateHistory}>` with a single `<Area dataKey="tps">` (`:1536,1544`). XAxis/YAxis are hidden, so nothing discloses the interleaving.

#### 120. 3D heatmap disposes and rebuilds every mesh and canvas label texture on each cell click
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/LoadImpact3DHeatmap.tsx:327` · **Area:** AREA-27 · **Category:** rendering-perf · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The scene-population effect lists `selectedCellKey` in its dependency array (LoadImpact3DHeatmap.tsx:432) and unconditionally disposes every mesh and label sprite at the top (:333-342) before recreating them. Selection only affects one bar's material colour (colorForIntensity(..., item.cellKey === selectedCellKey) at :383), yet each click reruns the full rebuild: a `new THREE.BoxGeometry` + `MeshStandardMaterial` per populated cell (:381-387) and a fresh `document.createElement('canvas')` + `THREE.CanvasTexture` per axis label (:398-426, createLabelSprite at :115-161). With the default 15 metric rows × up to 8 buckets that is up to 120 geometry/material pairs plus ~25 canvas rasterisations and GPU texture uploads per click.

**Failure scenario:** Open a completed run's Load Impact card, switch to the 3D view, and click bars to inspect cells. Every click tears down and recreates ~120 Three.js meshes and re-rasterises ~25 label canvases into new CanvasTextures, producing a visible hitch and a GPU texture re-upload on each selection. Exploring a heatmap by clicking through a dozen cells does this a dozen times; on a lower-powered laptop the auto-rotating scene stutters on every selection, and the repeated allocate/dispose churn drives GC pressure while the animation loop is running at rAF cadence.

**Suggested fix:** Split the effect in two: keep [model, sceneCells] for geometry/label construction, and add a separate effect on [selectedCellKey] that walks meshesRef.current and only calls `mesh.material.color.copy(colorForIntensity(...))` for the previously- and newly-selected keys. Labels never depend on selection at all, so they should move entirely into the layout-keyed branch alongside the grid.

#### 121. Multi-run archive comparison charts only the first 120 intervals of each run, unlabelled
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ResultsPage.tsx:653` · **Area:** AREA-27 · **Category:** data-integrity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

The comparison loader fetches interval summaries with `{ limit: 120, offset: 0, action }` (ResultsPage.tsx:654). The Go handler treats limit/offset as plain pagination and only downsamples when `sample_limit` is supplied (pkg/api/handlers_archive.go:396-415), so the response is literally the first 120 records of the run, and the returned `total` field is discarded. comparisonChartData then indexes rows by array position (`sample: sampleIndex + 1`, ResultsPage.tsx:784-791) and the chart's X axis is labelled just "Sample" (ResultsPage.tsx:1348-1352) with the copy "Showing <metric>; color identifies the run" (:1325-1327) — nothing tells the user the series is truncated. The same truncated array feeds peakComparisonSummaryMetric (ResultsPage.tsx:296-302), which is the fallback used for P50/P90/P95/P99/TPS in the comparison table whenever the per-action stats lack the field (ResultsPage.tsx:317-327).

**Failure scenario:** Two 40-minute regression runs at the default 1s metrics interval have ~2400 interval summaries each. On Results, tick both runs and click Compare. The loader pulls only summaries 1-120, i.e. the first two minutes of each run — the ramp-up. The "Archived Summary Curves" chart shows two TPS curves climbing from zero and ending mid-ramp, with an X axis reading "Sample 1..120" and no truncation notice, so the analyst compares ramp-up behaviour believing they are comparing the whole runs. Switch the metric tab to P95 and pick a single action from the action filter: comparisonTableMetricValue falls back to peakComparisonSummaryMetric, so the reported "P95" for each run is the maximum over the first 120 intervals only — for a ramping profile that is the lightly-loaded portion, understating the real peak, and the Delta-vs-Baseline column is computed from those understated numbers.

**Suggested fix:** Switch the comparison fetch to `{ sample_limit: ARCHIVE_CHART_MAX_SAMPLES }` (or a smaller chart-appropriate limit such as 480) so the backend returns a representative downsample spanning the whole run, and stop passing limit/offset. Keep aligning by index (the downsampler preserves ordering and endpoints), but surface `response.total` and `response.sampled` in the chart copy, e.g. "120 of 2,400 intervals sampled". Also stop using the summaries array for percentile fallbacks, or label those cells as a windowed peak.

#### 122. Results "Duration" column sorts durations as raw strings
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ResultsPage.tsx:557` · **Area:** AREA-27 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

The duration sort branch assigns the raw duration string (`aValue = a.duration || ''`, ResultsPage.tsx:557-559) and the comparator then uses `<`/`>` on those strings (:570-572), so ordering is lexicographic over values like "5m", "10m", "1h", "30s". The column is exposed as a sortable numeric header (`<SortHeader label="Duration" field="duration" ... numeric />`, ResultsPage.tsx:1545). DashboardPage already solves exactly this with parseDurationValue (DashboardPage.tsx:248-259, used at :1014-1015); ResultsPage does not use it.

**Failure scenario:** On the Results page for a release containing runs of 30s, 5m, 10m, 45m and 1h, click the Duration header to sort ascending. Lexicographic ordering yields 10m, 1h, 30s, 45m, 5m — the 1-hour soak appears second and the 30-second smoke test third. A user trying to find the longest run picks the wrong one; clicking again to sort descending gives 5m at the top. The header is styled as a numeric sort so nothing signals that the ordering is textual.

**Suggested fix:** Move parseDurationValue out of DashboardPage.tsx into a shared util (e.g. dashboard/src/utils/durationUtils.ts) and use it in ResultsPage's duration sort case so both tables order by seconds. Falling back to 0 for unparseable values matches the existing DashboardPage behaviour.

#### 123. alignBaselineTimeline does an O(n*m) nested scan over two full archive histories
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/runReport/runReportModel.ts:219` · **Area:** AREA-27 · **Category:** rendering-perf · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

alignBaselineTimeline maps over every current point and, for each one, linearly scans the entire baseline array to find the nearest timestamp (runReportModel.ts:221-232). Both arrays are already sorted ascending by timestampMs (mergeTimelineHistory ends with a sort at :216; mapArchiveSummarySamples preserves archive order), so a two-pointer merge would be O(n+m). It is called synchronously inside RunReportPage's timelineHistory useMemo (RunReportPage.tsx:180-183) with arrays bounded only by ARCHIVE_CHART_MAX_SAMPLES = 5000 per dataset (archiveHistorySampling.ts:1), i.e. up to ~10k current points against 5k baseline points.

**Failure scenario:** Open a long soak run's Run Report and enter a baseline run id in the Baseline Compare bar (or have one pinned so suggestedCompareId applies automatically). Both the current merged history and the baseline history hit the 5000-sample ceiling, so alignBaselineTimeline performs up to ~50 million iterations plus an object spread per current point, synchronously inside a useMemo on the render path. The tab freezes for roughly a second with no loading indicator (the spinner is keyed off the fetch, which has already resolved), and the cost is paid again on every change to the compare id or to either history array.

**Suggested fix:** Replace the inner loop with a two-pointer walk: keep a cursor into the sorted baseline array, advance it while the next baseline timestamp is closer than the current one, and pick the nearer of cursor/cursor+1. That is O(n+m) and needs no allocation beyond the output. Guard with a cheap early return when either array is empty (already present at :220).

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D038 — alignBaselineTimeline O(n*m) nested scan**

**Verdict: confirmed (medium)**

Code confirmed at HEAD: `runReportModel.ts:221-232` runs `for (const baselinePoint of baseline)` inside `current.map(...)` with no early break and no index/cursor — a full linear scan of `baseline` per current point. Guard at :220 only short-circuits when either array is empty.

Reachability chain established. `RunReportPage.tsx:180-183` calls it synchronously in a `useMemo` on the render path, unconditional in the component body. `current` = `mergeTimelineHistory(archiveSummaryHistory, archiveResourceHistory)` (union by timestamp, up to 5000+5000); `baseline` = `baselineSummaryHistory` from the same hook (`RunReportPage.tsx:82`). So ~10k × 5k ≈ 50M iterations is genuinely attainable.

Measured (scratch node repro, realistic 70-key points from `mapArchiveSummarySamples` group expansion at `testExecutionMetricsModel.ts:293-307`): 644 ms at n=10000/m=5000, 327 ms at 5000/5000. Attribution: object spread alone is 56 ms; a two-pointer rewrite gives 58 ms — ~90% of the cost is the nested scan, so the suggested fix is correct (11x).

#### 124. Archive transaction filter inputs fire two backend JSONL scans per keystroke (no debounce)
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/useExecutionArchiveModel.ts:142` · **Area:** AREA-27 · **Category:** reliability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

archiveTransactionQueryParams is a useMemo over archiveTransactionFilters (useExecutionArchiveModel.ts:142-168), and every filter keystroke calls onArchiveTransactionFilterChange → setArchiveTransactionFilters (:364-371), producing a new params object. That object is a dependency of both the transactions effect (:259) and the archive-analysis effect (:311), so each character typed triggers `GET /archive/transactions` and `GET /archive/analysis`. There is no debounce anywhere on the path — the free-text "Status" and "Contains" inputs (TestExecutionArchive.tsx:1852-1859, 1906-1913) and the four numeric min/max inputs (:1863-1902) are all wired directly to that handler.

**Failure scenario:** Open a completed run's archive Transactions view and type `timeout` into the error "Contains" filter. Seven keystrokes produce fourteen requests: seven /archive/transactions and seven /archive/analysis, each of which rescans the archived transactions JSONL server-side and (for analysis) rebuilds the merged graph. On a multi-GB archive the controller is saturated for the duration of the typing, the table flickers through partial-prefix result sets, and the analysis panel re-renders its node/link tables seven times. Typing `1000` into Min ms does the same for the prefixes 1, 10, 100 and 1000. Correctness is preserved by the `cancelled` guards, but the request amplification is entirely avoidable.

**Suggested fix:** Keep the raw filter state for the controlled inputs but derive a debounced copy (200-300ms) and build archiveTransactionQueryParams from the debounced values. Immediate-commit controls (select dropdowns, errors-only checkbox, page size, sort) should bypass the debounce so they stay snappy. A small useDebouncedValue hook in the model keeps the change local to useExecutionArchiveModel.ts.

#### 125. Clearing DurationField's number input silently resets the unit to minutes, turning second...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/DurationField.tsx:51` · **Area:** AREA-28 · **Category:** data-integrity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

DurationField derives its unit purely from the current value: `const parts = useMemo(() => splitDurationInput(value), [value])` (DurationField.tsx:51) with no fallbackUnit argument, so splitDurationInput falls back to 'm' whenever the value is empty or unparseable (utils/timeUtils.ts splitDurationInput signature `(input?: string, fallbackUnit: DurationUnit = 'm')`, and its `if (!parsed.valid) return { value: '', unit: fallbackUnit }`). Emptying the number input calls emitValue('', unit) -> serializeDurationFieldValue returns '' for an empty value -> onChange('') -> the controlled value becomes '' -> parts.unit snaps from 's' to 'm'. The next character the user types is therefore serialized with the wrong unit. The existing DurationField tests only cover replacing the number in one shot and switching the unit explicitly (DurationField.test.tsx:38-58), never clear-then-retype.

**Failure scenario:** A group's Ramp Up shows '30' + 'Seconds'. The operator wants 45 seconds and backspaces twice to clear the number. After the second backspace the value becomes '' and the unit dropdown flips to 'Minutes'. Typing '45' now emits '45m'. The scenario is saved with a 45-minute ramp instead of 45 seconds — inside a 10-minute test, so the group never reaches its VUser target and the run produces a fraction of the intended load. The same sequence on the required Duration field turns an intended 30s smoke run into 30m.

**Suggested fix:** Keep the last known unit in component state (seeded from splitDurationInput) and pass it as splitDurationInput's fallbackUnit, so an empty numeric draft preserves the unit the user was editing in. Reset the remembered unit only when the incoming `value` prop parses to a different unit.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D050 — verifier A evidence**

Chain traced at HEAD, no refuting guard found.

1. `dashboard/src/components/DurationField.tsx:51` — `const parts = useMemo(() => splitDurationInput(value), [value])`. Unit is derived purely from the controlled `value` prop; the component holds no unit state, and the second (`fallbackUnit`) argument is omitted.
2. `dashboard/src/utils/timeUtils.ts:176-180` — `splitDurationInput(input?, fallbackUnit: DurationUnit = 'm')` returns `{ value: '', unit: fallbackUnit }` when parsing fails, so `''` always yields unit `'m'`.
3. `DurationField.tsx:88-90` — the number input's `onChange` calls `emitValue(event.target.value, parts.unit)`; clearing the last digit fires with `''`.
4. `DurationField.tsx:60-62` → `timeUtils.ts:156-157` — `serializeDurationFieldValue('', unit)` returns `''`, so `onChange('')` propagates the empty string.
5. Production wiring: `TestHub.tsx:3232-3247` (Ramp Up/Down) → `updateScenarioGroup` (TestHub.tsx:1968-1976) → `ensureScenarioGroups` (`scenarioFormModel.ts:44-45`, `group.ramp_up || ''`) stores `''` verbatim; `TestHub.tsx:3143-3154` (required Duration) does `setForm({...form, duration: value})`. Same pattern in `CreateTestGroupsEditor.tsx:97-112`.

Re-render with `value=''` flips `parts.unit` from `'s'` to `'m'`, and the select at line 94 visibly (but in `compact` mode, subtly) changes. The next keystroke serializes with `'m'`.

`DurationField.test.tsx` covers one-shot replacement, explicit unit change, and precision round-trips — nothing pins clear-then-retype, so no test refutes the claim.

</details>


#### 126. New Test 'Modeled Load Profile' ignores stair-step stages and draws a flat trapezoid at p...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/newTestRunModel.ts:456` · **Area:** AREA-28 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

buildRunLoadProfilePreview only reads `group.vusers`, `group.ramp_up` and `group.ramp_down` (newTestRunModel.ts:459-472); it never inspects `group.stages`. The groups it receives come from buildEffectiveScenarioGroups -> applyGroupOverride, which for a staged group sets `vusers: stagedPeak` (newTestRunModel.ts:354, via stagedGroupPeakVUsers) while still leaving the stages unread. So a stair-step or spike group is rendered as a single ramp to peak, a hold at peak for the whole duration, and a ramp down. The scenario builder's preview does render stages correctly (scenarioWizardUtils.ts:758-760 `group.stages?.length ? stagedValue(...) : simpleGroupValue(...)`), so the same scenario looks completely different on the two pages, and the New Test chart is the one shown next to the capacity/reservation decision.

**Failure scenario:** Operator selects a stepped-ramp scenario (75 peak VUsers reached in 20 steps over 12m, so mean concurrency is roughly half the peak). New Test's Modeled Load Profile shows a solid 75-VUser block for the full 12 minutes and reports peak 75. The operator uses that picture to justify a capacity reservation and to explain the expected load to stakeholders; the real run averages roughly 38 VUsers and only touches 75 in the final step. Any visual sanity check of the staircase (the whole point of the stepped-ramp shape) is impossible from this page.

**Suggested fix:** Reuse the stagedValue/collectTimeline logic from scenarioWizardUtils inside buildRunLoadProfilePreview (extract it into a shared module) so a group with stages is sampled from its stage timeline, and only fall back to the simple ramp model when stages are empty.

#### 127. Scenario builder Model Preview places ramp-down inside the duration; the engine runs it a...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/scenarioWizardUtils.ts:660` · **Area:** AREA-28 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

simpleGroupValue computes `rampDownStart = Math.max(rampUpSeconds, durationSeconds - rampDownSeconds)` (scenarioWizardUtils.ts:664) and decays to zero by `durationSeconds`, so buildScenarioModelPreview's timeline ends at exactly the scenario duration (collectTimeline caps every point at durationSeconds, scenarioWizardUtils.ts:706-726). The engine does the opposite: the steady-state deadline is `start.Add(mge.preBaseline + mge.targetDuration)` and only after that deadline passes does it call `mge.rampDownVUsers()` (pkg/engine/group.go:468-472), which spreads the cancellations across group.RampDown (pkg/engine/group.go:1381-1385). The other two previews in this same area model it correctly — newTestRunModel.ts:447 `totalSeconds = preBaselineSeconds + steadySeconds + maxRampDown + postBaselineSeconds` and CreateTestModal.tsx:118 — so the same scenario renders two different shapes and two different total lengths depending on which page the operator is looking at.

**Failure scenario:** Operator configures duration 10m, group ramp_up 1m, ramp_down 2m, 100 VUsers. The builder's Model Preview panel shows load falling from 100 to 0 between 8m and 10m and reports a 10m timeline, so the operator believes only 7 minutes are at full load and sizes the SLA window accordingly. The actual run holds 100 VUsers from 1m to 10m and then ramps down until 12m — 9 minutes at full load and a 12-minute wall clock. Opening the same scenario on New Test shows the correct 12m trapezoid, so the two pages contradict each other.

**Suggested fix:** Make simpleGroupValue/collectTimeline model ramp-down as post-duration: extend the timeline to `durationSeconds + max(rampDownSeconds)` and hold `target` through durationSeconds before decaying. #### 128. Scenario builder fires an un-debounced POST /tests/estimate on every keystroke
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/TestHub.tsx:1334` · **Area:** AREA-28 · **Category:** rendering-perf · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

The draft-estimate effect depends on the whole `form` object and on `buildScenarioDraftPayload`, which itself is a useCallback over `[dataPools, form, showBrowserRuntimeSettings]` (TestHub.tsx:1236), so its identity changes on every form mutation. The effect body immediately calls `api.estimateTest(buildCreateTestPayload({...}))` (TestHub.tsx:1347) with no timer — estimateTest is a POST to /tests/estimate (dashboard/src/hooks/api/useTestApi.ts:359-362). #### 129. Capacity reservation timezone field is inert: windows are entered and displayed in the br...

The New Reservation form presents Start/End as `datetime-local` inputs directly above a 'Timezone (IANA)' text field (TimeslotsPanel.tsx:325-337), but toISO converts with `new Date(local).toISOString()` (TimeslotsPanel.tsx:34-38), which interprets a bare datetime-local string in the BROWSER's zone — the timezone field is never consulted. Server-side, `Timezone` is only length/validity-checked and stored; StartAt/EndAt are absolute time.Time values used directly for overlap math (pkg/api/handlers_timeslots.go:129-133, 160, 580). **Suggested fix:** Either (a) drop the timezone input and label the datetime-local fields with the browser's resolved zone, or (b) convert the wall-clock entry into the selected IANA zone before calling toISOString (same approach the schedule form takes by delegating to the backend), and render slot windows with `toLocaleString(undefined, { timeZone: slot.timezone })` so the printed time and the printed zone agree.

#### 130. Re-selecting the same file after Change or a validation reject is a silent no-op (input v...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ImportDropzone.tsx:122` · **Area:** AREA-29 · **Category:** reliability · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

ImportDropzone's hidden `<input type="file">` (ImportDropzone.tsx:122-129) never clears `inputRef.current.value`. The Change button clears React state with `onFile(null)` (ImportDropzone.tsx:143) but leaves the input's value pointing at the previously chosen path, and `acceptFile` (ImportDropzone.tsx:40-51) returns without calling `onFile` when `validate` rejects — again leaving the value set. Because the browser only fires `change` when the selected path actually changes, re-picking the identical file produces no event and no feedback. JMeterImport has the same shape (input at JMeterImport.tsx:478, Change at JMeterImport.tsx:486). The rest of this area already knows the fix: SampleScriptImport.tsx:1012 and 1054 and EnterpriseArchiveImport.tsx:1881/1886/1981 all do `e.target.value = ''`.

**Failure scenario:** In a browser (not the desktop shell), open Import OpenAPI, click the dropzone and pick `spec.yaml`. No change event fires, `acceptFile` is never called, the dropzone stays empty and 'Convert OpenAPI' stays disabled with no error message. The same dead end occurs after a validation reject: drop a 60 MB HAR, get 'imports are limited to 50.0 MB', shrink the file on disk keeping the name, re-pick it — nothing happens. The only workaround is to select some other file first and then re-select the intended one. This affects all eleven ProtocolAssetImport kinds plus the JMeter dropzone.

**Suggested fix:** Reset the input in acceptFile's terminal paths and in the Change handler: `onChange={event => { acceptFile(event.target.files?.[0]); event.target.value = '' }}` and `onClick={event => { event.stopPropagation(); onFile(null); if (inputRef.current) inputRef.current.value = '' }}`. Apply the identical change at JMeterImport.tsx:478/486.

no `value` reset anywhere in the file; there is no `useEffect` that clears it. `acceptFile`

#### 131. dslLineStatus does an O(top-level DSL nodes x mappings) string scan that reruns on every ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/sourceMappingModel.ts:330` · **Area:** AREA-29 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

`dslLineStatus` builds `targetPaths` from every mapping (sourceMappingModel.ts:347) and then, for each notable top-level DSL node, runs `targetPaths.some(target => pathsRelated(nodePath, target))` (sourceMappingModel.ts:349-351) with `pathsRelated` doing up to three string comparisons per pair (sourceMappingModel.ts:304-309). Notable nodes are every `actions[N]` / `init[N]` / `teardown[N]` / `parameters[N]` / `data_sources[N]` (NOTABLE_NODE_PATTERN at sourceMappingModel.ts:26), so the work is actions x mappings and short-circuits only for covered nodes — uncovered nodes, which are exactly the ones this reverse-coverage pass exists to find, always scan the full mapping list. SourceMappingReview memoizes it on `[dslDocument, mappings]` (SourceMappingReview.tsx:260-263) and `dslDocument` is memoized on `[script]` (SourceMappingReview.tsx:259), so the whole pass re-runs whenever the script object identity changes.

**Failure scenario:** Import a LoadRunner archive with ~1,500 generated actions and ~8,000 source mappings, open it in the Script Editor, open the 'Source Mapping' center tab once (it stays mounted — CenterTabbedPane renders every open tab, ScriptEditor.tsx:440-452), then switch to the Script JSON tab and type. Each keystroke changes the `script` object identity, which invalidates `dslDocument` and therefore `dslLineStatus`; the reverse-coverage pass then performs on the order of 1,500 x 8,000 = 12 million pathsRelated calls (~36M string comparisons) synchronously on the render path for a panel the user cannot even see. The observable outcome is multi-hundred-millisecond input lag per character in the editor, which disappears the moment the Source Mapping tab is closed.

**Suggested fix:** Replace the linear scan with an index: bucket targetPaths by their leading `actions[N]` / `parameters[N]` prefix into a Set/Map once, then look up each notable node in O(1) instead of scanning. The prefix is already computable with the same regex used by NOTABLE_NODE_PATTERN.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

#### 132. Editing the script name (or any convert toggle) permanently disables the credential value...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/BrowserRecorderControlPanel.tsx:1766` · **Area:** AREA-30 · **Category:** state-management · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

Every keystroke in the Script Name field calls `advancePreviewReviewGeneration()` (BrowserRecorderControlPanel.tsx:1766), as do the three convert checkboxes (:1772, :1777, :1782) and the parameterization apply path (:715). That state feeds `reviewGeneration={`${previewReviewGeneration}:${sessionId}`}` into SecretBindingReview (:1738). SecretBindingReview's reset effect fires on any reviewIdentity change and unconditionally executes `setStatuses(new Map()); setStoreProvider(''); setStoreWritable(false); setProbeState('idle')` (SecretBindingReview.tsx:305-309) - these lines are OUTSIDE the `if (!preserveEdits)` guard - while its probe effect keys only on `[api, probeRetryGeneration, projectId, uniqueValidNames]` (SecretBindingReview.tsx:446), none of which change when only the generation moved (names/destinationChoices are preserved, the requirements array identity is unchanged). So the card never re-probes, and the value input is `disabled={... || probeState !== 'ready' || !storeWritable || ...}` (SecretBindingReview.tsx:1075) with the placeholder falling through to 'Provider is read-only' (:1086-1088). The 'Retry credential check' button only renders for probeState === 'unavailable' (:940), not 'idle'.

**Failure scenario:** Stop a browser recording that captured a login, click 'Preview Conversion'; the credential card appears and probes the project secret store (probeState 'ready', storeWritable true, per-name status badges shown). The user then does the obvious next thing and edits 'Script Name' - or ticks 'Parameterize inputs', or applies a parameterization suggestion. On that single keystroke the card's status badges vanish, the summary line changes to '<provider> · read-only', and every 'Secret value (optional)' input becomes disabled with the placeholder 'Provider is read-only'. No retry button is offered because the state is 'idle', not 'unavailable'. The user can no longer enter the password they were about to store and has no in-place recovery; the only escape is re-running Preview Conversion (which mints a fresh source-secret session and resets the whole card), and nothing on screen tells them that.

**Suggested fix:** Root fix in SecretBindingReview: either move the probe-state clears inside the `!preserveEdits` branch, or add the review identity to the probe effect's dependency list so a generation bump re-probes. Recording-side mitigation: stop advancing the review generation on every script-name keystroke - the name is not part of the credential scope; advance it on blur/commit (or only where the preview request key actually changes) instead.

#### 134. Recorded-request detail table renders every captured request (up to 10,000 rows) with no ...

The recorder caps a session at 10,000 requests (pkg/recorder/recorder.go:35 `maxRecordedRequests = 10_000`), and the same component deliberately caps the *live* feed at 20 rows (RecordingStudio.tsx:3317-3319), so the ceiling here is an oversight rather than a deliberate bound. **Failure scenario:** Record a normal SPA login+checkout flow through the proxy recorder (a few thousand requests once static assets, XHR polling and analytics are counted), stop it, then click the session card under 'Recorded Sessions'. handleSelectSession fetches the full session and setSelectedSession renders one <tr> per request: at ~5,000 requests that is ~55,000 table cells plus 10,000 buttons in a single synchronous commit, which locks the tab for seconds to tens of seconds. If the user then clicks a row and types a step name, every character re-renders the whole table because requestDraft is state on the same component - the field becomes unusable. There is no workaround in the UI (no filter, no paging), so reviewing/excluding requests before conversion - the entire point of the proxy recorder - is impractical on any realistic capture.

**Suggested fix:** Wrap the tbody in @tanstack/react-virtual (already a dependency, same pattern as the virtualized lists added for large imports), or as a stopgap render a bounded window with a 'showing N of M' control plus a host/path filter. #### 135. Saving a user's role bindings deletes first and creates second, with no minimum-binding g...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/AccessPage.tsx:617` · **Area:** AREA-31 · **Category:** data-integrity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

updateSelectedUser (AccessPage.tsx:617-647) computes desiredBindings, then loops deleting every existing binding not in the desired set (lines 629-633) BEFORE looping to create the new ones (lines 634-642). There is no guard that desiredBindings is non-empty - unlike createUser, which explicitly rejects an empty set (AccessPage.tsx:574-578) - and the binding editor lets the admin remove every row (removeBindingDraft, line 937-939). On any error the catch block only sets userActionError; `await loadUsers()` runs solely on the success path (line 647), so selectedUser.bindings still shows the pre-delete state and a retry recomputes existingBindings from that stale list.

**Failure scenario:** Deterministic path: an admin opens Access -> Users, selects a user, clicks Edit, removes the one 'Project: Payments (Editor)' binding row intending to replace it, and clicks Save before adding the new row. desiredBindings is empty, the existing binding is deleted, no binding is created, and the banner says 'Updated access for jane@example.com' - the user now has zero role bindings and is locked out, with no confirmation dialog (unlike 'Remove Access' and 'Delete User', which both window.confirm). Error path: the admin changes 'Project: Payments (Editor)' to 'Project: Payments (Project Admin)'. The delete of the editor binding succeeds; createAuthUserBinding then fails (403 because the actor may not grant project_admin, or a transient 5xx). The user is left with no binding, the error reads only 'Unable to update user', and because loadUsers() was skipped the inspector still lists the deleted binding - so pressing Save again re-attempts a DELETE on a binding that no longer exists and aborts before reaching the create.

**Suggested fix:** Create the desired bindings before deleting the removed ones (create is additive and idempotent per signature), require desiredBindings.length > 0 (or a window.confirm) before saving, and call loadUsers() in the catch block as well so the inspector reflects whatever partial state actually landed.

No equivalent exists on the edit path, and Save Changes (:1103) is disabled only by `!canManageUserBindings || editUserEmailInvalid`. `removeBindingDraft` (:937-939) lets the admin delete every row; the empty state (:1029-1032) is advisory text living in a *separate* section rendered below the Save button (:1102-1121), so it is easy to miss. #### 137. Repository catalog issues 5 requests per project in one unbounded Promise.all and renders...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ApplicationRepositoryPage.tsx:287` · **Area:** AREA-31 · **Category:** rendering-performance · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

loadCatalogAssets (ApplicationRepositoryPage.tsx:287-308) runs five loadProjectAssets passes concurrently, and each pass itself does `Promise.all(projects.map(...))` (line 137) with no concurrency cap - 5 x N in-flight requests for N domain-scoped projects. The resulting rows are flattened by buildRepositoryCatalogRows and rendered with a plain `visibleRows.map` into a <table> at line 1092, with per-row checkboxes and action buttons and no windowing, even though the repo already depends on @tanstack/react-virtual (dashboard/package.json) and uses it elsewhere. Sort/filter (lines 426-431) rebuild and re-sort the full array on every filter keystroke.

**Failure scenario:** A domain with 40 projects is opened in the Application Repository. The page fires 200 concurrent XHRs (40 releases + 40 scripts + 40 scenarios + 40 tests + 40 data pools); the browser serializes them ~6 at a time per origin, so the catalog spinner runs for tens of seconds and every other dashboard request queues behind it. When it finally resolves, the 'All' tab renders on the order of 10,000 <tr> elements (up to 200 tests per project plus scripts, scenarios, releases, projects and data pools) in one pass - the tab freezes for seconds, and every keystroke in the search box re-filters and re-sorts the whole array and re-renders the full table.

**Suggested fix:** Batch the per-project fetches (e.g. a small concurrency pool of 4-6, or a single server-side catalog endpoint), fetch heavy kinds lazily per tab instead of eagerly for the 'All' tab, and virtualize the catalog table body with @tanstack/react-virtual as ScriptEditor already does.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D080 slot A — verification evidence**

Every hop traced statically at HEAD in the snapshot.

**Reachable in production.** App.tsx:165 lazy-imports the component; App.tsx:2148 renders it for `view.page === "repository"` with the live `projects` prop from ProjectProvider (hooks/ProjectProvider.tsx:12).

**Unbounded fan-out.** ApplicationRepositoryPage.tsx:287-308 wraps five `loadProjectAssets` calls in one `Promise.all`; `loadProjectAssets` (137-143) itself does `Promise.all(projects.map(...))` over every domain-scoped project (scopedProjects, 237-240) with no pool or chunking. The mount effect (348-384) fires it on every domain change. So 5×N requests start in one tick. No throttle exists anywhere on the path; the API hooks are thin `request()` wrappers (useTestApi.ts:325, useScriptApi.ts:347/1327/1354, useRepositoryApi.ts:69).

**Row volume.** `/tests` defaults to limit 200 per project (pkg/api/handlers.go:113-134, 135-137 `defaultTestListLimit = 200`); `/scripts` is entirely uncapped (handlers.go:841-861). buildRepositoryCatalogRows (repositoryCatalogUtils.ts:170-400) flattens every asset with no cap.

**No virtualization / no debounce.** Table body is a plain `visibleRows.map` (1092-1144) with a checkbox and action button per row; the search input writes `filters.query` on every keystroke undebounced (845-847), and filteredRows/visibleRows (426-431) re-filter and re-`localeCompare`-sort the whole array. CSS (Pages.css:8655-8662) adds only `overflow-x`/`table-layout: fixed` — no `content-visibility`. `@tanstack/react-virtual` is present (package.json:33) and used in ResultsPage/ScriptEditor/SourceMappingReview.

**Refutation attempts that failed:** no pagination or slice, no row cap, no memo that avoids re-render (visibleRows identity changes each keystroke), no test pinning batching/virtualization, projects are not polled so no other guard.

One caveat: the "~6 at a time per origin" serialization holds for HTTP/1.1; over HTTP/2 the requests multiplex, so the burst hits the controller rather than queueing in the browser. The defect (unbounded fan-out + unvirtualized table) stands either way.

</details>


#### 138. GitHub import file browser's parent-directory button joins path segments with '' instead ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/GitHubSyncModal.tsx:554` · **Area:** AREA-31 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The '⬆ ..' row calls `browse(browsePath.split('/').slice(0, -1).join(''))` (GitHubSyncModal.tsx:554). Joining with the empty string concatenates the remaining segments without separators, so going up from 'apexload/scripts/checkout' requests the path 'apexloadscripts' rather than 'apexload/scripts'. It only appears to work at depth 1 (a single remaining segment joins to itself) and depth 0 (empty -> repo root).

**Failure scenario:** An admin opens Import script from GitHub, drills into apexload -> scripts -> checkout (browsePath = 'apexload/scripts/checkout'), realizes the script is under a sibling folder, and clicks '⬆ ..'. The modal requests contents of 'apexloadscripts', GitHub returns 404, and the modal shows 'Unable to browse repository' while the listing stays on the current folder (browse only commits state when the response type is 'dir'). The only way back up is to re-select the repository in the dropdown, which resets to the root and discards the selected path.

**Suggested fix:** Change `.join('')` to `.join('/')` on GitHubSyncModal.tsx:554.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D081 — parent-directory button joins with '' (verifier A)**

Code at HEAD: `dashboard/src/components/GitHubSyncModal.tsx:554` —
`onClick={() => void browse(browsePath.split('/').slice(0, -1).join(''))}`. The
empty-string join is literal, not a typo in the report.

Reachability: the row is inside the `mode !== 'push' && !importDraft` branch
(GitHubSyncModal.tsx:477, 551-557) and renders whenever `browsePath` is truthy
(553). The modal is wired in production at ScriptsPage.tsx:916-923 (`mode="import"`).

Path accumulation: drill-down calls `void browse(entry.path)` (566-568) and
`entry.path` is GitHub's repo-root-relative full path — the backend copies it
verbatim (pkg/api/github_handlers.go:141-147, exercised with
`path=apexload/scripts` in github_handlers_test.go:129). So depth-3 browsing
yields `browsePath = 'apexload/scripts/team-a'`; slice(0,-1).join('') produces
`'apexloadscripts'`. Depth 1 and 2 coincidentally work (single segment / root).

Consequence: `browse()` (233-251) awaits `githubApi.getContents` (useGitHubApi.ts:78-86);
GitHub 404 → doJSON error (github_client.go:358) → writeGitHubUpstreamError →
catch sets `Unable to browse repository` (249) and never commits `setBrowsePath`,
so the listing stays put. Depth 3 is the normal layout given the default
template `apexload/scripts/{project}/{ref_key}.json` (settingsPageModel.ts:113).

Refutation attempts: no memo/guard normalizes the argument; no test pins the
behavior (GitHubSyncModal.test.tsx has no parent-directory case). Only the
"only way back" claim overstates — switching branch or another repo, or
reopening the modal, also re-runs `browse('')` (253-257).

</details>


#### 139. One manage_system-gated fieldset wraps the whole General section, disabling audit filter/...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/SettingsPage.tsx:2473` · **Area:** AREA-31 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** previously_reported_open

The General settings card opens `<fieldset className="settings-fieldset" disabled={formDisabled}>` at SettingsPage.tsx:2473 and does not close it until line 3569, so it encloses the Platform, Usage, Entitlements, Readiness, Authentication and Governance sub-panels. formDisabled (line 739) is `loading || loadFailed || settingsMutationBusy || !canManageSystem`. An HTML disabled fieldset disables every descendant form control, so for a principal that holds view_audit but not manage_system the audit action/actor_type/status inputs and the Export CSV button (lines 3533-3538) are inert even though exportAuditEvents guards on canViewAudit (line 1428-1433) and the button has its own `disabled={!canViewAudit}`. The same fieldset also disables 'Refresh Usage', 'Capture Snapshot' and 'Export Usage CSV' (lines 2630-2638), 'Refresh Readiness' (line ~2705), the EntitlementsPanel 'Refresh' button, and 'Open Access & API Keys' (line 3431) - all read-only or separately-permissioned actions.

The only message on the page is 'Current session can view settings but cannot save global configuration changes', which does not explain why a read-only export is blocked. The auditor has no way to filter or export from the UI despite holding exactly the permission that endpoint requires.

**Suggested fix:** Scope the disabled fieldset to the sub-panels that actually mutate DashboardSystemSettings (platform + authentication), and leave Usage, Entitlements, Readiness and Governance/Audit outside it, relying on their existing per-action canViewAudit / canManageSystem checks. Alternatively wrap only the settings-bound inputs in their own fieldset.

Reachability: Sidebar.tsx:149-157 gives the Settings nav item no `requiresAccess` gate; App.tsx:2182 renders SettingsPage unconditionally; GET /api/v1/system/settings is `viewerGlobalAccess()` (route_registry_foundation.go:38), so a viewer/editor/project_admin loads the page with formDisabled=true and no early return (:2419-2427).

The defect is still real for every non-admin: the General subnav tab buttons are inert (cannot reach Usage/Readiness/Governance at all), and Refresh Usage (:2629), Export Usage CSV (:2635) and Refresh Readiness (:2705) are disabled though `/system/usage/export` is viewer-allowed (route_registry_system.go:29) and `/system/readiness` is public. #### 141. loadSettings seeds savedSettings with live-derived generator capacity, so the Capacity ta...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/SettingsPage.tsx:460` · **Area:** AREA-31 · **Category:** data-integrity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** previously_reported_open

When the stored capacity block still matches every default (usesDefaultGeneratorCapacity, settingsPageModel.ts:845-855), loadSettings fetches /system/inventory and derives cpu_cores / memory_mb / max_vusers / configured_available_generators from connected generator pods, then assigns the derived object to BOTH setSettings and setSavedSettings (SettingsPage.tsx:471-472). Because hasUnsavedChanges compares settings against savedSettings (line 727-730), the page reports no unsaved changes and the topbar primary action renders 'Saved' with canSave false (lines 2391-2396). The manual 'estimate from live pods' path sets an explanatory saveMessage (line 1597); this automatic path sets nothing.

**Failure scenario:** On a fresh distributed install (capacity still at defaults: 4 cores / 8192 MB / 10000 max VUsers / 1 generator), an admin opens Settings -> Capacity. The panel shows values derived from the currently connected pods - say 2 cores / 4096 MB / 4000 max VUsers / 6 generators - and the header button says 'Saved'. The admin plans a 30,000-VUser test against that displayed envelope, but the controller's stored capacity model is still 1 x 10,000, so the backend admission/planning numbers (and the capacity preview in Create Test, which reads the server's health snapshot) disagree with what Settings shows. Worse, if the admin later edits an unrelated setting (say a threshold) and saves, the live-derived capacity numbers are silently persisted as the configured envelope without ever having been reviewed as a change.

**Suggested fix:** Keep setSavedSettings(response) (the server's actual document) and only apply the live preset to setSettings, so the derived values show up as a real unsaved change with the Save button enabled; or render an inline note ('estimated from N connected pods - not yet saved') when the automatic preset fires.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D084 slot A — verification**

Chain traced at HEAD in the snapshot, every hop:

1. `dashboard/src/components/SettingsPage.tsx:451-474` — `loadSettings` fetches settings, and when
   `usesDefaultGeneratorCapacity(response)` is true (line 460) it fetches `/system/inventory` and builds
   `resolvedSettings = applyLiveGeneratorPresetToSettings(response, deriveLiveGeneratorPreset(inventory))`
   (line 464), then calls **both** `setSettings(resolvedSettings)` and `setSavedSettings(resolvedSettings)`
   (lines 471-472). No `saveMessage`/banner is set on this path.
2. Defaults match the server: dashboard `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.capacity_planning` = 4 cores / 8192 MB / 1000 Mbps /
   10000 max VUsers / 1 generator (`settingsPageModel.ts:45-58`), identical to `pkg/api/settings.go:709-721`,
   so a fresh install satisfies `usesDefaultGeneratorCapacity` (`settingsPageModel.ts:845-855`).
3. `applyLiveGeneratorPresetToSettings` (`settingsPageModel.ts:857-874`) overwrites cpu_cores, memory_mb,
   max_vusers and availability.configured_available_generators with the connected-pod minima
   (`deriveLiveGeneratorPreset`, lines 812-843).
4. `hasUnsavedChanges = JSON.stringify(settings) !== JSON.stringify(savedSettings) || hasCapacityDraftChanges`
   (lines 727-730); drafts are cleared at 473, so it is **false**. Topbar renders `'Saved'` with
   `disabled: !canSave` (lines 2391-2396) and hides "Discard Changes" (line 2406).
5. Later saves PUT the whole `settings` object (`saveSettings`, line 1469), and the server only carries over
   `capacity_planning` when the raw body omits it (`pkg/api/system_settings_service.go:279-281`), so an
   unrelated edit silently persists the derived envelope.
6. Production wiring: `dashboard/src/App.tsx:169,2183`.

Refutation attempts failed: no inline "estimated" note in the Capacity panels (only the manual
`applyLiveGeneratorPreset` at 1591-1601 sets an explanatory message); `SettingsPage.test.tsx:1384-1413`
pins the displayed values but asserts nothing about save state, so no test pins the opposite. The adjacent
load-failure comment (lines 466-468 region, "so fabricated defaults are never editable or fake-clean")
shows the authors guard exactly this hazard on the sibling path. Not a regression of the prior
"SettingsPage god-file" refactoring item (unrelated size finding).

Original scenario overstates slightly: its arithmetic example is incoherent (24,000 derived vs 30,000 planned
vs 10,000 stored) and I did not verify the Create Test preview source. Core defect holds. Severity: medium.

</details>


#### 142. auth.trusted_proxy_cidrs / trusted_proxy_secret_env_var are missing from the TS contract ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/types/auth.ts:6` · **Area:** AREA-31 · **Category:** api-contract · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The Go AuthSettings struct carries TrustedProxyCIDRs (`trusted_proxy_cidrs`) and TrustedProxySecretEnvVar (`trusted_proxy_secret_env_var`) at pkg/api/settings.go:592-593, and pkg/api/server.go:1238 makes the controller REFUSE TO START in production when auth mode is trusted_headers and neither is set. DashboardAuthSettings (dashboard/src/types/auth.ts:6-27) declares neither field, DEFAULT_SETTINGS.auth (settingsPageModel.ts:75-93) does not include them, validateSettingsDetailed's trusted_headers branch (settingsPageModel.ts:595-612) does not check for them, and the Authentication panel renders no input for them. (Existing values do survive a round-trip, because normalizeDashboardSystemSettings spreads `...settings.auth` at settingsPageModel.ts:756 and that preserves unmodelled runtime keys - so this is a configurability gap, not a wipe. 'Reset All Settings to Defaults' does clear them, as expected.)

**Failure scenario:** A system admin switches Settings -> General -> Authentication -> Access Control Mode from 'Dev Bypass' to 'Trusted Headers', fills in the user/roles headers, and saves. Client validation passes and the backend accepts the PUT. The UI's 'Restart required' badge tells them to restart the controller. On a production deployment (APEXLOAD_ENV=production) the controller then refuses to start with 'refusing to start: auth mode "trusted_headers" in production requires a trusted-proxy gate' - the platform is down and the two fields that would fix it cannot be entered anywhere in the dashboard, so recovery requires hand-editing the settings store or calling the API directly.

**Suggested fix:** Add trusted_proxy_cidrs?: string[] and trusted_proxy_secret_env_var?: string to DashboardAuthSettings and DEFAULT_SETTINGS.auth, render a CIDR list + env-var name input in the trusted_headers branch of the Authentication panel, and extend validateSettingsDetailed's trusted_headers branch to require at least one of them (mirroring pkg/api/server.go:1238) so the save is blocked before the restart bricks the controller.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D083 — verification (slot A)**

Backend: `pkg/api/settings.go:592-593` declares `TrustedProxyCIDRs` / `TrustedProxySecretEnvVar`.
`pkg/api/server.go:1237-1239` (reached from `Server.Start` at `server.go:1289`) returns
"refusing to start: auth mode \"trusted_headers\" in production requires a trusted-proxy gate"
when `productionMode()` (`pkg/api/security.go:25-31`, APEXLOAD_ENV / APEXLOAD_REQUIRE_AUTH) and
`trustedProxyGateConfigured` is false (`pkg/api/auth_resolution.go:97-107`). The settings PUT does
NOT enforce the gate: `validateAuthSettings`'s trusted_headers branch (`settings.go:1462-1483`)
only validates CIDR syntax and, if a secret env var is set, that it resolves — so the save is
accepted with both fields empty.

Dashboard: `grep -rn "trusted_proxy" dashboard/src` matches only `types/generated/openapi.ts`.
`DashboardAuthSettings` (`types/auth.ts:6-27`) omits both fields; `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.auth`
(`settingsPageModel.ts:75-92`) omits them; the trusted_headers validation branch
(`settingsPageModel.ts:594-611`) checks only user/roles headers + login/logout URLs; every
`updateAuth(...)` key in `SettingsPage.tsx` (17 keys, none trusted_proxy_*) confirms no input
exists, and the mode selector (`SettingsPage.tsx:2746-2757`) offers Trusted Headers with a
"Restart required" badge.

Round-trip: `useSystemApi.ts:260-268` PUTs `JSON.stringify(payload)` of the whole state object,
and `normalizeDashboardSystemSettings` spreads `...settings.auth` (`settingsPageModel.ts:753-758`),
so stored keys survive; `mergeOmittedSystemSettingsSections` (`system_settings_service.go:292-294`)
merges only at section granularity, so preservation genuinely depends on that spread (no wipe, as
the finding concedes). Auth Diagnostics does surface the gap (`handlers_auth.go:2658-2682`,
rendered near `SettingsPage.tsx:3182-3230`) but names fields the UI cannot set. Chain holds:
configurability gap + client validation that lets a UI save brick the next production restart;
only recovery is the raw API or the settings store. One correction: a production controller cannot
already be in Dev Bypass (bypass modes are rejected at boot and on save), so the realistic entry is
an oidc→trusted_headers switch in production, or a non-production instance promoted to production.

</details>


#### 143. SHAKEOUT / SHAKEOUT_REVIEW runs are filtered out of the active-run set, dropping the topb...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/appTopbar.ts:118` · **Area:** AREA-32 · **Category:** state-correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

isTopbarActiveRunStatus (appTopbar.ts:118-120) accepts a status only if it is a key of ACTIVE_RUN_STATUS_PRIORITY (appTopbar.ts:12-21: RUNNING, INITIALIZING, PAUSED, STOPPING, PENDING, QUEUED, RESERVED, SCHEDULED) or isPendingTestStatus() returns true. isPendingTestStatus covers only PENDING/QUEUED/RESERVED/SCHEDULED (utils/testStatusUtils.ts:12), so SHAKEOUT and SHAKEOUT_REVIEW - real backend statuses set at pkg/api/testexecution.go:685 and treated as live everywhere else in the dashboard (App.tsx:175-182 PROTECTED_METRICS_STATUSES, components/CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:147, components/useExecutionMetricsStream.ts:17) - are rejected. The surrounding functions in this same file already handle them: topbarRunStatusLabel returns 'Shakeout'/'Shakeout Review' (appTopbar.ts:125-126) and topbarRunTone maps both to 'pending' (appTopbar.ts:135). Both branches are unreachable dead code today, which is direct evidence the omission from the priority table is an oversight rather than a decision. Consequences flow through selectTopbarActiveRuns (appTopbar.ts:141-154), which App.tsx uses to rebuild activeTopbarRuns on every 10s poll (App.tsx:851-859) and to compute desktopActiveRunCount (App.tsx:860-872); that count feeds useKeepAwakeDuringRuns and useDockBadge (App.tsx:1166-1171), and desktop/useKeepAwake.ts:19 releases the OS sleep inhibitor whenever the count is 0. Secondary latent trap: compareTopbarRuns (appTopbar.ts:183) does ACTIVE_RUN_STATUS_PRIORITY[a.status] - ACTIVE_RUN_STATUS_PRIORITY[b.status], so if SHAKEOUT is admitted to the list without also being added to the priority table the comparator returns NaN and the chip ordering becomes implementation-defined.

**Failure scenario:** On the desktop shell, a user launches a single test with script shakeout enabled and leaves the machine unattended. Status goes PENDING (chip shows, sleep inhibitor engaged) -> SHAKEOUT. On the next WS status message App.tsx:580 calls updateTopbarActiveRuns, isTopbarActiveRunStatus('SHAKEOUT') returns false, and the run is removed from activeTopbarRuns; the 10s poll at App.tsx:851-859 confirms the removal because selectTopbarActiveRuns filters it too. desktopActiveRunCount drops to 0, useKeepAwakeDuringRuns calls SetKeepAwake(false), and the dock badge clears. Observable wrong outcome: the topbar shows no active run and the About/dock badge shows zero while a test is demonstrably running, and the host is free to sleep during the shakeout phase - the exact corruption the App.tsx:836-837 comment says the inhibitor exists to prevent. The window widens indefinitely for SHAKEOUT_REVIEW, which waits for a human decision.

**Suggested fix:** Add SHAKEOUT and SHAKEOUT_REVIEW to ACTIVE_RUN_STATUS_PRIORITY with priorities between INITIALIZING and PAUSED (they precede RUNNING), which simultaneously fixes isTopbarActiveRunStatus, makes the existing label/tone branches reachable, and keeps compareTopbarRuns from producing NaN. Better still, hoist a single shared isActiveRunStatus() into utils/testStatusUtils.ts and have appTopbar, CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:147 and useExecutionMetricsStream.ts:17 all consume it, so the next status added to the backend cannot drift across three hand-maintained lists.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D090 (slot A) — SHAKEOUT/SHAKEOUT_REVIEW dropped from topbar active-run set**

Chain verified at HEAD, every hop:

1. `dashboard/src/appTopbar.ts:12-21` — `ACTIVE_RUN_STATUS_PRIORITY` has RUNNING/INITIALIZING/PAUSED/STOPPING/PENDING/QUEUED/RESERVED/SCHEDULED only; no SHAKEOUT keys. `appTopbar.ts:118-120` admits a status only via that table or `isPendingTestStatus`, and `utils/testStatusUtils.ts:12` `PENDING_TEST_STATUSES` is exactly PENDING/QUEUED/RESERVED/SCHEDULED. So `isTopbarActiveRunStatus('SHAKEOUT')` === false.
2. Backend really emits these: `pkg/api/testexecution.go:685` sets `SHAKEOUT`, `:743` sets `SHAKEOUT_REVIEW`; `broadcastEvent` (`pkg/api/metrics.go:957-968`) puts `test.Status` in the WS payload; `pkg/api/handlers.go:175` counts both as active for `active_only=true`, the exact param App.tsx:800-820 polls with. So server sends them and the client filter throws them away.
3. Reachable by a normal user: `components/CreateTestModal.tsx:375-376` checkbox → `script_shakeout`; wizard preset `components/scenarioWizardUtils.ts:536` defaults it true.
4. Consumption: `App.tsx:581` (WS) and `App.tsx:851-859` (10s poll) both rebuild `activeTopbarRuns` through the same filter; `App.tsx:860-872` → `1166-1171` → `desktop/useKeepAwake.ts:19` (`wantAwake = count > 0`) and `useDockBadge`. Chips render at `App.tsx:1850-1886`.
5. Intent evidence: `appTopbar.ts:135` maps both to tone `pending`, and `topbarRunTone` has no caller other than App.tsx:1854 — that branch is unreachable today. (`topbarRunStatusLabel` is also used by TestExecution.tsx:317, so only the tone branch is strictly dead.) `App.tsx:175-182` treats both as protected/live.

No refuting guard found: no memoization, parent gate, or test pins the exclusion (`appTopbar.test.ts:52-131` never asserts SHAKEOUT is filtered out).

#### 144. Filtering JSON by a key name renders the matched object/array as empty because only the c...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/JsonViewer.tsx:296` · **Area:** AREA-32 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The filter builds visiblePaths by traversing the data and adding currentPath only when that node itself matched (JsonViewer.tsx:320-323). A container node matches when its own key contains the query (:302) or when any descendant matched (:309,:314 propagate the child's boolean up), but the descendants' own paths are added only if those descendants matched independently. JsonNode then hard-returns null for any path not in the set (JsonViewer.tsx:97-99), while the effect at :84-95 force-expands every surviving node whenever visiblePaths is non-null. The combination means a container whose key matched is expanded and rendered with its opening brace (:207), its children all render null (:220-252), and the closing brace renders at :255-260 - the object appears to have no contents. This is not the 'show only matches' behavior it looks like: the summary chip that would say '3 keys' is suppressed by `!expanded` guards (:208-214), so nothing on screen indicates the children were filtered out rather than absent.

**Failure scenario:** In a failed-transaction snapshot the user expands the JSON response body and types 'headers' into the JsonViewer filter to find the header block. The traverse pass marks $.headers as visible because the key matched, but none of $.headers.* match the literal string 'headers', so every child returns null. Observable wrong outcome: the viewer shows `"headers": object{7} {` immediately followed by `}` - an apparently empty object - so the user concludes the response carried no headers, or that the filter is broken, and loses the evidence they were searching for. Any key-name search (auth, error, items, result) reproduces it.

**Suggested fix:** In traverse(), when a node matches on its own name/value, add the whole subtree under it to the visible set (a small addAllPaths(value, currentPath) helper), so a key match reveals that key's contents. Keep the existing ancestor-propagation for descendant matches. Alternatively, have JsonNode render the collapsed summary chip ('7 keys') instead of nothing when the node is visible but all children are filtered, so the filtered state is at least legible.

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **D092 — JsonViewer key-name filter renders matched container as empty**

`JsonViewer.visiblePaths` (dashboard/src/components/JsonViewer.tsx:296-328) traverses the data and
`paths.add(currentPath)` **only** when that node itself matched (:320-322). A container matches when its
own key contains the query (:302) or when a descendant returned true (:309, :314), but the descendants'
paths are added only if they matched independently. For `{headers:{a:'1',b:'2'}}` with filter `headers`
the set is exactly `{"$", "$.headers"}` — `$.headers.a` / `$.headers.b` fail both the key test (:302) and
the primitive value test (:317).

`JsonNode` hard-returns `null` for any path not in the set (:97-99), and the effect at :84-95 forces
`setExpanded(true)` whenever `visiblePaths` is non-null. Path strings are produced by the same
`formatPathKey` helper in both traverse (:313) and render (:241), so there is no key-mismatch escape.
Result: `$.headers` renders its key + `{` (:206-207), the children `<div>` renders only nulls (:218-252),
then the closing `}` (:255-260) — a container that looks empty. Same for arrays (`$.items[i]` never gets a
name to match). No memo, parent gate, or test refutes this; there is no JsonViewer.test.tsx.

Reachable in production: SnapshotBodyPreview.tsx:245,287 renders JsonViewer for JSON bodies, and that
component is used by TestExecutionArchive.tsx:2032,2061,2089 and ScriptReplayDebuggerView.tsx:832,990,…

One overstatement in the original: `renderKey()` (:140) still prints the `object{7}` / `array[10]` type
indicator, and collapsing the node by hand restores the "7 keys" chip (:208-214), so the count is not
entirely invisible — but the contents remain unreachable while the filter is applied.

#### 145. The expanded and "Open full body" snapshot views render an unbounded body as per-token Re...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/SnapshotBodyPreview.tsx:167` · **Area:** AREA-32 · **Category:** rendering-perf · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

SnapshotBodyPreview caps the collapsed preview to MAX_PREVIEW_LINES=14 / MAX_PREVIEW_CHARS=1400 via buildPreviewBody (SnapshotBodyPreview.tsx:9-10,22-31,222), but both paths that show the whole body apply no cap at all. renderHighlightedCode (SnapshotBodyPreview.tsx:167-179) splits the full formatted body on newlines and, for json and xml formats, tokenizes every line into individual <span> elements via renderJSONLine (:33-82) and renderXMLLine (:141-165, which emits 3-5 spans per tag through renderXMLTag :84-139). It is called with the uncapped formattedBody in the full-body dialog at :291 and with visibleBody at :249 when `expanded` is true. The JSON branch is no better: :245 and :287 hand the whole parsed object to JsonViewer, and :287 uses defaultExpandedDepth={4}, which mounts every node down to depth 4 as a JsonNode with three buttons and three useEffects each (JsonViewer.tsx:55-278) with no virtualization anywhere in the component. The body sizes are real and known: the engine bounds a single error snapshot at 1 MiB with the response body allowed up to maxBytes/2 (pkg/engine/snapshot_store.go:9-10,42,53), so a captured SOAP or JSON response of several hundred KB reaches the browser intact. The existence of the 14-line/1400-char cap on the sibling path shows the author knew large bodies occur here.

Observable wrong outcome: the tab locks up for many seconds (or triggers the browser's unresponsive-page prompt) and stays sluggish while the dialog is open, on the single screen an engineer needs most when triaging a failed run. The JSON variant behaves the same way once defaultExpandedDepth=4 mounts a large nested payload.

**Suggested fix:** Gate the full render on a byte/line budget: if formattedBody exceeds e.g. 128 KB or ~4000 lines, render plain uncolored text (renderHighlightedCode already returns the raw string for format==='plain') plus a 'syntax highlighting disabled for large bodies' note and a download/copy affordance. Do the same for the JsonViewer branch - fall back to the plain <pre> when the parsed payload exceeds a node budget, or clamp defaultExpandedDepth to 1 above a size threshold. Both checks are cheap and derivable from body.length before any element is constructed.

4. JSON branch: JsonViewer with `defaultExpandedDepth={4}` (:287); JsonViewer.tsx:218-252 mounts every child of an expanded node, each JsonNode carrying 2-3 buttons and 3 useEffects (:55-95,145-177). No virtualization, no node budget.

Reachable + realistic size: rendered in TestExecutionArchive.tsx:2032/2061/2089, CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:2713/2727, ScriptReplayDebuggerView.tsx (8 sites); "Open full body" shows whenever `body` is truthy (:219,264).
