#### 146. Direct-import compensation returns before transaction.rollback(), leaking the library-cla...
**Where:** `pkg/api/direct_import_idempotency.go:359` · **Area:** CC1-A · **Category:** resource-lifecycle · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

`directImportAttempt.rollback` is the sole compensator wired into the deferred cleanup of the JMeter and browser-recording save handlers (pkg/api/handlers_import_jmeter.go:611-617, pkg/api/handlers_browser_recorder.go:1327-1333). It renews the receipt fence first and returns early on either failure — `if err != nil { return err }` at pkg/api/direct_import_idempotency.go:359-361 and `if !owned { return errors.New("...compensation skipped") }` at :362-364 — so it never reaches `transaction.rollback()` at :365-369. `createImportTransaction.rollback` (pkg/api/create_import_transaction.go:240) is the only path that calls `tx.claims.abandon()` (:252), and `abandon()` is one of only two callers of `stopHeartbeat()` (pkg/api/library_import_claims.go:374; the other is `complete()` at :343). The heartbeat goroutine started at pkg/api/library_import_claims.go:165 loops on a ttl/3 ticker with no context and no deadline (:290-323), exiting only when `h.stop` closes. So the early return leaks the goroutine for the process lifetime AND — worse — the goroutine keeps rewriting `ExpiresAt = now.Add(h.ttl)` on the durable claim rows every ~100s (:308-312), so `recoverExpiredLibraryImportClaims` (called at the top of `acquireLibraryImportClaims`, :97) never sees them as expired and every later import of the same (remote, project, kind, sourceInstanceID, sourceItemID) identity is rejected with `errLibraryImportClaimBusy` (:138-140). Skipping asset compensation on lost receipt ownership is deliberate (see the comment at :343-345), but the claim handle is owned by *this* process under a private owner UUID (:102) — releasing it is unconditionally safe and is what the early return wrongly discards along with it.

**Failure scenario:** Single controller, default settings (claim TTL 5m, receipt lease 5m30s per pkg/api/direct_import_idempotency.go:34-43). An operator POSTs a large JMeter plan to the save endpoint with an operation ID. Script persistence is slow (busy SQLite, ~200 scripts), so the `attempt.renew()` guard before commit (pkg/api/handlers_import_jmeter.go:645-648) sees the receipt lease expired and returns owned=false; the handler writes 409 "receipt ownership was lost; retry the save" and returns. The deferred compensator runs `attempt.rollback(transaction)`, whose own `RenewDirectImportReceipt` also returns owned=false, so it returns at direct_import_idempotency.go:363 without calling `transaction.rollback()`. Observable outcome: (a) a goroutine that will never exit now writes the claims settings blob every ~100 seconds for the life of the controller; (b) the operator's retry — and every future import of those same scripts, from any replica, since the claims live in shared settings storage — fails with `library import claim busy: script <id> is held until <timestamp that keeps moving forward>`. The only recovery is restarting the controller, after which the heartbeat is gone and the expired claims are reclaimed. A transient DB error inside `RenewDirectImportReceipt` (the `err != nil` branch at :359) produces the identical outcome with no long-running import required.

**Suggested fix:** Release the process-local claim handle unconditionally, before the receipt fence is consulted. In `directImportAttempt.rollback`, hoist the transaction's claim release above the RenewDirectImportReceipt call — e.g. always `defer transaction.stopClaims()` (a new method that calls `tx.claims.abandon()` / at minimum `stopHeartbeat()`) — and keep only the durable *asset* compensation (journal rollback + AbandonDirectImportReceipt) behind the ownership check. Splitting `createImportTransaction.rollback` into `releaseClaims()` (always safe, stops the heartbeat and expires the lease this process owns) and `compensateAssets()` (fenced) makes the two concerns separable.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**downgraded @ medium — verifier A:** **X01 — direct-import compensation skips claim release (verdict: downgraded, medium)**

Chain verified statically in the snapshot (repo-relative paths):

1. `directImportAttempt.rollback` returns at pkg/api/direct_import_idempotency.go:359-364 (err / `!owned`) before the `transaction.rollback()` block at :365-369.
2. `createImportTransaction.rollback` (pkg/api/create_import_transaction.go:240-259) is the only production caller of `tx.claims.abandon()` (:252); grep for `.abandon()` over pkg/ returns only :252 and pkg/api/library_bundle.go:520 (separate federated path).
3. `abandon()` calls `stopHeartbeat()` (pkg/api/library_import_claims.go:374); `stopHeartbeat` is the sole closer of `h.stop` (:327-335); the goroutine started at :165 exits only on `h.stop` (:290-325) and rewrites `ExpiresAt = now+ttl` every ttl/3 (:305-313), so `recoverExpiredLibraryImportClaims`' expiry test (:610) never fires and `acquire` keeps returning `errLibraryImportClaimBusy` (:137-141).
4. Both compensators route through it: pkg/api/handlers_import_jmeter.go:611-617 (route pkg/api/server.go:887) and pkg/api/handlers_browser_recorder.go:1328-1334 (route server.go:996; operation id always set at :1226).

Trigger correction: pkg/storage/direct_import_receipts.go:168-176 renews on `id + state=pending + owner_token` with **no lease predicate**, so a merely slow import does not yield `owned=false`; it needs a concurrent takeover (:129-147) or a DB error. No test run.

</details>


#### 147. A failed buildRunEngine returns without finalizing the run archive writer, permanently le...
**Where:** `pkg/api/execution_backend.go:98` · **Area:** CC1-A · **Category:** resource-lifecycle · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

`localExecutionBackend.Run` creates the run artifacts first (pkg/api/execution_backend.go:93), and `newRunArtifacts` -> `newRunArchiveWriter` opens three archive files with 256 KiB bufio writers each (pkg/api/archive_writer.go:43-66, buffer size at :48) and starts a permanent flush goroutine on a 1-second ticker (`go writer.flushLoop()` at :97; the loop at :101-117 exits only when `w.flushStop` closes). `stopFlushLoop` (:119-128) is called from exactly one place in the non-test tree — `runArchiveWriter.Finalize` at :365 — and Finalize is only reached through `runArtifacts.finalize` (pkg/api/execution_backend.go:482). Every other early return in `Run` calls `artifacts.finalize(...)` first (:108 for a start error, :116 for a cancelled-before-start run, :164 on the normal path), but the `buildRunEngine` failure branch at :99-102 calls `tr.failTestBeforeRunAndLog(test, err.Error())` and returns with no reference to `artifacts` at all. `failTestBeforeRunAndLog` never sees the artifacts object, there is no `runtime.SetFinalizer`/`AddCleanup` anywhere in the tree, and `localExecutionBackend{}` is the default backend (pkg/api/runner.go:1271, testexecution.go:456), so the leak is on the ordinary single-node path. `buildRunEngine` failure is not exotic: it propagates `engine.NewMultiGroup` errors including the import-execution gate (`importExecutionGateError(g.Script, "launch")` in pkg/engine/group.go's NewMultiGroup), invalid workload settings, zero-VUser groups, and java_vuser lifecycle mismatches, plus the controller workload-bound checks in pkg/api/workload_bounds.go:18-79.

**Failure scenario:** Operator imports a script that still carries an unresolved import-execution gate (needs review/approval), builds a scenario from it, and clicks Start. `newRunArtifacts` succeeds — archive dir created, three .jsonl files opened, flushLoop goroutine running. `buildRunEngine` then fails inside `engine.NewMultiGroup` with `group[0] "...": ...` and Run returns at pkg/api/execution_backend.go:101. The test correctly shows FAILED in the UI, so nothing looks wrong, and the operator fixes the script and retries — or simply clicks Start on several such scenarios. Each attempt permanently adds: one goroutine waking 1x/second forever, three leaked file descriptors, ~768 KiB of retained bufio buffers, and a manifest-less archive directory on disk. Observable outcome after a few hundred such attempts on a controller with a 1024 fd limit: `too many open files` on every subsequent socket accept, archive file open, or SQLite handle — the controller stops serving the API and cannot start new runs, with nothing in the logs pointing at the import path. Restarting the controller is the only recovery.

**Suggested fix:** Give runArchiveWriter an idempotent `Abort()`/`Close()` that calls stopFlushLoop + syncAndCloseDataFilesLocked (and optionally removes the empty archive dir), expose it on runArtifacts, and either `defer` it in localExecutionBackend.Run with a flag cleared once finalize() has run, or simply call `artifacts.finalize(test, "FAILED", time.Now(), err.Error())` in the buildRunEngine branch exactly as the startManagedTestRun branch at :105-112 already does. The second option is the smaller diff and also makes the failed run produce a consistent archive record like every other pre-run failure.

The `buildRunEngine` branch at execution_backend.go:98-102 returns with no `defer`, no finalize, and no other reference to `artifacts`; `failTestBeforeRunAndLog` (testexecution.go:3252) never sees it. No `SetFinalizer`/`AddCleanup` in pkg/. The live goroutine keeps `w` (and its `*os.File`s) reachable, so os.File finalizers cannot reclaim the fds. **Stated trigger: refuted**

#### 148. HA script read-refresh has no coalescing window: every script GET does a full ListScripts...
**Where:** `pkg/api/script.go:801` · **Area:** CC1-B · **Category:** concurrency · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** previously_reported_open

refreshScriptsForHARead (pkg/api/script.go:801-806) is the only one of the four HA read-refresh paths with no staleness/coalescing guard, so it calls reloadStoredScripts unconditionally on every read. reloadStoredScripts (pkg/api/persistence.go:98) takes the process-global tr.contentReloadMu at persistence.go:102 and holds it across tr.scriptStore.ListScripts("", nil) at persistence.go:107 - a full scripts-table scan that SELECTs and JSON-decodes metadata_json, config, data_sources, parameters, init, actions and teardown for EVERY script in the install (pkg/storage/sqlite_scripts.go:477 column list, decodeStoredScriptJSON at sqlite_scripts.go:513) - then rebuilds the whole tr.scripts map and re-indexes every ref key under a global tr.mu.Lock() at persistence.go:129. The revision guard at persistence.go:130 fires only AFTER the expensive read, so it prevents clobbering but never avoids the work. Callers are the ordinary read APIs: GetScript (script.go:789), ListScripts (script.go:908), ListScriptsFiltered (script.go:922), ListScriptsWithUsage (script.go:1351), reached from 30+ handlers. Sibling paths all got the fix this one missed: refreshScenariosForHARead has a 250 ms window (pkg/api/scenario.go:561) and even performs the same reloadStoredScripts call under that window (scenario.go:563); refreshTestsForHARead has haTestRefreshInterval (pkg/api/tests.go:143) with a comment at tests.go:136-142 describing exactly this bug ('Concurrent dashboard polls therefore queued one complete DB scan each behind testReloadMu even though the first scan had already made the others redundant'); refreshCapacityBindingsForHAListRead implements a full singleflight with a completion channel (pkg/api/timeslot_reservation.go:464-500). refreshScriptsForHARead also lacks the holdsExecutionLeadership() short-circuit that tests.go:131 has, so the leader pays the cost too.

**Failure scenario:** HA mode (cfg.HAExecutionLeadership true, so tr.leadership is non-nil per pkg/api/server.go:346-350) on an install with a few hundred imported LoadRunner scripts - the repo's own notes describe single imported scripts in the ~98k-line range, so a script row's JSON blobs are megabytes. An operator opens the Scripts page: ListScriptsFiltered (script.go:922) triggers one full reload. They click a script: GetScript (script.go:789) triggers a second full reload of every script in the install just to return one. Meanwhile another operator creates a 6-group scenario; scenarioRequestProjectID (handlers_scenarios.go:99) calls GetScript once per group, issuing 6 more full-table reloads for a single POST. Because reloadStoredScripts holds tr.contentReloadMu (persistence.go:102) for the whole read, these do not share work - each one waits for the previous to finish and then repeats the identical scan, and each ends by taking the global tr.mu write lock (persistence.go:129), which blocks every concurrent tr.mu.RLock reader (GetTest, ListScenarios, run calendar, live metrics). Observable outcome: script-list and script-detail latency grows linearly with total script count and with the number of concurrent dashboard clients, the whole controller UI stalls in bursts each time the write lock is taken, and CPU is dominated by repeatedly JSON-decoding scripts nobody asked for. The identical scenario against the tests, scenarios, and capacity-binding endpoints is fast, because those three paths collapse a request burst into one refresh.

**Suggested fix:** Give refreshScriptsForHARead the same treatment its three siblings already have. Minimal version: add haScriptRefreshMu sync.Mutex + haScriptRefreshAt time.Time to TestRunner (pkg/api/runner.go, next to haScenarioRefreshMu at runner.go:194) and gate reloadStoredScripts behind a staleness window, mirroring pkg/api/scenario.go:558-572 including the `force ...bool` escape hatch for the write paths that need read-your-writes. Better version: extract the timeslot_reservation.go:464-500 singleflight into one shared helper and route all four refresh paths (scripts, scenarios, tests, capacity bindings) through it, so concurrent callers share one in-flight reload instead of queueing redundant ones. Also consider adding the `|| tr.holdsExecutionLeadership()` short-circuit that tests.go:131 uses, if scripts (unlike tests) are only mutated through the leader.

#### 149. Default in-process cache backend never sweeps expired entries or rate-limit buckets, so i...
**Where:** `pkg/api/cache_backend.go:356` · **Area:** CC1-C · **Category:** resource-lifecycle · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

memoryCacheBackend is the default cache backend -- pkg/api/cache_backend.go:152-156 selects it for the empty/unset backend value -- and neither of its two maps has any eviction path. (1) Idempotency: enforceIdempotencyKey (pkg/api/middleware.go:320-331) builds `scope = actor|method|path|Idempotency-Key` and calls ReserveIdempotencyKey with a 15-minute TTL (middleware.go:353-355). The memory implementation at cache_backend.go:342-357 writes `m.entries[key] = memoryCacheEntry{... expiresAt: ...}` and returns; nothing sweeps. The only place an entry is removed is the lazy delete inside getJSON at cache_backend.go:479-485, which fires only when that EXACT key is looked up again after expiry -- and by construction a fresh idempotency key is never looked up again. So each distinct Idempotency-Key permanently costs one map entry plus the full scope string. (2) Rate limits: AllowRateLimit at cache_backend.go:386-395 writes `m.rateLimits[cacheKey] = bucket` and resets the bucket's counter in place when its window rolls over, but never deletes the key. Two of the three callers key by remote peer address -- `"oidc-login:"+peer` (pkg/api/auth_oidc.go:616) and `"ci-oidc-exchange:"+peer` (pkg/api/ci_auth.go:359) -- so the key space is one permanent entry per distinct client IP that has ever authenticated. Both maps are guarded by a single mutex with no size ceiling and no background sweep anywhere in the file.

**Failure scenario:** A CI fleet drives the API with idempotent mutating calls -- the exact pattern the Idempotency-Key header exists for -- at a modest 1 request/second against a single-node (default, no Redis) controller. Each request adds one permanent memoryCacheEntry whose key is `service-account:<id>|POST|/api/v1/...|<uuid>` (~120-200 bytes with map overhead). That is ~86k entries and ~15 MB per day, ~5 GB per year, and the controller RSS climbs steadily with request volume and never falls, including across long idle periods. Independently, because CI runners get ephemeral addresses, every runner that performs a CI OIDC token exchange leaves a permanent rateLimits entry keyed by its IP, so that map grows with cumulative distinct runner IPs. Neither is adversarial -- it is the documented happy path -- and the only recovery is a controller restart.

**Suggested fix:** Give memoryCacheBackend a bound and a sweep: (a) run an opportunistic sweep on write -- every Nth setJSON/ReserveIdempotencyKey, walk and drop entries whose expiresAt has passed (amortized O(1) and needs no goroutine); (b) add a hard maxEntries with oldest-expiry-first eviction so a burst cannot outrun the sweep; (c) drop rateLimits buckets whose resetAt is older than one window during the same sweep. The existing boundedcache/StringCache pattern in pkg/internal/boundedcache is the house style for (b) and could be reused directly.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **X10 — memoryCacheBackend never sweeps expired entries or rate buckets**

CONFIRMED (medium, resource-lifecycle).

Default backend: newCacheBackend returns memoryCacheBackend for the empty/unset value (cache_backend.go:150-156); struct holds bare maps with no size/byte fields (:276-282). Exhaustive grep of `m.entries` / `m.rateLimits` in non-test code shows writes at :356 (ReserveIdempotencyKey), :372 (LoadOrStoreValue), :472 (setJSON), :395 (AllowRateLimit) and exactly one delete — the same-key lazy expiry inside getJSON (:483-486). No sweeper goroutine, no cap, no time.AfterFunc.

Trigger is production wiring: enforceIdempotencyKey runs in both auth middlewares (middleware.go:204,269) with `s.cache` as the store (server.go:573) and keys on the client-supplied header (middleware.go:330-331), so each key is written once and never re-read. An additional non-opt-in driver exists: CI OIDC exchange caches a per-token hashed key via LoadOrStoreValue (ci_auth.go:888). Rate-limit keys carry the peer IP (auth_oidc.go:612-616, ci_auth.go:355-359) and are never deleted.

</details>


#### 150. Scheduler sweep re-materializes the entire script and scenario library from the database ...
**Where:** `pkg/api/scheduler.go:313` · **Area:** CC1-C · **Category:** efficiency · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

Under HA (APEXLOAD_CONTROLLER_HA=true, cmd/controller/main.go:119 -> pkg/api/server.go:350 -> WithExecutionLeadership) the leader's schedule sweep unconditionally reloads all durable content on every tick. pkg/api/scheduler.go:313 calls reloadStoredScripts and :316 calls reloadStoredScenarios, and the sweep ticker interval is defaultScenarioSchedulerSweepInterval = 30 * time.Second (pkg/api/scheduler.go:81, used at :150/:179/:192). reloadStoredScripts (pkg/api/persistence.go:98-140) does `ListScripts("", nil)` and then builds a COMPLETE second map `loaded` holding a StoredScript for every script -- including the embedded full `Script: script` payload with its entire action list -- before atomically swapping it in at persistence.go:137. So peak resident memory is 2x the whole script library, every 30 seconds, and the old copy becomes garbage. reloadStoredScenarios (pkg/api/persistence.go:182-223) is worse on the database: for each scenario it issues GetScenario, ListScenarioDataPoolBindings and ListScenarioSchedules, i.e. 3N+1 queries per tick. Neither function has any change detection -- there is a contentRevision guard at persistence.go:130 but it only aborts the swap if something else mutated concurrently; it does not skip the read when nothing changed. This is distinct from the already-owned scheduler finding about conflict schedules being durably rewritten each tick; that one is about writes, this one is about unconditional full-content reads and re-materialization.

**Failure scenario:** An enterprise install has 400 imported LoadRunner scripts, several of which are the ~100k-action imports this project explicitly supports, plus 120 scenarios. Every 30 seconds the HA leader reads all 400 script rows, allocates a full duplicate of every action list, swaps, and drops the previous copy; simultaneously it issues 361 scenario-related queries. Observable outcome: the controller shows a 2x sawtooth in RSS with a 30-second period even when no test is running, GC runs constantly, and on SQLite (the default store, which serializes on a single connection per the project's SetMaxOpenConns discipline) the sweep's query burst contends with live metric writes, so run status/metric persistence latency spikes on a fixed 30s cadence. If the library is large enough, the transient 2x peak alone can push the pod over its memory limit.

**Suggested fix:** Make the pre-sweep refresh change-driven instead of unconditional. Cheapest correct version: have ListScripts/ListScenarios expose a max(updated_at)+row-count probe (or reuse the existing contentRevision as a durable column) and skip the full reload when it is unchanged since the last sweep; that alone removes the steady-state cost since content rarely changes between ticks. Second, mutate the existing tr.scripts map in place for added/changed/removed IDs rather than building a full parallel map, which removes the 2x peak. Third, batch the scenario child reads (one query per child table filtered by the scenario ID set) instead of 3N per tick.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **X09 — Scheduler sweep re-materializes script/scenario library every 30s**

CONFIRMED (medium, efficiency).

Chain verified end to end: worker ticker uses `sweepInterval` defaulting to `defaultScenarioSchedulerSweepInterval = 30 * time.Second` (scheduler.go:81,150,177,192); Start is wired in production (server.go:2190). RunDueSchedules returns early for non-leaders (scheduler.go:261), then at :312-319 unconditionally calls reloadStoredScripts/reloadStoredScenarios whenever `runner.leadership != nil` (HA only; set at server.go:347-350 from APEXLOAD_CONTROLLER_HA, cmd/controller/main.go:119).

reloadStoredScripts (persistence.go:98-153) issues unfiltered `ListScripts("", nil)`, which selects and decodes the full `actions` payload per row (sqlite_scripts.go:477,514), builds a complete parallel `loaded` map (:111-128) and swaps at :147 — 2x peak. The contentRevision check at :130 aborts only the swap, never the read. reloadStoredScenarios (:191-222) does GetScenario + ListScenarioDataPoolBindings + ListScenarioSchedules per scenario: 3N+1 queries per tick. Weakest part of the report is the "SQLite default store" flavor — HA realistically implies Postgres.

</details>


#### 151. listOperationalTestSnapshots deep-clones every run ever stored on each Prometheus scrape ...
**Where:** `pkg/api/tests.go:512` · **Area:** CC1-C · **Category:** efficiency · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

listOperationalTestSnapshots (pkg/api/tests.go:512-527) iterates all of tr.tests and calls cloneManagedTestFieldsLocked on every entry while holding tr.mu.RLock. That clone is a full deep copy of every exported field -- Groups, DataPools, GeneratorShards, GoalTargets, VUserRamps, CapacityAdvisory, RuntimeSettings, Archive, TelemetryHealth, the thresholdAlert maps, and critically `cloned.LiveMetrics = cloneLiveMetrics(test.LiveMetrics)` at pkg/api/tests.go:798, which copies the run's final per-transaction / per-dependency / per-group metric maps. Only History and Sparkline are dropped (tests.go:523-524). Because tr.tests never evicts terminal runs (see the companion finding at pkg/api/persistence.go:406), the cost of this call is O(all runs ever created), not O(active runs). It is invoked from eleven read paths, including the Prometheus scrape handler at pkg/api/prometheus_exposition.go:15, the fleet capacity and load-zone dashboard endpoints at pkg/api/handlers_fleet.go:215 and :221, usage accounting at pkg/api/usage_accounting.go:215/226, entitlements at pkg/api/handlers_entitlements.go:42, and the run calendar at pkg/api/run_calendar.go:514. Every one of those consumers reads only cheap scalar fields: scalingSignalStats (prometheus_exposition.go:298-319) touches Status, TotalVUsers and Groups; the status histogram at prometheus_exposition.go:18-23 touches Status alone.

**Failure scenario:** A controller with 3,000 accumulated runs is scraped by Prometheus every 15s and has four dashboards open polling fleet capacity every 5s. Each of those requests deep-clones 3,000 ManagedTests including 3,000 LiveMetrics maps, allocating tens of MB of short-lived garbage per call, several times per second. Observable outcome: controller CPU sits high with no test running, GC pressure and pause time climb, and because the clone loop holds tr.mu.RLock for its whole duration, writers that need tr.mu (metrics ingestion, status transitions) queue behind it -- so live-run metric updates stutter on an otherwise idle controller. The symptom scales with historical run count, so it appears gradually and looks unrelated to load.

**Suggested fix:** Introduce a narrow value type (id, status, project, total VUsers, protocol->VUsers, created/started/ended) and a listOperationalTestSignals() that materializes only that under the read lock; repoint prometheus_exposition, scalingSignalStats, entitlements, usage accounting and the restart guard at it. Keep the deep-clone variant only for callers that genuinely serialize a ManagedTest. As a cheap independent win, skip cloneLiveMetrics when the caller does not need it.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **X08 — listOperationalTestSnapshots deep-clones every retained run per scrape**

CONFIRMED (medium, efficiency).

Mechanism verified: pkg/api/tests.go:512-527 iterates all of `tr.tests` under `tr.mu.RLock` (deferred unlock at :516) and calls `cloneManagedTestFieldsLocked` per entry; only History/Sparkline are dropped (:523-524). That clone (tests.go:777-807) deep-copies Groups, DataPools, RuntimeSettings, Archive, threshold maps and `LiveMetrics` (:798 -> cloneLiveMetrics, tests.go:832+ copying ErrorBreakdown/Transactions/DependencyHealth/GroupMetrics/GeneratorResources maps).

Reachability/scale: 12 non-test call sites, including the /metrics scrape (prometheus_exposition.go:15, routed at server.go:1046/1418) and two per fleet poll (handlers_fleet.go:215,221). Consumers read scalars only (prometheus_exposition.go:298-319). `tr.tests` has no automatic eviction — deletes exist only at tests.go:1257 (user delete), persistence.go:584 (row gone) and :1329 (project delete); no test-record retention job exists. Terminal runs keep populated LiveMetrics (persistence.go:1036). Guard hunt found no memoization on any caller.

#### 152. Final-drain network-latency probe is a context-free fire-and-forget goroutine that writes...
**Where:** `pkg/api/metrics.go:864` · **Area:** CC1-D · **Category:** resource-lifecycle · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

pkg/api/metrics.go:864, inside publishFinalLocalMetrics, launches `go tr.measureNetworkLatency(test, live)` as a bare goroutine with no context and no lifecycle ownership (it does not go through s.launchBackground at pkg/api/server.go:1946, so no WaitGroup tracks it). pkg/api/execution_backend.go:154 calls publishFinalLocalMetrics and then at :163-168 immediately takes the archive commit fence, finalizes the archive, and transitions the run to COMPLETE - microseconds later. The probe itself is slow and uncancellable: pkg/api/latency.go:53 fans out over up to 64 targets (maxLatencyProbeTargets, :31) with only 8 concurrent workers (maxConcurrentLatencyTargets, :32), and each target costs up to 5s for the HEAD probe plus 5s for the GET fallback (pkg/api/latency.go:612-624 with the 5s client Timeout at :707) plus up to 2s of traceroute (:907-909), so the goroutine can run for tens of seconds past run completion. When it finally writes back at pkg/api/latency.go:55-66 the only guard is `tr.tests[test.ID] != test` - there is no terminal-status check - and a completed test stays in tr.tests (the only deletes are explicit test delete at pkg/api/tests.go:1257, project delete at pkg/api/persistence.go:1329, and retention at pkg/api/persistence.go:584). So it overwrites test.lastNetworkLatency (:61), replaces test.LiveMetrics and rewrites the final test.History entry via replaceLiveMetricsLocked (:65, pkg/api/metrics.go:665-682), appends the post-run sample into the stability window at pkg/api/latency.go:482-517 (skewing SampleCount/SuccessRatePct/JitterMs on that final point), and broadcasts a latency_update WebSocket event (:73-80) for a run the controller has already reported COMPLETE.

**Failure scenario:** A local (non-distributed) run finishes normally against a script with several slow or unreachable endpoints. MultiGroupEngine.Run returns; pkg/api/execution_backend.go:154 calls publishFinalLocalMetrics, which at pkg/api/metrics.go:864 spawns the latency probe and returns. Lines 163-168 finalize the archive and mark the run COMPLETE, and the UI shows the finished run. Meanwhile the probe is still working through its targets - each unreachable one burning 5s on HEAD, 5s on the GET fallback, and 2s on traceroute - and finishes, say, 40s later, with zero load now on the endpoints. It takes tr.mu, sees the test still present in tr.tests (completed tests are never removed on completion), and overwrites the finished run's test.LiveMetrics.Latency and its final History point with the idle measurement, appends that idle sample to the per-target stability window so SuccessRatePct and JitterMs for the run's last point are computed over a mix of under-load and no-load samples, and pushes a latency_update WebSocket event for a run that is already COMPLETE. Observable wrong outcome: GET /tests/{id} for the finished run reports network latency measured with no load applied - the opposite of what the panel is for - and a completed run's dashboard visibly mutates seconds after it stopped. A controller restart silently 'fixes' it, because the reload path rebuilds LiveMetrics from the durable per-interval summaries (pkg/api/persistence.go:1024-1036), which were written during the run and are correct - which is exactly what makes this hard to notice or reproduce from persisted state.

**Suggested fix:** Two independent fixes, either of which closes it; do both. (1) Give measureNetworkLatency a context and stop spawning it bare: thread the run's execution context (or an s.launchBackground-tracked context) in, pass it down through collectLatencyTargets into measureEndpointHTTPLatency/measureEndpointTCPLatency/measureLatencyRoute (which already takes a ctx internally at pkg/api/latency.go:907, and http.NewRequest at :634 just needs to become NewRequestWithContext), so the probe dies with the run and with controller shutdown. (2) Independently, harden the write-back at pkg/api/latency.go:56 to also reject terminal runs - `if test == nil || tr.tests[test.ID] != test || isTerminalTestStatus(test.Status) { return }` - so a probe that is already in flight when the run ends discards its result instead of publishing it. Consider whether publishFinalLocalMetrics should spawn the probe at all, since by construction its result can only ever describe an unloaded system.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **X12 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Chain verified end to end in the snapshot.

- `pkg/api/metrics.go:864` — bare `go tr.measureNetworkLatency(test, live)` inside `publishFinalLocalMetrics`; not `s.launchBackground` (`pkg/api/server.go:1943`), so untracked.
- `pkg/api/latency.go:40` — signature takes no `context.Context`; probes are uncancellable (`http.Client{Timeout: 5s}` at :707, HEAD then GET fallback :613-624, TCP fallback :590, traceroute 2s :907; 64 targets/8 workers :31-32,:98,:325).
- `pkg/api/execution_backend.go:154` then :163-168 — probe is spawned, then the archive fence, `artifacts.finalize`, and `completeTestRunUnderArchiveFence` run immediately; `testexecution.go:3309` sets COMPLETE.
- Write-back guard at `pkg/api/latency.go:56` is only `tr.tests[test.ID] != test`; no `isTerminalTestStatus` check (`execution_backend.go:556`), and completed tests stay in `tr.tests` (only deletes: `tests.go:1257`, `persistence.go:584`, `:1329`).
- Effect: overwrites `test.lastNetworkLatency` (:61), `test.LiveMetrics` and `History[last]` via `replaceLiveMetricsLocked` (`metrics.go:665-682`), appends an idle sample to the stability window (:492-517), and broadcasts `latency_update` (:73-80). `GetTest` serves this in-memory clone (`tests.go:29-44`).

Guard hunt: `beginLatencyProbe` (:122) only de-dupes concurrent probes — an in-flight ticker probe (:832) has the same shape. Blast radius correctly self-limited by the finding: the durable per-interval rows were already written from the pre-probe clone (`metrics.go:516-519`), so a restart heals it. Only qualifier: :848 suppresses the drain (and the probe) when the ticker already published that window.

</details>


#### 153. Every Go type declared outside pkg/api is erased to a free-form object in the spec and to...
**Where:** `pkg/api/openapi_contract_infer.go:1100` · **Area:** CC3-A · **Category:** schema-fidelity · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

inferRouteContracts parses only the single directory containing server.go (openapi_contract_infer.go:62 parser.ParseDir(..., dir, ...)), so openAPISchemaForASTType's *ast.SelectorExpr branch (:1100-1127) cannot resolve any cross-package type. Apart from six hardcoded exceptions (time.Time, json.RawMessage, storage.SharedDataPool, storage.SharedDataPoolRow, correlate.DiffClass, generatorrpc.ProtocolRuntimeCapacity) it returns `{type: object, additionalProperties: true, description: "Go type: pkg.T"}`. The committed docs/swagger.yaml contains 1299 such placeholders, covering dsl.Script (the platform's core payload), storage.User, storage.ExecutionPlan, storage.CapacityReservation, storage.RunArchiveRecord, recorder.Session, engine.ReplayReport and ~30 more - all of which are ordinary json-tagged structs whose shape is fully knowable.

**Failure scenario:** GET /api/v1/auth/users/{id} and POST /api/v1/auth/users/{id}/revoke-sessions return the full storage.User (handlers_auth.go:952 via visibleUserForRequest, which clones the struct verbatim at :1757). storage.User carries SessionEpoch `json:"session_epoch,omitempty"` (pkg/storage/storage.go:325), which becomes non-zero the moment an admin revokes a session, so the field is on the wire. But the generated contract for that operation is the opaque `Go type: storage.User` object, so the dashboard cannot use it and hand-writes DashboardUser (dashboard/src/types/auth.ts:184-195) - which has no session_epoch field; `grep -rn session_epoch dashboard/src` returns nothing. A dashboard feature that needs to show or act on the session epoch has no typed path to it, and nothing in CI will ever report the omission. This is the same mechanism behind the already-confirmed auth.ts trusted_proxy_cidrs drift.

**Suggested fix:** Give inferRouteContracts a bounded set of additional packages to parse (pkg/storage, pkg/dsl, pkg/engine, pkg/recorder) and resolve pkg.Type through their type definitions with the existing depth guard, or register named component schemas for the highest-traffic ones (storage.User, storage.ExecutionPlan, dsl.Script) the way SharedDataPool already is.

#### 154. Fleet-pool restriction (assignment.pool_id) is silently stripped by the dashboard's scena...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/scenarioPayloadUtils.ts:215` · **Area:** CC3-B · **Category:** silent-data-loss · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

pkg/api/runner.go:1093-1099 defines `PoolID string \`json:"pool_id,omitempty"\`` on the TEST-level GeneratorAssignmentSettings; it is live and enforced - runner_assignment.go:12-15 resolves it to the pool's member targets at create, launch_preflight.go:432 and capacity.go:88 read it, and distributed_execution_backend.go:529-532 applies lenient pool-scoped placement. The handwritten dashboard/src/types/testConfiguration.ts:23-31 GeneratorAssignmentSettings omits pool_id, and both payload builders that produce the root assignment rebuild it from an explicit whitelist that has no pool_id branch: scenarioPayloadUtils.ts:215-234 buildRootAssignmentPayload returns a fresh object in all four branches, and it is the only root-assignment producer (called from buildScenarioUpsertPayload at :372 and buildCreateTestPayload at :424). scenarioDraftUtils.ts:26-35 cloneGeneratorAssignment does the same on the way in, so the value is already gone before the payload stage. `pool_id` appears nowhere in dashboard/src outside the unrelated data-pool and capacity-reservation contexts.

Keep it out of buildGroupAssignmentPayload, which is correct today - the backend rejects a group-level pool_id per normalizeGroupGeneratorAssignmentSettings.

#### 161. The generated action reference states that jms/kafka validators reject engine actions; bo...
**Where:** `pkg/dsl/catalog.go:199` · **Area:** CC3-C · **Category:** generated-doc-vs-code · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

docs/DSL_ACTION_REFERENCE.md:27 (emitted verbatim by pkg/dsl/schemagen/schemagen.go:252) says engine actions are 'Valid in every script except jms-* and kafka, whose validators accept only their own action types.' That is false. validateActionForProtocolAtPath short-circuits on `isEngineActionType` at pkg/dsl/validate.go:432 and returns before reaching the jms/kafka/eventhubs membership check at validate.go:439-444, and the messaging validators independently opt engine actions out of their own sweeps: pkg/dsl/catalog_kafka_validation.go:183-185 and pkg/dsl/catalog_jms_validation.go:225-227 both `return nil` for isEngineActionType. The engine then executes them protocol-independently (pkg/engine/vuser.go:712 -> handleEngineAction). Yet pkg/dsl/catalog.go:199 sets `allowEngine := family != "jms" && family != "kafka"`, so ActionSpecsForProtocol — and therefore GET /api/v1/dsl/actions?protocol=kafka (pkg/api/handlers_dsl_catalog.go:36) — omits control_if, control_loop, control_break, control_continue, rendezvous, error_message and every source_* action for those two families. Event Hubs, which took the opposite (correct) route, spells the intent out at pkg/dsl/catalog_eventhubs_validation.go:69 ('Common lifecycle validation handles engine actions').

**Failure scenario:** An author writes a Kafka soak scenario that needs a control_loop around kafka_produce plus a rendezvous before the burst. In the dashboard editor the action-type list is populated from GET /api/v1/dsl/actions?protocol=kafka, which returns only the 8 kafka_* types — control_loop and rendezvous are simply absent, so the loop cannot be inserted from the UI. If the author checks the published DSL reference for a workaround, line 27 tells them those actions are invalid in kafka scripts. Both statements are wrong: the validator accepts the script and the engine runs the loop. The result is a capability that exists, is tested internally, and is undiscoverable to every consumer of the catalog and the docs.

**Suggested fix:** Decide the intended contract once. If engine actions are valid in jms/kafka (as the validators and engine already behave), delete the allowEngine special case at catalog.go:199, fix the sentence at schemagen.go:252, regenerate, and flip the two assertions in catalog_test.go:269/277. If they are meant to be rejected, add the rejection to validate.go before the engine short-circuit and to the two messaging validators.

Emitted verbatim by `pkg/dsl/schemagen/schemagen.go:252`. `go test ./pkg/dsl/schemagen -run TestGeneratedReferenceIsFresh -count=1` (real tree) → `ok` — fresh, so the sentence is code-authored, not stale.

**Source side.** `pkg/dsl/validate.go:432` short-circuits `isEngineActionType` before the jms/kafka/eventhubs membership branch at `:439-444`; `pkg/dsl/catalog_kafka_validation.go:183-185` and `catalog_jms_validation.go:225-227` both `return nil` for engine types; `catalog_eventhubs_validation.go:69` says the opposite explicitly. Same run: `ActionSpecsForProtocol("kafka")` = 8 kafka_* only, `("jms-solace")` = 14 jms_* only, `("eventhubs")` includes control_*/rendezvous/source_*. **Where:** `pkg/convert/enterprisearchive/converter_test.go:831` · **Area:** CC4-C · **Category:** false-confidence-test · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The test is named and positioned as the verification that web_set_user maps to HTTP basic auth, and it asserts auth.Type/Username/Password precisely (converter_test.go:858-862). It is green - I ran it: `go test ./pkg/convert/enterprisearchive -run TestConvertMapsWebSetUserToHTTPAuth -count=1` -> ok, 0.652s. It nevertheless cannot detect the confirmed High at pkg/convert/enterprisearchive/converter.go:836, because it calls `Convert([]*ParsedAction{parsed}, ConvertOptions{})` (converter_test.go:852) with an empty options struct. The destructive statement is guarded: converter.go:835 `if opts.HTTPConfig != nil {` / :836 `result.Script.Config.HTTP = *opts.HTTPConfig` - a wholesale struct replacement that discards the Auth field the web_set_user mapping just wrote. With HTTPConfig nil the branch is skipped, so the assertion can never fail. The real import path always populates it: zip.go:159-161 does `callerHTTPConfig := opts.HTTPConfig != nil` / `if opts.HTTPConfig == nil { opts.HTTPConfig = runtimeCfg.ToHTTPConfig() }`, and ToHTTPConfig (runtime_config.go:879) returns a non-nil *dsl.HTTPConfig. So every real archive that carries a runtime config takes the branch the test avoids. This is category (b) false confidence: a specific reviewed claim ('web_set_user basic auth is imported') is guarded by a test that is structurally incapable of falsifying it. The immediately following line, converter.go:839 mergeScriptConfig, carries a second confirmed High (config_merge.go:60, web_global_verification content checks wiped) that the same empty-options fixture hides.

**Failure scenario:** A user imports a real enterprise/LoadRunner archive containing web_set_user("perfuser","perfpass","secure.example.com:443") plus any runtime configuration file - the normal shape of an exported archive. ConvertZip sets opts.HTTPConfig from runtimeCfg.ToHTTPConfig(), converter.go:836 overwrites Config.HTTP wholesale, and the basic-auth credentials are silently dropped from the imported script with no diagnostic. Every replayed request then runs unauthenticated and the load test measures 401 handling instead of the application. Because TestConvertMapsWebSetUserToHTTPAuth is green and named for exactly this behaviour, a maintainer auditing 'is web_set_user import covered?' gets a false yes, and a fix to converter.go:836 would land with no test change and no regression signal either way.

**Suggested fix:** Add a table dimension to the existing test rather than a new one: run the same web_set_user fixture twice, once with ConvertOptions{} and once with ConvertOptions{HTTPConfig: &dsl.HTTPConfig{Version: "1.1"}}, asserting auth survives in both. That second case fails today and is the regression guard for the converter.go:836 fix (which should merge rather than replace, preserving Auth).

Doc quoted verbatim, DEVELOPMENT.md:465-470, under "## Useful Commands": "# Profile CPU/memory during test" / `go run ./cmd/controller -cpuprofile=cpu.prof -memprofile=mem.prof` / "# Analyze profile" / `go tool pprof cpu.prof`. Present tense, no caveat, no "planned".

Args after the package path go to the program, which ignores them entirely, so no profile file is written and nothing errors at the point of the mistake — the only signal is the later `go tool pprof cpu.prof` failing on a missing file. The real mechanism is env-gated: cmd/controller/main.go:66 `debugserver.StartPprofFromEnv(os.Getenv)`, keyed on APEXLOAD_PPROF_ADDR (pkg/debugserver/pprof.go:31), which DEVELOPMENT.md never mentions.

</details>

#### 176. Load-profile phase shading is misdrawn: numeric ReferenceArea bounds do not exist as cate...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/NewTestPage.tsx:3134` · **Area:** CC6-A · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

Both load-profile previews shade phases with <ReferenceArea x1={someSeconds} x2={otherSeconds}> while their <XAxis dataKey="second"> has no `type` prop, so it is a CATEGORY axis (recharts@3.9.2 es6/state/selectors/axisSelectors.js:76 implicitXAxis.type = 'category'; types/cartesian/XAxis.d.ts documents @defaultValue category). The data is sampled at `second = 0, step, 2*step, ...` with `step = Math.max(1, Math.floor(totalSeconds / 30))` (newTestRunModel.ts:452-456, testExecutionScenarioModel.ts:110-114), so the phase boundaries - preBaselineSeconds, preBaselineSeconds + steadySeconds, totalSeconds - postBaselineSeconds - are almost never one of the ~30 sampled categories. For an unknown band input, es6/util/scale/RechartsScale.js:44-47 `map` returns undefined; ReferenceArea.getRect coerces that to null (es6/cartesian/ReferenceArea.js:38-50) and es6/util/CartesianUtils.js rectWithPoints computes Math.min(null, x2) = 0 and Math.abs(x2 - null) = x2. The default ifOverflow='discard' does not rescue this because CartesianScaleHelperImpl.isInRange treats a null coordinate as in-range (es6/util/scale/CartesianScaleHelper.js:51-57), so the degenerate rectangle is rendered rather than discarded.

**Failure scenario:** A 10-minute run with resource_baseline enabled and a 60s ramp-down: preBaselineSeconds=300, steadySeconds=600, postBaselineSeconds=300, totalSeconds=1260, step=floor(1260/30)=42, so the sampled seconds are 0,42,84,...,1218,1260. (a) The blue steady-state band x1=300 x2=900 maps to null/null, so the rect is {x:0,width:0} and the band the caption promises simply is not drawn. (b) The amber start-delay band x1=0 x2=300 maps to (plotLeftPx, null) and is drawn from SVG x=0 to plotLeft - a stray amber sliver over the Y-axis labels instead of over the first 300 seconds. (c) The amber post-baseline band x1=960 x2=1260 maps to (null, plotRightPx) and is therefore drawn from SVG x=0 all the way to the right edge, washing the ENTIRE chart amber at 0.05 opacity. TestExecutionScenarioPreview even carries a caption asserting the opposite: 'The blue span marks steady-state load, and the amber spans mark the zero-load start delay and optional resource baseline windows.' An operator sizing a run reads the wrong phase boundaries off the preview.

**Suggested fix:** Either (a) make the X axis numeric - <XAxis dataKey="second" type="number" domain={[0, totalSeconds]}> - so ReferenceArea bounds are interpolated rather than looked up (this is the smaller change and also fixes tick spacing for irregular final samples), or (b) snap each ReferenceArea bound to the nearest sampled `second` in the points array before passing it. TestExecutionLiveControls.tsx:303 is already correct by construction because its model emits a point at exactly vuserTransitionSeconds - worth a comment there so it is not 'fixed' into the same trap.

#### 177. cpu_process_pct is gopsutil's since-process-start lifetime average, not current CPU, and ...
**Where:** `pkg/engine/sys_metrics.go:107` · **Area:** CC6-C · **Category:** library-semantics · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

ResourceCollector.collect publishes `res.CPUProcessPct = rc.proc.CPUPercent()` every sampling interval as if it were an instantaneous gauge. In the installed gopsutil v3.24.5, Process.CPUPercentWithContext (process/process.go:350-368) is `100 * cput.Total() / time.Since(created).Seconds()` — cumulative CPU seconds divided by the process's entire wall-clock lifetime. It is an average since process start, it never decreases when the process goes idle, and because it is not divided by NumCPU it is a percentage of ONE core (a fully busy 8-core generator reports ~800). Every other rate in this same file is computed correctly as a delta over dt — cpu.Times deltas at :95-104, net counters at :140-150, cgroup CPU at :198-200 — so this one call is the outlier, and it is the only place in the collector where a library's cumulative semantics were not unwound.

**Failure scenario:** A generator pod runs a 10-minute ramp then holds steady for an hour pegged at ~2 cores. Ten minutes into steady state the true instantaneous usage is ~200% of a core, but cpu_process_pct reports the lifetime mean, which is still climbing through the ramp's low values and lags reality for the whole run; after the test ends and the pod idles awaiting the next run, the value stays high indefinitely and poisons the NEXT test's readings because the collector's process (and therefore createTime) is unchanged. dashboard/src/components/generatorImpact.ts:125 uses `(resources?.cpu_process_pct ?? 0) >= 95` as one of the two triggers for the 'CPU saturation' generator-impact verdict, so: on a long-running multi-core pod the threshold trips at a mere ~1 core of long-run average and flags healthy generators as saturated; on a pod restarted for the run it stays under 95 through the early minutes even while genuinely pegged, and fails to flag a generator that is invalidating its own results. The same number is also written into pkg/perfevidence/run.go:399 as ProcessCPUPercent and emitted at :792 as the `process_cpu` percent metric in the evidence bundle, so the wrong figure is what an operator reads back when auditing whether a run was generator-bound. Neither a type-checker nor a unit test can see this — the value is well-formed, plausible, and only wrong relative to what it claims to measure.

**Suggested fix:** Compute the process rate the same way the rest of the collector does: store the previous `rc.proc.Times()` (gopsutil's cumulative TimesStat) alongside lastTime, and set CPUProcessPct = (cur.Total() - prev.Total()) / dt * 100. Decide explicitly whether the published number is per-core or per-machine and say so in the field name or docs — if the >=95 dashboard threshold is meant as 'saturated', divide by runtime.NumCPU() (or by ContainerCPULimitCores when the cgroup limit is known, which the collector already reads at :196) so the threshold means what it reads as. Leave the first sample at 0 like the other rate fields do via rc.initialized.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **R20 — CONFIRMED (medium)**

Verified against the installed package, not memory. gopsutil v3.24.5
`process/process.go:350-368`: `CPUPercentWithContext` = `100 * cput.Total() /
time.Since(created).Seconds()` — cumulative CPU seconds over the whole OS-process
lifetime, with no NumCPU division (two busy cores reads ~200).
`pkg/engine/sys_metrics.go:106-109` publishes that verbatim as `CPUProcessPct`,
while every sibling rate in the same file deltas against a stored sample (net
:146-151, disk :184-187, cgroup CPU :198-201, which also normalises by
CPULimitCores). gopsutil even ships the delta-based `Percent(0)` at :241-278.
Consumers treat it as an instantaneous 0-100 gauge: `generatorImpact.ts:125` ORs
it with `container_cpu_usage_pct` at `>=95`; `root_cause_analysis.go:116-122`
flags `>=80/90`; `perfevidence/run.go:399,792` emits `process_cpu` percent.

On returning to it, replayScopeMatches (:1011-1014) is still true (replayReviewGeneration/-ScriptIndex/-ProjectId were written at :2445-2447 and nothing reset them), so replayValidationLoading resolves to true -> browserReplayStarting/browserReplayInProgress true (:1197,:1202) -> the polling effect early-returns on `|| replayValidationLoading` at :1703 so nothing will ever refresh it, the Start button is disabled at :3629, and primarySaveDisabled (:1205-1213) keeps Save disabled with the label 'Draft Browser Replay In Progress'. A cannot be saved to the library at all without re-running the whole import.

#### 181. Error drill-down selection is keyed on array index, so it jumps to the top pattern whenev...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:892` · **Area:** GAPFE-2 · **Category:** state-management · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

buildLiveErrorPatterns mints ids as `live-${index}-${pattern.signature}` (:892) - the array index is part of the identity. The backend re-sorts the pattern list by Count descending (ties by FirstSeen) on every metrics tick: pkg/api/live_error_evidence.go:250-255, rebuilt into live.ErrorPatterns each interval at pkg/api/metrics.go:474. As soon as the ordering changes, the stored state.selectedErrorId no longer matches any row, and the resolution at :1182 (`errorPatterns.find(error => error.id === state.selectedErrorId) || errorPatterns[0]`) silently falls back to the highest-count pattern. That fallback also re-keys the evidence effect, whose dep is selectedError?.signature (:1218), so a fresh getTestErrorEvidence request fires for the wrong signature and liveEvidenceBySignature is repopulated for it. Nothing repairs state.selectedErrorId, so the drill-down snaps back to the top pattern on every re-rank.

**Failure scenario:** A live run is producing three error signatures. The operator opens Error Details, clicks the third row ('Solace publish retry burst', currently 66 occurrences, id live-2-Solace...), and starts reading its captured request/response evidence. One metrics interval later Solace overtakes 'Cart lookup p99 spike' (118 -> Solace 121), so the backend emits it at index 1 and the frontend regenerates its id as live-1-Solace.... `find` misses live-2-Solace..., the selection silently falls back to errorPatterns[0] ('HTTP 401 token refresh race'), the evidence table under the operator's cursor swaps to a different error's snapshots, and a new evidence request fires for the wrong signature. Re-clicking the row works until the next re-rank, so triage of anything other than the top-ranked error is effectively impossible while counts are still moving.

**Suggested fix:** Key patterns by signature alone (e.g. `id: pattern.signature || \`pattern-${index}\``), which is already unique per run because the backend maps patterns by signature (pkg/api/live_error_evidence.go:236 takes a map keyed by signature). Optionally add a fallback that re-resolves state.selectedErrorId by signature before falling back to index 0, and only reset selectedEvidenceId when the resolved signature actually changes.

#### 182. Auto-discovery asks for an unfiltered test list, so a live run outside the 200 newest is ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:1090` · **Area:** GAPFE-2 · **Category:** api-contract · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The discovery loop calls `api.listTests({ application_id: applicationId, project_id: projectId })` (:1090) with no active_only, no summary and no limit, then filters client-side with isCommandCenterDiscoverableStatus (:1092). The backend defaults limit to 200 (pkg/api/handlers.go:137 defaultTestListLimit) and - critically - only enables active-first ordering when the caller passes an explicit limit (`limitExplicit` at :99 feeding prioritizeActive at :124, consumed by sortTestList's activeFirst at pkg/api/handlers.go:182-198). With prioritizeActive false the page is ordered purely by CreatedAt descending, so the 200 most recently CREATED runs are returned regardless of whether any of them is live. api.listTests already accepts active_only and limit (dashboard/src/hooks/api/useTestApi.ts:326-339) and the backend already implements active_only (pkg/api/handlers.go:144, isActiveTestListStatus at :173-180); neither is used. The same request repeats on a 5s interval (:1113) for as long as the empty state is open.

**Failure scenario:** A busy CI project creates runs continuously. An 8-hour soak test is RUNNING, but 200+ other tests have been created in the project since it started. An operator opens Command Center from the sidebar (no run on the route): listTests returns the 200 newest by created_at, the soak is not among them, isCommandCenterDiscoverableStatus filters to zero, and the view sits on 'No active run selected' forever while the run is plainly live on the Dashboard. Meanwhile the same 200-row payload is re-downloaded every 5 seconds by every open Command Center tab. The workaround is to reach the run through a run chip so testId comes from the route.

**Suggested fix:** Pass `{ application_id, project_id, active_only: true, summary: true, limit: 50 }`. active_only makes the backend filter to live/pending statuses (a superset of isCommandCenterDiscoverableStatus, so keep the client-side filter as a refinement), and passing an explicit limit also flips prioritizeActive on so active runs sort first.

loadingTest spreads MOCK_TEST and overrides only id, ref_key, name, status, groups, total_vusers and live_metrics (:1129-1138). buildLoadModelProfile fabricates the 'planned' curve from a fixed shape - 0% at start, 28% of target at 12% elapsed, 58% at 24%, at-target from 40% to 78%, 72% at 90%, 0% at 100% (:3525-3536) - parameterised only by the summed current target. #### 186. Run-calendar cells are bucketed by the viewer's local day but the events inside them are ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/MonitoringPage.tsx:2347` · **Area:** GAPFE-3 · **Category:** correctness · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

buildRunCalendarModel assigns each event to a cell using local-midnight boundaries (dayStart/dayEnd from startOfLocalDay at :2340-2341, compared as absolute ms in runCalendarEventOverlapsDay :2377-2382), while RunCalendarEventButton renders the chip time with formatCalendarTime(event.start_at, event.timezone) (:2303), which formats in the event's declared IANA zone via calendarZoneOptions (:2431-2441). The detail panel's 'When' row goes further and renders the month and day in the event's zone too (formatCalendarDateTime, :2231/:2443-2447). Because pkg/api/run_calendar.go:815 and :958 stamp Timezone from the schedule (UTC is the first entry in COMMON_TIMEZONES, newTestScheduleFormat.ts:185-186, so it is the common default), a projected cron chip routinely shows a wall-clock time that belongs to a different calendar date than the cell it sits in.

**Failure scenario:** An operator in America/Los_Angeles opens Monitoring -> Schedules with a nightly cron schedule configured as '0 2 * * *' in UTC. The 2026-08-05T02:00Z occurrence is 2026-08-04 19:00 PDT, so buildRunCalendarModel drops it into the August 4 cell. The chip inside that cell reads '2:00 AM UTC'. The operator reads the grid as 'the nightly run is on Aug 4 at 2 AM' — a date/time pair that corresponds to no actual instant (the run is either Aug 4 7 PM local or Aug 5 2 AM UTC). Clicking the chip makes the contradiction explicit and unresolvable from the UI: the detail panel's 'When' row says 'Aug 5, 2:00 AM UTC' while the chip is still highlighted inside the cell whose header number is 4.

**Suggested fix:** Pick one zone for the whole grid. Either (a) bucket in the event's zone — derive the day key with Intl.DateTimeFormat(tz, {year,month,day}).formatToParts(start) instead of startOfLocalDay, or (b) keep local bucketing and render chip times with browser-local formatting, moving the event-zone rendering into the detail panel only, where the date is shown alongside it. Option (b) is the smaller change and keeps the grid internally consistent; add the zone as a secondary annotation (e.g. '7:00 PM (2:00 AM UTC)') so the schedule's declared zone is not lost.

2. Labelling is event-zone: the chip renders `formatCalendarTime(event.start_at, event.timezone)` (:2303), and `calendarZoneOptions` returns `{timeZone: tz, timeZoneName:'short'}` for any valid IANA name (:2431-2441). The detail "When" row renders month+day in that same zone (`formatCalendarDateTime` :2231, :2443-2447), so the panel can print a different calendar date than the cell the chip sits in.

Schedule drafts default to `'UTC'` (NewTestPage.tsx:257, ExecutionPlanSchedulesModal.tsx:45, both persisted as `timezone.trim() || 'UTC'`), so a non-UTC viewer is the common case.
4. Wiring: `RunCalendarPanel` gets `model={calendarModel}` and the events (MonitoringPage.tsx:1443-1462); MonitoringPage is rendered unconditionally for the monitoring/fleet/schedules views (App.tsx:2112-2126). No flag.

#### 188. The schedulable day cell's keyboard handler swallows Enter/Space on the run chips nested ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/MonitoringPage.tsx:2160` · **Area:** GAPFE-3 · **Category:** accessibility-interaction · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

Each month/week day cell is turned into a role='button' with tabIndex=0 via interactiveElementProps (:2160) while still containing real <button> event chips (:2177-2179). interactiveElementProps' onKeyDown calls event.preventDefault() for Enter and Space before invoking the activation callback (interactiveElementProps.ts:12-17), and it fires during the bubble phase of the keydown that originated on the focused chip. Cancelling that keydown cancels the button's default activation behaviour, so no click event is dispatched; the day handler then bails out anyway because its own guard sees the chip in event.target.closest('button') (:2151). Net effect: the keypress activates neither the chip nor the cell. onScheduleForDate is always supplied in the app (App.tsx:2122), so the wrapper is always present.

**Failure scenario:** A keyboard-only operator tabs through the Run Calendar month grid, lands on a run chip, and presses Enter (or Space) to open its detail panel. The keydown bubbles to the day cell, interactiveElementProps calls preventDefault, and the browser therefore never synthesises the chip's click — while the cell's own handler returns early because the target is a button. Nothing happens, for any chip, on any keypress. The only way to open a run's details in month or week view is a mouse click; the same operator can still schedule a run by activating an empty part of the cell, so the surface looks responsive while the primary action is dead.

**Suggested fix:** Guard before preventing the default: in the day cell's activation callback, return early on nested interactive targets *before* interactiveElementProps swallows the key — e.g. pass a handler that checks event.target and, for keyboard events, do not call preventDefault when the target is not the cell itself. Simplest local fix: replace the spread with an explicit onKeyDown that ignores events whose target !== currentTarget.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **DG21 (GAPFE-3) — verifier A**

Every hop reproduced in the snapshot.

1. Wiring: `dashboard/src/App.tsx:2122` passes `onScheduleForDate={navigateToScheduleForDate}` to `MonitoringPage` (rendered for view.page monitoring/fleet/schedules), which forwards it to `RunCalendarPanel` at `MonitoringPage.tsx:1461`. So `scheduleForThisDay` (`:2147-2155`) is always defined in the real app.
2. Cell: `MonitoringPage.tsx:2160` spreads `interactiveElementProps(...)` onto the day `<div>`, giving it `role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`, `onClick`, `onKeyDown`.
3. Nested chips: `:2178` renders `RunCalendarEventButton`, defined at `:2300-2302` as a real `<button type="button" onClick={() => onSelect(event)}>` with **no** `onKeyDown` and no `stopPropagation`.
4. Handler: `interactiveElementProps.ts:12-17` — on Enter/Space it calls `event.preventDefault()` unconditionally, then `onActivate`. React 18 delegates at the root container, so this bubble-phase handler runs while the native keydown is still dispatching; the browser's activation behaviour (click synthesis) is a post-dispatch default action, so the click is cancelled for Enter, and for Space the button never enters the active state so keyup fires no click.
5. Cell's own callback then returns early at `:2151` because `event.target.closest('button')` is the chip.

Refutation attempts failed: no memo/effect guard, no parent gating, no `stopPropagation`, no keyboard handler on the chip. `MonitoringPage.test.tsx:1526` exercises the chip via **click** only (clicks still work: the chip's onClick fires, and the bubbled click hits the same `closest('button')` guard), so no test pins the opposite. jsdom does not implement Enter→click activation, so a unit test could not have caught this. Day (agenda) view chips at `:2135` sit outside the interactive cell and are unaffected — a workaround exists, keeping this medium rather than high.

Verdict: confirmed, medium.

</details>

calendarRange is a useMemo over [calendarView, calendarAnchor] (:510) and both calendarRange.from and calendarRange.to are in refreshAll's dep list (:666), so pressing Previous/Next/Today or switching Month/Week/Day changes refreshAll's identity and the mount effect at :682 re-fires it. refreshAll awaits a single Promise.all over 13 endpoints (:617-637) and applies every setState only after all of them settle (:638-652) — including setRunCalendar. Card `run-calendar` is reachable in prod (`App.tsx:2115`, category `schedules` :43/:1524).

#### 191. Command Center live-run discovery omits `limit`, which both caps it at 200 rows and disab...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:1090` · **Area:** GAPFE-4 · **Category:** silent-truncation · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

The auto-discovery poll calls `api.listTests({ application_id: applicationId, project_id: projectId })` (CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:1090) with neither `limit` nor `active_only`, then filters client-side for discoverable statuses (CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:1092, predicate at :146-148). useTestApi.listTests simply omits any absent key from the query string (useTestApi.ts:326-341), so the server applies defaultTestListLimit=200 (pkg/api/handlers.go:137, 142) *and* -- because `limitExplicit` is false -- passes `prioritizeActive: false` into the page query (pkg/api/handlers.go:99, 121), so sortTestList does not hoist active runs to the front (pkg/api/handlers.go:182-196). The result is that this surface, the one whose entire purpose is finding the live run, is the only test-list caller that gets pure created-at-desc ordering with no active-first bias, and it also ignores the returned `total`.

**Failure scenario:** A 24-hour soak test is started in an application at 09:00 Monday. Over the next day, CI kicks off 210 short smoke runs in the same application. On Tuesday morning the operator opens Command Center without a testId (from the nav, not from a run row). The discovery poll fetches the 200 newest runs by created_at with no active-first hoist; the soak run is #211 and is excluded. `liveRuns` is empty, so runDiscoveryState.runs is [] and no auto-selection happens -- Command Center reports it has no run to attach to while a test is actively running, and the 5-second poll repeats the same wrong answer indefinitely.

**Suggested fix:** Pass `{ application_id, project_id, active_only: true, summary: true, limit: 200 }`. `active_only` filters server-side to exactly the statuses discovery cares about, and supplying `limit` flips limitExplicit so the server's prioritizeActive path also engages.

<details><summary>Verification evidence</summary>

**confirmed @ medium — verifier A:** **DG27 (slot A) — Command Center discovery omits `limit`**

Chain verified hop-by-hop at HEAD snapshot.

1. Code exists: `dashboard/src/components/CommandCenterPrototype.tsx:1090` — `await api.listTests({ application_id: applicationId, project_id: projectId })`, no `limit`, no `active_only`, no `summary`. Result filtered client-side at :1092 via `isCommandCenterDiscoverableStatus` (:146-148 → LIVE ∪ PENDING ∪ SHAKEOUT/SHAKEOUT_REVIEW/PAUSED, testStatusUtils.ts:11-12). `res.total` is never read.
2. Wrapper drops absent keys: `useTestApi.ts:325-343` builds queryParams from the object and `buildQuery` omits undefined, so no `limit` reaches the server.
3. Server: `pkg/api/handlers.go:99` `limitExplicit := query.Get("limit") != ""` → false; passed as `prioritizeActive` (:121). `parseTestListOptions` defaults `limit = defaultTestListLimit = 200` (:137,142). `listTestSummaryPage` (pkg/api/tests.go:545-608) sorts via `sortTestList(matches, false)` → pure CreatedAt-desc, no active hoist (handlers.go:182-196), then slices `matches[start:end]` at 200 and returns `total`.
4. Production wiring: `App.tsx:2004-2023` renders `<CommandCenterPrototype testId={view.testId} applicationId={...} projectId={...} />` with no `prototypeMode` (defaults false, :939). Navigating to Command Center from the nav leaves `view.testId` undefined, so the effect at :1070-1118 runs, polls every 5s, and drives `CommandCenterEmptyState` (:1619-1624, :1754-1806) which renders "No active run selected".
5. No refuting guard: the scope/generation guards present (:1071, :1091) address races, not truncation; the existing tests (CommandCenterPrototype.test.tsx:177-330) stub `/tests` regardless of query params and pin nothing about limit/ordering.

Caveat: the suggested fix's `active_only: true` would drop `SCHEDULED` (server's isActiveTestListStatus, handlers.go:169-176, excludes it while the client predicate includes it); an explicit `limit` alone is the safe part of the fix.

Severity: medium. Requires >200 runs newer than the live run inside the same application/project scope; consequence is a failed attach on a convenience surface (topbar active-run indicator and Results still reach the run), not data loss or wrong destructive targeting.

#### 192. Dashboard release KPI tiles are computed from a server-truncated 500-run window and under...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/DashboardPage.tsx:609` · **Area:** GAPFE-4 · **Category:** silent-truncation · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** regression

DashboardPage requests an application-scoped run page with `limit: 500` (DashboardPage.tsx:609) and destructures only `tests/error/loading/refreshing/updatedAt/refresh` from useSharedTestList (DashboardPage.tsx:611-618) -- it never reads `count` or `total`, both of which the store faithfully surfaces (useSharedTestList.ts:139-149) from the server response (pkg/api/handlers.go:115-124). It then narrows to the active release purely client-side (`releaseTests = resolvedTests.filter(t => t.release_id === activeRelease.id)`, DashboardPage.tsx:743-746) and derives releaseStats -- failed/aborted/archived counts and `totalTx`, a sum of archive.transaction_count -- from that narrowed slice (DashboardPage.tsx:1047-1054). Because the truncation happens on the *wider* application scope before the *narrower* release filter, the tiles under-report with no truncation indicator anywhere -- unlike ResultsPage, which computes `resultsTruncated = offset + count < total` and renders a banner (ResultsPage.tsx:373, 1482).

The user opens the Dashboard with release 1.2 active. #### 194. TimeslotsPanel.load has no project or request guard, so a slow previous-project response ...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/TimeslotsPanel.tsx:95` · **Area:** GAPFE-4 · **Category:** scope-race · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

TimeslotsPanel's loader is `useCallback(async () => { ... setTimeslots(res.timeslots || []) }, [api, projectId])` with no mountedRef, no cancellation flag, no request-generation counter and no projectId re-check after the await (TimeslotsPanel.tsx:95-111), and its driving effect is a bare `useEffect(() => { void load() }, [load])` (TimeslotsPanel.tsx:113-115). This is a direct consequence of the shared layer offering no cancellation primitive: `useCapacityApi.listTimeslots` takes only `params` and forwards nothing to `request()` (useCapacityApi.ts:22-26), even though apiClient's `request`/`apiFetch` do accept and merge an AbortSignal (apiClient.ts:414-416, 513-518). The two sibling panels on the same page hand-roll the guard the hook does not provide -- CorrelationRulesetPanel uses an `isCurrentRequest()` closure over project + request id (CorrelationRulesetPanel.tsx:83-92) and ObjectRepositoryPanel uses a mountedRef (ObjectRepositoryPanel.tsx:52-56) -- TimeslotsPanel does neither. The panel is not remounted on project change: App.tsx renders MonitoringPage without a project key, and MonitoringPage passes `<TimeslotsPanel projectId={activeProject?.id} .../>` as a prop element (MonitoringPage.tsx:1450), so only the prop changes.

**Failure scenario:** The user is on Monitoring -> Schedules -> Capacity Reservations with Project A selected, which has ~100 reservations (slow response). They switch the topbar project to Project B, which has 3. Request A is still in flight; the prop change re-runs the effect and fires request B, which returns first and renders B's 3 slots. A then resolves and unconditionally calls setTimeslots(A's 100 slots). The panel now lists Project A's reservations while the topbar and the surrounding calendar say Project B, and every row's Approve / Reject / Bind test / Delete button (TimeslotsPanel.tsx:281-300) targets a Project A reservation id -- so a user clicking Delete on what they believe is a stale Project B slot deletes a live Project A reservation. Nothing resets the list on projectId change, so the wrong data persists until the user manually re-triggers a load.

**Suggested fix:** Mirror CorrelationRulesetPanel: capture `const requested = projectId` and `const generation = ++requestRef.current` before the await, bail out of every setState when either has moved on, and clear `timeslots` in a layout effect keyed on projectId so the panel never shows the previous project's rows.

No client-side dedupe/coalescing.
2. Stability: `useCapacityApi` returns a `useMemo` over `[]`-dep `useCallback`s, so `api` is stable; `load` changes identity only on `projectId`, so the effect refires exactly on project switch — overlapping requests, not a render loop.

Wiring: `MonitoringPage.tsx:1450` passes `<TimeslotsPanel projectId={activeProject?.id} …/>` into `RunCalendarPanel`, rendered unconditionally at `MonitoringPage.tsx:2116-2122`; the card list keys on `card.id` (`:1675`) and `App.tsx:2115` renders MonitoringPage with no key. Because the limit is omitted the server returns at most the 200 newest tests in the project (pkg/api/handlers.go:137,142; pkg/api/tests.go:596-601), and the returned `total` is discarded. **Failure scenario:** A shared project holds 600 retained runs. An engineer expands the 'Runs' row for a login script that was last exercised four months and 400 runs ago. The list request returns only the 200 newest runs, none of which reference that script, so the expander renders an empty run list -- indistinguishable from a script that has never been run. Acting on that, the engineer deletes the script; the historical runs that reference it lose their script linkage. Because the empty result is memoized per script id, re-expanding the row does not correct it even after a new run using that script completes.

**Suggested fix:** Add a `scenario_id`-or-script-scoped server filter, or at minimum pass `{ project_id, summary: true, limit: 2000 }` and compare `offset + count` against `total` to render an explicit 'showing the most recent N runs' note instead of an empty state.

Server-side each of these defaults to 100 rows (handlers_object_repository.go:22,82; handlers_correlation_rulesets.go:23,233; handlers_timeslots.go:26,174) and -- unlike /tests -- none of the three responses carries a `total` field (handlers_object_repository.go:96; handlers_correlation_rulesets.go:257-266; handlers_timeslots.go:190-195), so the frontend cannot even detect that it received a page. None of the five surfaces renders a pager or a 'more results' affordance.

**Failure scenario:** A mature project accumulates 140 correlation rulesets (one per correlated endpoint family). The panel lists 100 and stops; there is no pager, no count, and no 'showing 100 of 140' text, so the ruleset simply appears not to exist and the user creates a duplicate. **Suggested fix:** Add `total` to the three list responses server-side, then either implement paging in the three panels or, as an interim, have the hooks default to `limit: <server max>` and have consumers render a 'showing N of M' notice when count < total. ScriptEditor's autocomplete should loop offsets until exhausted since it aggregates rather than displays rows.

#### 197. Changing a parameter's Data Source silently moves the Parameter Data panel onto a differe...
**Where:** `dashboard/src/components/ScriptEditorParameterFeatures.tsx:190` · **Area:** GAPFE-5 · **Category:** state-management · **Verification:** 1 adversarial verifier confirmed · **Prior:** new

ParameterDataDialog's first effect (:190-200) re-derives the selection from `openDataEditor`: it takes the name of data_sources[openDataEditor], finds the first parameter still mapped to that source (findFirstParameterIndexByDataSource, scriptEditorImportModel.ts:629-639), and if the currently selected parameter's data_source no longer matches that name it calls onSelectParameter(thatIndex). openDataEditor is only ever recomputed by selectParameterData (ScriptEditor.tsx:1665-1674) when a parameter is *selected*; nothing updates it when the selected parameter's data_source is edited in place through the Data Source select at :656. So the moment the operator repoints a parameter to another source, the effect classifies the selected parameter as a mismatch and hands the panel to a sibling parameter that still uses the old source. Every control in the panel writes through selectedParameterIdx (:265-267), so subsequent edits target the sibling.

**Failure scenario:** An LR-imported script has users.dat with two parameters mapped to it, `username` (index 0) and `password` (index 1). In the Parameter Data tab select `password`; openDataEditor is set to the users.dat index. Realising password should come from a different file, change its Data Source select from users.dat to accounts.csv. On the resulting render the effect at :190 sees data_sources[openDataEditor].name === 'users.dat', finds the first parameter still on users.dat (`username`, index 0), sees the selected parameter's data_source is now 'accounts.csv', and calls onSelectParameter(0). The header silently flips to 'Parameter: username'. The operator, still mid-task, picks a Column from the dropdown — that write goes to `username` (:265-267, :671), overwriting username's column mapping with a column name from accounts.csv, while `password` is left with a data source and no column. Nothing warns; the only cue is the small header title changing. On save the script has one parameter pointing at a column that does not exist in its file and another with no column, which the engine resolves per on_exhaustion rather than failing loudly.

**Suggested fix:** Make the effect adopt the selected parameter rather than fight it: if the selected parameter is valid but its data_source changed, ask the parent to re-point openDataEditor at the new source (a new onFocusDataSource callback) instead of calling onSelectParameter. At minimum, skip the effect when selectedParameterIdx is non-null and points at an existing parameter.
